docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, December 2023
pages:
Ministry of   Home     Affairs-Major    Achievements,  significant
Development and important events for the month of December, 2023.

       Hon'ble Union Home Minister presided over the signing of a Memorandum
of Settlement (MoS) on 29.12.2023 between Government of India, Government of
Assam and representatives of United Liberation Front of Assam (ULFA). As per
agreement, ULFA has agreed to abjure the path of violence, surrender all arms/
ammunition, disband their armed organization and join the peaceful democratic
process as established by the law and uphold the integrity of the country. A Special
Development Package of Rs. 5,000 crore (Rs. 3,000 crore by Gol and Rs. 2,000
crore by Govt. of Assam) will be provided over five years for various
developmental initiatives/projects in the State of Assam.

2.     Meeting of High Level Committee was held under the chairmanship of
Hon'ble Union Home Minister on 12.12.2023 for approving central assistance to
the State of Gujarat Cyclone (Biparjoy) and Himachal Pradesh (Cloud Burst/ Flood
land slide) to the tune of Rs.971.97 Cr (Rs.633.73 Cr for Himachal Pradesh and
Rs.338.24 Cr for Gujarat).

3.      National Crisis Management Committee (NCMC) had met on 01.12.2023
and 03.12.2023, under chairmanship of Cabinet Secretary, to review preparedness
of state governments and Central Ministries/Departments for impending cyclone at
"Michaungå in Bay of Bengal. The State Governments of Tamil Nadu, Andhra
Pradesh, Odisha, and Puducherry were assured of assistance from the central
agencies.

4.    On 14.12.2023, Union Home Secretary held the meeting of the Sub-
Committee of National Executive Committee (SC-NEC) for considering the
proposals of Expansion and Modernization of Fire Services for the States of
Andhra Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Telangana and UP.

5.    On 18.12.2023, Union Home Secretary reviewed the LWE scenario and Ops
preparedness of the State of Chhattisgarh.

6.     On 07.12.2023, Special Secretary (Internal Security) held a review meeting
of the Committee to study the best practices in the world of transport security.
Further, on 15.12.2023, she held a meeting of the Task Force Committee on
fratricide & suicide in CAPF, ARS & NSG.

7.    A meeting was held on 15.12.2023 under AS (PM) with GeM authorities,
ITBP and Assam Rifles Officers to discuss the proposals of ITBP & Assam Rifles
for exemption from mandatory procurement of free dry/fresh ration items through
GeM portal for the year 2024-25. Further on 28.12.2023, AS, PM held a meeting to
review procurement of various items by CAPFs through KVIC under Phase -I and
Phase-II of procurement.
8.    A presentation on Special Session Cyber Security: Emerging Challenges was
held during the 3rd National Conference of Chief Secretaries on 27.12.2023.

9.    Muslim League Jammu Kashmir (Masarat Alam faction)'/MLJK- MA was
declared as an 'Unlawful Association' under Section 3(1) of the Unlawful
Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) 1967 vide notification dated 27.12.2023.


                                   ******

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, November 2023
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
and important events for the month of November, 2023.

The Hon’ble President of India interacted with 200 tribal youths at Rashtrapati
Bhawan, New Delhi on 05.11.2023, who participated in the 15th Tribal Youth
Exchange Programme (TYEP) organized by MHA.

2. On 27th November, 2023 High- Level Committee (HLC) under the
chairmanship of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, has approved
the following proposal

(i). Recovery and reconstruction (R&R) plan of Rs. 1658.17 crore for
Joshimath, under the Recovery & Reconstruction window of NDRF.

(ii). First urban flood mitigation project of Rs. 561.29 crore for ‘Integrated
Urban Flood Management activities for Chennai Basin Project’ under the
National Disaster Mitigation Fund (NDMF).

3, The Government of India and Government of Manipur signed a Peace
Agreement with United National Liberation Front (UNLF), a valley-based Manipuri
armed group, on 29.11.2023 at New Delhi. As per agreement, UNLF has agreed to
return to mainstream by abjuring violence and agreeing to honour the Constitution
of India and jaws of the land.

4, On 03.11.2023 Union Home Secretary has taken a meeting with Chief
Secretary, Govt. of Gujarat and Advisor to Administrator, UT of Dadra Nagar Haveli
& Daman and Diu to discuss the transfer of four villages from Gujarat to Dadra
Nagar Haveli & Daman and Diu.

5. Under the Chairmanship of Home Secretary meeting of Sub-Committee of
National Executive Committee (SC-NEC) was held 09th November, 2023 to
consider the report of the Central Teams on damage caused by Flash flood/landslides
in Himachal Pradesh and on 15th November, 2023 to consider the proposals of
Urban Flood Risk Management Programme (UFRMP) under NDMF in respect of
the cities of Bengaluru and Ahmedabad.

6. Meeting held under the Chairmanship of Union Home Secretary on
15.11.2023 to discuss ongoing/ proposed/ feasible projects to be implemented in
Assam over next ten years. The Chief Secretary of Assam and Senior Officers of
concerned Central Ministries/ Departments have attended the meeting.
tf A meeting under the Chairmanship of Home Secretary was held on
16.11.2023 to consider the proposal for Government of India contribution towards
Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) Multi-Partner Trust Fund
(MPTF): Infrastructure Resilient Accelerator Fund (IRAF).

8. A meeting under the chairmanship of Home Secretary was held on 17.11.2023
for funds allocation under National Disaster Mitigation Fund (NDMF) for various
mitigation projects.

9. Union Home Secretary taken a meeting on 21.11.2023 with the representative
of Government of Andhra Pradesh and the Ministries/Departments of Government
of India to review the progress of Educational Institution/Infrastructural Projects in
Andhra Pradesh, as enumerated in A.P. Reogranisation Act, 2014.

10. Virtual Call between Home Secretary and Acting Deputy Secretary,
Department of Homeland Security, USA was held on 15.11.2023 to discuss various
issues of mutual concern.

11. On 09.11.2023 a meeting between Home Secretary and British High
Commissioner H.E. Mr. Alex Ellis was held.

12. The Meitei Extremist Organisations, namely, PLA, RPF, UNLF, PREPAK,
KCP, KYKL, CorCom and ASUK of Manipur have been declared as ‘unlawful
associations’ for a further period of 5 years w.e.f. 13.11.2023 upto 12.11.2028 under
the provisions of Section 3 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 vide
MHA’s Notification No. SO4899(E) dated 13.11.2023.

13. Advisory was issued on 28.11.2023 to. Principal Secretaries/Secretaries to
Governors of States, Lt. Governors and Administrations of UTs regarding Yuva
Sangam programme of M/o Education under ‘Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat’ Theme.

14. Total value of all sanctions accorded to CAPFs during the month of
November, 2023 is Rs.13,58,85,486=00.

15. NOC have been issued for changing the name of following villages
“Panjokhara” as “Panjokhara Sahib” in Ambala district, Haryana, “Ketsapo” as
“Kutsapo” and “Kotisu” as “Kutisu” in Phek district, Nagaland, “Chuhadpur” as
“Chandpur” in Jind district, Haryana.

16. A series of half day workshop were held w.e.f. 23.11.2023 to 01.12.2023 on
Cyber Security and Management of Critical Information Infrastructure for senior
functionaries of Critical Ministries/Departments of Government of India.
17. During the month, meetings of Joint Monitoring Committee were held under
the chairmanship of Additional Secretary (NE), MHA at New Delhi to review the
progress of implementation of Peace Agreements/ Accords signed with various
groups of Assam (Karbi Accord, 2021, DNLA Accord, 2023, Bodo Accord, 2020,
Adivasi Accord, 2022) and Tripura (NLFT (SD) Agreement, 2019, Bru Accord,
2020).

18. A meeting was held on 24.11.2023, under AS(PM&CIS), with MeiTY, BIS,
NIA, Delhi Police and domestic manufacturers of CCTV equipment, with a view to
address issues being faced by the domestic manufacturers and enhancement of their
production capacity.

19. A meeting was taken by Joint Secretary (CS) on 29.11.2023 with the
representative of Govt. of Bihar and Jharkhand, Principal AGs of both the States and

representative of C&AG to discuss the apportionment of pension liabilities between
Bihar and Jharkhand.

20. The first negotiation meeting with Kenya to discuss the Mutual Legal
Assistance Treaty in Criminal Matters was held on 10.11.2023. Further, Mr. Mikhail
Vinogradov, Head of the General Department of International Legal Cooperation,
Prosecutor General's Office of the Russian Federation met Joint Secretary (CIC) and
Joint Secretary UIS-I1) of MHA on 29.11.2023 to finalize the Memorandum of
Cooperation (MoC) between the Prosecutor General's Office of Russia and the
Ministry of Home Affairs of India.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, March 2023
pages:
Ministry of Home _ Affairs-Major Achievements, significant
Development and important events for the month of March, 2023.

Hon’ble Prime Minister inaugurated the 3rd Session of
National Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction (NPDRR-2023) which
was organized on 10th -11th March, 2023 at Vigyan Bhawan, New
Delhi. On the sidelines an exhibition on Disaster Management was
also inaugurated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister.

2. A meeting of High Level Committee (HLC) held on 10.03.2023
under the chairmanship of Union Home Minister considered the
recommendations of SC NEC for additional financial assistance
from National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) in r/o damage
caused by flood/landslides during 2022 in Karnataka, Assam,

Nagaland, Meghalaya, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh and Andhra
Pradesh.

3. RRU concluded an MoU with the Government of Karnataka on
24.3.2023, in the presence of Hon'ble Home Minister, for
establishing a campus at Shivamoga in Karnataka. The State
Government will provide land and building. 9 courses, with 220

seats, will be conducted from academic year 2023-24 in this
campus.

4. On 02.03.2023, a two-day, National Conference on Traffic
Technologies was organized at CAPT Bhopal in which Hon'ble Union
Minister for Road Transport and Highways, Shri Nitin Gadkari
addressed the participants virtually as the chief guest.

S. Union Home Secretary chaired the 54th High Level

Empowered Committee meeting held on 15th March, 2023 at North
Block, New Delhi on border infrastructure.

6. On 01.03.2023, Union Home Secretary reviewed the status of
settlement of inter-state border issues with Chief Secretaries of
Assam and Arunachal Pradesh.

7. A delegation led Mr. Bo Mathiasen, Deputy Director, Division
for Operation, United Nations offices on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)
met Ms. Sivagami Sundari Nanda, Special Secretary (IS), MHA and
other senior officers on 29.03.2023 in New Delhi. Matters of mutual
concern were discussed.
8. NOCs have been issued for changing the name of following
villages “Mangarh” as “Kripalu Dham Mangarh” in Uttar Pradesh;
“Kanalkond” as “Kanarkond” in Maharashtra; “Ayroor Kara” as
“Ayroor Kathakali Gramam” in Kerala; and “Bhanangkond” as
“Vrindavan” in Maharashtra. NOC has been issued for changing the

name of “Raghunathpur railway station” as “Baba Brahmeshwar
Nath railway station” in Bihar.

9. RRU has concluded an MoU on 27.3.2023 with
the Government of Puducherry for establishing a campus in
Puducherry. The UT of Puducherry will provide land and building. A

total of 15 courses with 300 seats, will be conducted from academic
year 2023-24 in this campus.

10. Total Value of all Sanction accorded to CAPFs during the
month of March, 2023 is Rs. 1,39,07,21,722-00 for procurement of
various equipments, vehicles etc.

11. During the month, BPR&D and its outlying units conducted
31 training courses in which 1195 personnel participated. Further,
BPR&D conducted a National Level Coastal Security Conference on

"Emerging Challenges for Coastal Policing and the Way Forward" on
10.03.2023

12. Police Training School, Goa conducted an Investigators
Training course on Women's Safety from 28.02.2023 to 04.03.2023
in which 40 Police officers were trained. Further, a one-day online
Symposium on Women's Safety was conducted by SVSPA, West

Bengal in collaboration with BPR&D on 15.03.2023, in which 78
officials participated.

13. A "National Security Module" for the Officer Trainees of 73rd
Batch of IRS (Customs & Income Tax) was organized on 02.03.2023
at BPR&D HQ. Trainees were given inputs on Building Blocks of
National Security, Terror Financing, and Predictive Analysis for
National Security etc.
14. Funds to the tune of Rs. 1202.40 crore, as Central share,
was released to 8 States, under the State Disaster Response Fund
(SDRF); funds to the tune of Rs. 1022.11 crore was released to 3
States namely Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka and Nagaland from
National Disaster Response Fund(NDRF); and funds to the tune of
Rs. 2154.20 Crore, as Central share, was released under State
Disaster Mitigation Fund (SDMF) to 18 States.

15. On 12.3.2023 at Itanagar (Arunachal Pradesh), a total of 15
armed cadres of ENNG (Eastern Naga National Government)
including its President Tosa Mossang surrendered their arms and
joined the mainstream of society.

16. The Meetings of Joint Monitoring Committee (JMC) were held
under Additional Secretary (NE), MHA at New Delhi on 15.03.2023

to review the progress of implementation of NLFT (SD) Agreement
(2019) and Bru Agreement (2020).

17. The Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act [AFSPA] has been
withdrawn w.e.f. 01.04.2023 from Lakhipur Sub Division of Cachar
district in Assam, 4 Police Station areas (Wangoi of Imphal, West
District, Nambol and Moirang of Bishnupur district and
Leimakhong of Kangpokpi district) in Manipur and 3 Police Station
areas (Akuluto and VK Town of Zunheboto district and Sungro of
Wokha district) in Nagaland.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, May 2023
pages:
Ministry of Home _ Affairs-Major Achievements, — significant
Development and important events for the month of May, 2023.

Hon'ble Union Home Minister visited violence affected areas of Manipur from
29th May, 2023 to Ist June, 2023 to review the security situation of the State of Manipur.

2 Hon'ble Union Home Minister presided over the 'Chintan Shivir of senior officers
of Ministry of Home Affairs on 19th May, 2023 in New Delhi. The objective of the
Chintan Shivir was to interact with the senior officers of the Ministry and to evolve
action plan for implementation of "Vision 2047".

>. On 22.5.2023, Hon'ble Union Home Minister released the bilingual
Compendium on Census of India titled as "A Treatise on Indian Censuses since 1981"
This is a 'Recount of the journey of counting people in India and much more’, while
inaugurating the new Janaganana Bhawan. A web portal for registrations of births &
deaths and an updated SRS App with Geo- fencing feature were also launched.

4. Hon'ble Union Home Minister inaugurated a workshop on the 'Vibrant Villages
Programme’ in New Delhi on 23.05.2023. The national-level workshop was conducted
for capacity building of the State & District level officers for planning & implementation
of VVP from 23™ to 24" May, 2023.

a Hon'ble Home Minister laid the foundation stone and did the Bhumi Poojan of off-
Campus of NFSU at Guwahati, Assam on 25.05.2023. Hon'ble MoS (Home) inaugurated
the ICP Dawki, Meghalya on 04.05.2023.

6. An Indian delegation led by Dr. P.K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to Hon'ble Prime
Minister and having members, Sh. Kamal Kishore, Member & Secretary (I/C), NDMA
and Sh. Sanjeev Kumar Jindal, JS (DM), MHA participated in the High Level Meeting
of the United Nations General Assembly on the Midterm Review of the Sendai
Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction held on 18" — 19" May, 2023 in New York,
USA.

7. British High Commissioner Mr. Alex Ellis met with Union Home Secretary on
26.05.2023 to brief regarding the visit of Lord Tariq Ahmad of Wimbledon, MOS, FCDO, UK
to India. Thereafter, on 29.05.2023, Union Home Secretary held a meeting with Lord Tariq
Ahmad of Wimbledon wherein various bilateral issues relating to Security of Indian High
Commission, Migration & Mobility partnership, criminal records sharing, Diplomatic visa
agreement, Anti India Pro Khalistani elements, E- visa for Crown dependencies etc. were
discussed .

8. Annual Conference of Relief Commissioners/Secretaries Department of Disaster
Management of States /UTs to review the status of preparedness for South West Monsoon-
2023 was held on 9th May, 2023.
9. One of the significant budget announcements this year is to provide financial support
to poor prisoners who are not able to bear the fine or bail amount. The Ministry of Home
Affairs has finalized a Scheme on the subject matter, which is proposed to be rolled out from
the current financial year. Home Minister has written to the Chief Ministers of all States on
23rd May, 2023 informing them of this initiative of the Government of India and have
requested them to extend the benefit of this scheme to poor prisoners.

10. A Model Prisons Act has been finalized by the Ministry of Home Affairs in
consultation with various stakeholders and subject experts. The Model Act, with approval of
HM, has since been forwarded to all States and UTs under cover of a letter from Home
Secretary on 1Oth May, 2023, for making use of the same in their respective jurisdictions.

11. A meeting was held under chairmanship of Secretary (BM) on 12th May, 2023
regarding preparation of Action Plan under VVP. Further, on 31°' May, 2023 Secretary (BM)
held a meeting regarding identification of villages situated in the (i) border blocks of
States/UTs covered under BADP and (ii) blocks along the coastlines in Coastal
States/UTs for comprehensive development.

12. The meeting of Monitoring Committee to monitor and redressal of issues relating to
racial discrimination faced by the people of North East was held under Additional Secretary
(NE), MHA on 25.5.2023 at New Delhi. The meetings of Joint Monitoring Committee
(JMC) under Additional Secretary (NE), MHA were held on 29.05.2023 to review the
progress of implementation Bodo Accord (2020), Karbi Accord (202 1) and Adivasi Peace
Accord (2022) of Assam.

13. Meeting on Special assistance to rehabilitate the affected families at alternative safe
places and undertake planned redevelopment of Joshimath in Uttarakhand was held on 3“
May, 2023 under Additional Secretary (DM), MHA.

14. A meeting was held on 10.05.2023 under Additional Secretary (LWE), MHA with the
officials of DoT and Nodal Officers of all LWE affected states on the subject "Pending issues,
especially security related issues pertaining to mobile/broadband connectivity project in LWE
affected areas". A meeting was held on 11.05.2023 under Additional Secretary (LWE), MHA
with the officials of Chhattisgarh Government, MoRTH, MoRD & CAPFs to review the
construction of roads/bridges works in Chhattisgarh under RRP-I & RCPLWEA. Further, on
23.05.2023, AS(LWE) met with the officials of NYKS to review the "Implementation of
Tribal Youth Exchange Programmes (TYEP)" under Media Scheme.

15. NOC issued for change in the name of village "Bhairavwadi" Tal-Tasgaon as “Navi
Chinchani" in District - Sangli, Maharashtra, "Itavari Railway Station" as "Netaji Subhash
Chandra Bose Itwari Railway Station" in Nagpur, Maharashtra and "Shivamogga city Railway
Station" as “shri Shivappa Nayaka-Shivamogga Railway Station" in Karnataka.
16. | The Bihar Special Courts (Amendment) Bill, 2022 has been assented to by the Hon'ble
President of India. Previous Sanction of the Hon'ble President of India for introduction of The
Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of
Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Madhya Pradesh Amendment
Bill, 2022 in the State Legislature of Madhya Pradesh has been conveyed to the Government
of Madhya Pradesh.

17. Virtual Negotiation meeting with Kazakhstan was held on 31.05.2023 to discuss the
Agreement on Mutual Protection of Classified Information. The Kazakh side was led by Col
Saragul Abdikarim, Head of the Directorate of International Legal Support of the Department
of International Cooperation, MoD and Indian side was led by Joint Secretary (IC), MHA

18. A meeting under Joint Secretary (PM), MHA was held on 01.05.2023 to review the
progress made by CAPFs in implementation of vehicles scrapping policy issued by MoRTH.
Further, a meeting with the States was also held on 30.05.23 regarding scrapping of vehicles
of the State Governments/Police Forces which are more than 15 years old and ensure the
success of Vehicle Scrapping Policy/Voluntary Vehicle-Fleet Modernization Programme
(VVMP). The States were guided/ informed regarding processes involved viz. e-auction,
guidelines regarding determination of Reserve Price of Government vehicles, incentives under
the scheme of Special Assistance to States etc.

19. | Promulgation of the Government of NCT of Delhi (Amendment) Ordinance, 2023 was
issued on 19.05.2023.

20. The 13" meeting of Standing Committee of the Southern Zonal Council was held on
05.05.2023 in Chennai.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, August 2023
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
and important events for the month of August, 2023.

The National Security Strategies Conference (NSSC)-2023 under the
Chairmanship of Hon'ble Home Minister was held on 24th & 25th, August, 2023
to discuss contemporary security issues.

2. Union Home Secretary chaired a meeting of Sub-Committee of National
Executive Committee (SC-NEC), on 09.08.2023 to consider following two flood
mitigation proposals:

(i) Integrated Urban Flood Management for Chennai Corporation (GCC)
under Urban Flooding Risk Management programme for the city of
Chennai having financial outlay of Rs. 561.29 Crore (With Central
assistance of Rs. 500 crore) and;

(ii) Urban Flood Management Programme from Ahmedabad Municipal
Corporation (AMC) under Urban Flooding Risk Management programme
for the city of Ahamedabad having financial outlay of Rs. 277.78 Crore
(With Central assistance of Rs. 250 crore).

3s Union Home Secretary held a meeting on 11.08.2023 at New Delhi with
UK Minister of State for Security.

4. A total of Rs. 36.87 crore was released to CAPFS under Civic Action
Programme (CAP) in LWE affected areas and to Indian Air Force on account of
Airlift provided for Anti-LWE Operations under Assistance to Central Agencies
for LWE Management (ACALWEM) Scheme.

5, In order to re-enact and replace (i) The Indian Penal Code, 1860 with a
new Bhartiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 (ii) The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
with a new Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita Bill, 2023 and (iii) The Indian
Evidence Act, 1872 with the new Bhartiya Sakshya Adhiniyam Bill, 2023, three
Bills have been introduced in the Lok Sabha on 11th August, 2023. These Bills
have been further referred to the Department related Parliamentary Standing
Committee on Home Affairs for consideration and report.

6. The concurrence of Central Government was accorded for release of 19
prisoners as part of special remission to certain categories of prisoners.

7. On the occasion of Independence Day-2023 the following medals have been
awarded to the Police personnel of various States/UTs/ CAPFs/CPOs:-

(i) President's Police Medal for Gallantry : 01 Nos.
(ii) | Police Medal for Gallantry ; 229 Nos
(iii) | President Police Medal for Distinguished Service : 82 Nos.
(iv) | Police Medal for Meritorious Service : 645 Nos.

8. On 12th August, 2023 total 140 officials of State/ Central Intelligence
Agencies have been awarded "Union Home Minister's Medal for Excellence in
Investigation for the year -2023".
9. Meeting of High-Powered Committee (HPC) was held on 11.08.2023 to
consider the Action Plan proposals of the financial year 2023-24 pertaining to
03 States' namely, Karnataka, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh and One UT of Ladakh
under the Scheme of Assistance to States & UTS for Modernization of Police
(ASUMP). An amount of Rs. 5.09 crore has been released to the State
Government of Karnataka under the ASUMP Scheme, vide Ministry's Sanction
Order dated 31.08.2023.

10. NOC issued for change in the name of the name of village "Ghotoi" as
"Qhitohe", "Hukpong" as "Hukphang" and "Yaong Phom" as "Yaongyimchen" in
Nagaland.

11. Sth Executive Committee Meeting was held on 22.08.2023 under the
Chairpersonship of Special Secretary (Internal Security) regarding NCORD.

12. A review meeting under Special Secretary (Internal Security) was held on
02.08.2023 of SRE Standing Committee for J&K to evaluate the progress of many
proposals. Based on recommendation, it was decided that works/proposals of
UT of J&K are considered as per their operational requirements. Status of funds
utilization of various projects was apprised by DG, J&K.

13. Hon'ble President of India has approved 101 awards to the Fire Service,
Home Guards and Civil Defence personnel on the occasion of the Independence
Day, 2023.

(i) President's Fire Service Medal for Gallantry f 03
(ii) Fire Service Medal for Gallantry : O01
(iii) Present's Fire Service Medal for Distinguished Service : 08
(iv) Fire Service medal for Meritorious Service i 41
(v) Present's HG & CD Medal for Distinguished Service : OS
(vi) Home Guards & Civil Defence Medal for Meritorious Service : 43

14. Funds to the tune of Rs. 389.27 Crore was released to the State
Government of Himachal Pradesh under National Disaster Response Fund
(NDRF).

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, October 2023
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development and
important events for the month of October, 2023.

1. A meeting was held on 06.10.2023 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi under the
Chairmanship of Hon’ble Union Home Minister with Chief Ministers, IB,
DsG CAPFs, DGPs of LWE affected States to review left wing extremism
scenario and related issues on both security and development.

2. Hon’ble Union Home Minister interacted with 200 tribal youths at Bharat
Mandapam, New Delhi on 18.10.2023, who participated in the 15" Tribal
Youth Exchange Programme (TYEP) at New Delhi.

3. The 55th High Level Empowered Committee on Border Infrastructure was
on 03.10.2023.

4. On 18.10.2023 Sub-Committee of National Executive Committee (SC-NEC)
met to consider the proposal of National Glacial Lake Outburst Flood
(GLOF) Risk Mitigation Programme (NGRMP). Further on 20.10.2023
SC-NEC again met to consider the Post Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA)
report for recovery and reconstruction needs in respect of the States of
Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Meghalaya.

5. On 09.10.2023, 6th meeting of the Apex Committee of NCORD under
Home Secretary reviewed the progress on the actions being taken.

6. On 14.10.2023, Home Secretary held a meeting to discuss issues related to
National Cyber Forensic Software/Equipment Standardization.

7. Home Secretary on 17.10.2023 reviewed security situation of the State of
Manipur with the Chief Secretary of Manipur.

8. On 12.10.2023 Australian High Commissioner to India called on Union
Home Secretary and discussed the issues of mutual interest.

9. Meeting of Empowered Committee was held on 16.10.2023 under
chairpersonship of Special Secretary (IS) to discuss and review the I4C
scheme and the issues of convergence of NCTC and NCRI&C vertical with

I4C.

10. A series of one-day Review meeting-cum-workshop of regional Joint
Cybercrime Coordination Team (JCCT) were organized and coordinated by
I4C at Guwahati, Vishakhapatnam and Lucknow on 07.10.2023, 12.10.2023
and 18.10.2023 respectively for meaningful review of JCCT and effective
coordination with I4C to prevent cybercrime.

11. Following Bills have been assented to by the Hon'ble President of India:
(i) The Manipur Shops and Establishment (Regulation of Employment
and Conditions of Service) Bill, 2021.
(ii) The Karnataka Societies Registration (Amendment) Bill,,2021.
(iii) The Andhra Pradesh Land Titling Bill, 2022.

12. Shri Raghubar Das has been appointed as Governor of Odisha on
18.10.2023 and Shri Indra Sena Reddy Nallu has been appointed as
Governor of Tripura on 18.10.2023.

13. NOC issued in respect of proposal of change in the name of "Bolagarh
Road Railway Station” as "Manikgoda Railway Station".

14. Gallantry Medals in various categories have been merged and 5 new
medals have been instituted viz. "President's Medal for Gallantry (PMG)",
Medal for Gallantry(GM)", "President's Medal for Distinguished
Service(PSM)", "Medal for Meritorious Service(MSM)". In this regard,
three new portals namely Gallantry Medal-PMG/GM, President's Medal for
Distinguished Service and Medal for Meritorious Service have been on-

boarded on National Award Portal.

15. The National Liberation Front of Tripura (NLFT) and All Tripura Tiger
Force (ATIF) have been declared as ‘unlawful associations’ for a further
period of 5 years upto 02.10.2028 under the provisions of Section 3 of the

Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.

16. A total of 181 cadres of the Dimasa National Liberation Army (DNLA)
formally surrendered on 28.10.2023 in Assam along with huge quantity of
arms ammunition and joined the main stream.

17. An advisory was issued to the State Governments/CAPF's to sensitize them
to counter the LWE activities in the LWE affected areas.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, September 2023
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
and important events for the month of September, 2023.

Union Home Secretary taken following meetings during the month of
September, 2023:

(i) On 01.09.2023, meeting with Chief Secretary of Manipur
to review the security situation of the State of Manipur.

(ii) On 22.09. 2023, meeting with Chief Secretary of Tripura to
review the progress of implementation of Bru Agreement (2020).
(iii) On 30.9.2023, meeting with the delegation of Eastern
Nagaland People's Organization (ENPO) to discuss their
demands.

2. Union Home Secretary chaired a meeting of Sub-Committee of National
Executive Committee (SC-NEC) on 12.09.2023 to consider the Post Disaster
Needs Assessment (PDNA) reports for recovery and reconstruction needs in
respect of the States of Assam, Gujarat and Uttarakhand.

3. Union Home Secretary held a meeting on 22° September, 2023 to
consider the report of Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT) on cyclonic storm
‘Biparjoy” of 2023 in Gujarat.

4. A meeting was held with Members of NDMA on 27'% September, 2023 to
review progress of activities under the National Disaster Mitigation Fund.

5. Ceasefire Agreement with National Socialist Council of Nagaland (K) Niki
group has been extended for a further period of one year w.e.f. 08.09.2023 to

07.09.2024.

6. 8 districts and 21 Police Station areas in 5 other districts of Nagaland and
Tirap, Changlang and Longding districts of Arunachal Pradesh and area of 3 Police
Stations in Namsai district of Arunachal Pradesh, bordering Assam have been
declared as ‘disturbed area’ under Section 3 of the Armed Forces (Special Powers)
Act, 1958 (AFSPA) for a period of six (6) months w.e.f. 01.10.2023 upto 31.3.2024
vide MHA’s Notifications dated 26.9.2023.

7. Government of Manipur has declared the entire State of Manipur excluding the
areas of 19 Police Stations as ‘disturbed area’ for a period of six (6) months w.e.f.
01.10.2023 vide Notification dated 27.09.2023.

8. In Assam, AFSPA has been removed from 4 more districts vide State of
Assam’s Notification dated 27.09.2023.

9. 31St meeting of the Northern Zonal Council was held on 26.09. 2023 in
Amritsar.
10. NOC issued in respect of proposal of change in the name of

(i) Villages “Longpho” as "Longphaoh", "Longching”’ as "Longchang”,
"Goching” as "Chi Guhching”, "Tang” as "Tangnyu”, "Tingalibam” as "Sakho” in Mon
district & village "Dimapur’” as "Phuheto”, in Dimapur district, Nagaland.

(ii) "Udhampur Railway Station” as “Martyr Captain Tushar Mahajan
Railway Station” in Udhampur district, Jammu & Kashmir.

11. Meeting of High Powered Committee (HPC) was held on 04.09.2023 to
consider the Action Plan proposals of the Financial year 2023-24 pertaining to
Maharashtra, Lakshadweep, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu under the
Scheme of Assistance to States & UTs for Modernization of Police (ASUMP).

12. A meeting of Emergency Response Group was held on 01.09.2023 to review
and discuss cyber security issues related to G20 Summit. In order to keep a close
watch and to monitor any untoward incidents of cyber-attack, it was decided to
establish a 24*7 Coordination Control Room comprising of |4C, CERT-In, NCIIPC,

Delhi Police and NIC-CERT to manage cyber-attack during the G-20 leader
Summit.

13. A meeting was held on 05.09.2023 to discuss the provisions of Secure
e-mail set up developed by NIC for 10000 users of Critical/sensitive
Ministry/Department/ Organization. A list of 17 Ministries /Departments was
provided and discussed and agreed that in the initial phase 10000 users
may be migrated to. the secure ZTA e- mail set up by NIC. The same was
followed by a review meeting which was held on 13.09.2023.

14. A series of one-day Review meeting-cum-workshop of regional Joint
Cybercrime Coordination Team (JCCT) was organized and coordinated by |4C
at Hyderabad on 15.09.2023 and at Gandhinagar on 25.09.2023 for

meaningful review of JCCT and effective coordination with 14C to prevent
cybercrime.

16. 37* Meeting of Committee constituted to study the best practices in the
world on Transport Security was held on 20.09.2023 to discuss and find
out an appropriate legal and operational framework for transport security

in the country considering the national security perspectives and existing
mechanisms.

16. An Empowered Committee Meeting for Financial Inclusion in LWE
affected districts was held on 22.09.2023 under AS(LWE) with Officers of D/o
Financial Services and D/o Post.

17. 02 Advisories were issued to the State Governments/ CAPEFs to sensitize
them to counter the LWE activities in the LWE affected areas.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, July 2023
pages:
Ministry  of   Home     Affairs-Major   Achievements,     significant
 Development and important events for the month of July, 2023.


       A meeting between Ambassador                          of United States of America to India, Mr.
 Eric M. Garcetti and Hon’ble Home                        Minister was held on 11.07.2023.                    During
 the meeting matters of mutual interest were discussed.

 2.      A meeting, under the Chairmanship of Hon'ble Home Minister, was held on
  10th July, 2023 to review the proposed amendments in the Disaster Management
 Act, 2005.

3.     G20      conference        on     "CRIME       AND         SECURITY         IN    THE      AGE OF NFTs,     Al
 AND     METAVERSE"    was  held  from   13th-14th  July,  2023. Hon'ble Home
 Minister Shri Amit Shah was the Chief Guest of the Inaugural Session and Shri
 Ashwini Vaishnaw, Hon'ble Minister of Railways, Communication, Electronics &
 Information     Technology            was   the     chief       guest    of the        Valedictory    Session    and
 exhibition was put up at the venue with many startups and Government stalls. It
 was    a Multi-Stakeholders   Conference, comprising  of Regulatory  Agencies,
 Industries, Academic Communities and Experts. The Plenary Session which was a
 part of this conference was attended by G20 +9 Countries as well as invited
 Countries which comprised of EU and international organizations like Interpol,
 UNODC, Caricom, AU etc.

4,     Union      Home        Secretary            held      a     meeting     on         19.07.2023       with   the
 representatives of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Ministry of Power to discuss the
 issues related to development of Pumped Storage Power Projects in Andhra Pradesh
 & Odisha.

o,    A meeting of Central Level Committee (CLC) was held on 07.07.2023
under the Chairmanship of Additional Secretary (LWE) with the Nodal Officers
of Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Odisha & Telangana under Special Central
Assistance (SCA) for most LWE affected districts to review physical & financial
progress.

6.     03      meetings      of    Project         Clearance         Committee            (PCC)     were   held    on
04.07.2023,      05.07.2023            & 12.07.2023 respectively under the Chairmanship                            of
Additional Secretary (LWE) with                    10 States (Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand,                      Odisha,
Telangana, Kerala,        Andhra Pradesh, Bihar,                         Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh
and Maharashtra)           to review progress of                         approved works under Special
Infrastructure Scheme (SIS) for LWE effected areas.

7     Meeting of High Powered Committee (HPC) was held on 11.07.2023 and
25.07.2023 to consider the proposals pertaining to '09 States and 01 UT' Action
Plans under the scheme of Assistance to States & UTs for Modernization of Police
(ASUMP).

8.       Review of the Ist Draft of UN Cyber Crime Convention was held on
 21.07.2023 for discussing the ramifications of this convention on what could be the
 necessary changes in the existing systems if this convention was signed and
 ratified by India.
9.     A meeting on targeting of Indian Co-operative Banks by Cyber Threat
 Groups and finding solutions was held on 31.07.2023 with Ministry of
 Cooperation.

10.   Advisory issued to all States on 04.07.2023 to 'Know your Police: Jane          8
Peher ke Prehari' campaign under the Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav- ‘Unity’ theme.

11.   Ministry   of Home   Affairs   has   launched   a "Scheme   for   Expansion   and
Modernization of Fire Services in the States" from the earmarked allocation of
Preparedness and Capacity Building Funding Window under the National Disaster
Response Fund (NDRF) for strengthening fire services in the States with a total
outlay of Rs. 5,000 crore. An amount of Rs. 500 crore, out of the total outlay, has
been kept for incentivizing the States on the basis of their legal and infrastructure
based reforms.
 12.     On 21.07.2023, High Level Committee has approved proposal of Grant of
additional Central Assistance to the State of Sikkim, for the Flood/Flash
flood/Landslide     of the year 2022 and also the proposal of revised cost estimate
for setting up the Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response (ICR-ER)
project in Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). Funds to the tune of Rs. 9517.20 crore
as Central share, was released to 24 States, under State Disaster Response Fund
(SDREF).

13.   A video conference /meeting was held under the chairmanship of Secretary
(BM) on 13th July, 2023 to review the preparation of Action Plan of Vibrant Villages
Programme (VVP) by the States/UTs.

14.   NOC issued in respect of proposal of change in the name of

      (i)    "Ambewadi Railway Station" as "Dandeli Railway Station" in Karnataka
      "Pratapgrah" as "Maa Belha Devi Dham Pratapgarh Junction” "Antu" as
      "Maa Chandikadevi Dham Antu" and "Bishnathganj" as "Shanidev Dham
      Bishnathganj" in district-Pratapgarh, Uttar Pradesh.

      (ii)   Village "Tanda" as "Juni Baravali Tanda" in Udaipur, Rajasthan.

      (i)    Village "Wanyachiwadi" as "Haripur" in district - Satara, Maharashtra
      "Kedarwadi" as "Kedargaon" in Maharashtra "Dhondgewadi" as "Revangaon
      Khurd", "Bhatwadi" as "Bhatwade", "Dukkarwadi" as "Rampur”, "Chutiya" as
      "Nandgaon" in Maharashtra.
      (iv)   Village "Prem Kotli" as "Kotli Khurd" in district Bathinda, Punjab.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, April 2023
pages:
Ministry  of   Home’    Affairs-Major   Achievements, — significant
 Development and important events for the month of April, 2023.


        A Memorandum of Settlement (MoS) has been signed on 27.04.2023
 between Government of India, Government of Assam and representatives of
 Dimasa National Liberation Army /Dimasa Peoples' Supreme Council (DNLA
 /DPSC) of Assam to end the insurgency in Dima Hasao District of Assam.
 Hon'ble Union Home Minister presided over the signing of this historic
 agreement. As a result of this agreement, over 168 cadres of DNLA have joined
 the mainstream by laying down their arms. As per MoS, a Special Development
 Package of Rs.1,000 crore over five years will be provided by Govt. of India and
 Govt. of Assam for all round development of NCHAC as well as Dimasa people
 residing in other parts of the State.

2.       A historic Agreement was signed at New Delhi on 20.04.2023 by the Chief
 Minister of Assam and the Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh to settle the long-
 pending inter-state border dispute between Assam and Arunachal Pradesh in
 respect of 123 villages. Hon'ble Union Home Minister presided over the signing
 of this historic agreement. Both States have agreed that this agreement will be
 final with regard to 123 disputed villages and neither of the States will make any
 new claim related to any area or village in future.

3:     A Meeting   between   Hon'ble MoS,   Shri Nityanand   Rai and Hon'ble Minister
of Public Secretary of Vietnam was held on 10.04.2023. During the meeting,
bilateral security issues as well as cooperation at the Regional and Multilateral
forums such as ASEAN and G-20 were discussed.

4.       The 5" India- UK Home Affairs Dialogue (HAD) was held on- 12.04.2023.
 Union Home Secretary led the Indian delegation and the UK delegation was led
 by Shri Matthew Rycroft, Permanent Secretary, and Home Office. During the
 meeting both sides reviewed the ongoing cooperation and identified further steps
 that can be taken to explore opportunities and synergies in advancing
 cooperation in counter-terrorism, cyber security, drug trafficking, migration,
 extradition, anti-India activities in UK including Pro-Khalistan Extremism among
 other issues. India’s concerns over the breach of security of Indian High
 Commission were also emphasized.

5,     The ceasefire agreement with National Socialist Council of Nagaland /K-
Khango (NSCN / K-Khango) has been extended for one-year w.e.f. 18.04.2023
to 17.04.2024. Ceasefire agreements with NSCN (NK) and NSCN(R) have been
extended for a further period of one-year w.e .f. 28.04.2023 to 27.04.2024.

6.      Two (2) Meetings were held on 12.04.2023 & 17.04.2023 under the
 chairmanship of AS(LWE ), MHA with Nodal Officers of LWE Affected States, IB
 & CAPFs under Security Related Expenditure (SRE) Scheme to review the LWE
 affected districts.
7.    A   total   of   Rs.83   lakh   released    to   CAPFs   under   Assistance   to   Central
Agencies for LWE Management (ACALWEM) Scheme.

8.     The Himachal Pradesh Ceiling on Land Holdings (Amendment)                     Bill, 2021
 was assented to by the Hon’ble President of India in April, 2023.

9. Constable (GD) examination will be conducted in 13 regional languages other than
Hindi and English. The decision will give impetus to participation of local I oul in the
CAPFs and encourage regional languages

10.    13" meeting of Standing Committee of the Western Zonal Council was held on
15.04.2023 in Gandhinagar.

11.     1° Negotiation Meeting to discuss the Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty in
Criminal Matters was held on 13.04.2023 with Nepal through VC. JS (CIC) attended
the meeting along with representatives of Ministry of Law & Justice, CBI, MEA (L&T)
& 1S.I| Division (MHA) from the Indian side..

12. A meeting was taken by Joint Secretary (CS) on 26.04.2023 with the
representative of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana to discuss the division of Andhra
Bhavan as per the provisions of A.P. Reorganisation Act, 2014.

13. NOC issued for changing the name of "Bagribari Railway Station" as "Mahamaya
Railway Station" in Assam       and name of revenue village "Kukarwari" as
"Ramchandrapur" in Dausa District, Rajasthan.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, February 2023
pages:
Ministry of Home _ Affairs-Major Achievements, — significant
Development and important events for the month of February, 2023.

The Consultative Committee Meeting was held on issues relating to Left Wing
Extremism in February, 2023.

2. Union Home Secretary wrote to the Chief Secretaries of 09 LWE affected
States on the current LWE scenario and suggesting way forward.

a Union Home Secretary held a meeting with Secretary of Department of Home
Affairs, Australia, Mr. Michael Pezzullo on 01.02.2023. During the meeting, issues of
bilateral security concerns were raised including growing incidents of anti-India
Khalistani activities in Australia. He was requested to take swift and stern action against
perpetrators of such violence.

4. Union Home Secretary met the Charged' Affairs, US Embassy, Ambassador Ms.
A. Elizabeth Jones on 10.02.2023. Issues of mutual concern / interests including holding
of 03" Homeland Security Dialogue in 2023 was discussed.

oe Union Home Secretary have also taken a meeting on 24.02.2023 with Chief
Secretary and DGP of Arunachal Pradesh to discuss the measures to augment the
capacity of the Police Force of Arunachal Pradesh.

6. A meeting of Sub-Committee of National Executive Committee (SC-NEC) was
held on 09.02.2023, to consider the reports of the Inter- Ministerial Central Teams
on damages caused by floods/landslides- of 2022 in Karnataka, Assam, Nagaland,
Meghalaya and Gujarat.

7. During the month of February, 2023, an amount of Rs.1976.40 Crore was
released, (Rs.594.80 Cr.-Bihar+ Rs.1353.20 Cr.-Maharashtra + Rs.28.40 Cr.-Tripura) as
Central share of SDRF to the State Governments.

8. Meeting of the Empowered Committee under Special Secretary (IS), MHA was
held on 03.02.2023, for procurement of HAZMAT vehicles by NDRF. Pursuant thereto,
approval for procurement of 04 HAZMAT vehicles by NDRF was given on 21.02 .2023.

9. The Vibrant Villages Programme has been approved on 15.02.2023 by the
Cabinet. Further, a total amount of %123.92 crore has been released, so far, to the
States/UTs under BADP.

10. A meeting was held under the chairmanship of Joint Secretary (BM-II) on
20.02.2023 and 27.02.2023 regarding integration of the features developed by BISAG-N
for VVP in PM "Gati Shakti" portal with the VVP module being developed by NIC in
BADP-OMS.
11. A meeting was held on 08.02.2023 under Additional Secretary (LWE) with the
officials of M/o Information & Broadcasting and other stakeholders regarding
"Distribution of DD Free Dish Receiver Sets with STBs in Strategic areas".

12. A total of Rs.9,03,00,000/- was released to SSB, BSF, CRPF and 02 Coys of 19
Bn CRPF under CAP scheme; Rs.2,34,78,847/- to NYKS under Media Plan Scheme;
Rs.98.23 crore released to Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Odisha &
Telangana States under Special Central Assistance (SCA) Scheme; and Rs.3.59 crore
was released to BSF, CRPF and ITBP under Assistance to Central Agencies for LWE
Management Scheme (ACALWEMS).

13. Meeting between Joint Secretary (CIC) and Deputy Chief of Mission, Embassy of
Israel was held on 21.02.2023 to discuss the possibility of holding the Joint Steering
Committee (JSC) meeting between India & Israel at an early date. Thereafter, in principle
approval has been given to hold the 04" JSC in May, 2023 in New Delhi.

14. 15" meeting of the Standing Committee of Central Zonal Council was held on
02.02.2023 at Dehradun.

15. NOCs have been issued for changing the name of city "Osmanabad" as
"Dharashiv" in Maharashtra & "Aurangabad" as "Sambhaji Nagar" in Maharashtra .

16. Total value of all Sanction accorded to CAPFs during the month of February, 2023
is Rs.86,49,80,694/- for purchase of equipments etc.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, January 2023
pages:
Ministry of Home _ Affairs-Major Achievements, _ significant Development and important events for the month of January, 2023. The President of India has approved conferment of 106 Padma Awards on the occasion of Republic Day, 2023. The list comprises 06 Padma Vibhushan, 09 Padma Bhushan and 91 Padma Shri Awards. Zi Gallantry Medals and Service Medals were awarded to the State/Union Territories/CAPF Officers/ Personnel on the occasion of Republic Day, 2023 including 140 Police Medals for Gallantry, 96 Police Medals for Distinguished Service & 670 Police Medals for Meritorious Service. 3: The President of India has also approved a total of 102 Gallantry & Service medals to the Fire Service, Home Guards and Civil Defence personnel on the occasion of the Republic Day, 2023. 4. Annual DGP Conference, 2022 was held under the chairmanship of Hon'ble Prime Minister from 20"-22" January, 2023. 5. Hon'ble Union Home & Cooperation Minister held a meeting to review the Implementation Plan for the Police Technology Mission. 6. 20" meeting of Standing Committee of the Northern Zonal Council was held on 12" January, 2023 in Chandigarh. Ts Union Home Secretary held a second High-level meeting on Streamlining the Security and Airport Infrastructure in Delhi Airport. A Modern Layout plan for Immigration bay arid enhanced security measures at Delhi Airport were agreed to be put in place. 8. A High Level Central Team led by Secretary (Border Management) having members from MHA, NDMA, CWC, NDRF and GS! was constituted by MHA and visited Dehradun and Joshimath on 09-10" January,2023. Thereafter, on 31% January, 2023, | also reviewed the relief and rehabilitation works being carried out in Joshimath, Chamoli District, Uttarakhand. 9. On 04" January; 2023, SS(IS) held an_ inter-ministerial meeting regarding drafting of Drone Act/Rules which was attended by the representatives of MoCA, Delhi Police DGCA and MHA Stakeholder. 10. Meeting regarding Gati Shakti National Master Plan was chaired by SS (IS) on 12.01.2023 which was attended by representatives of BPR&D, BISAG-N and Director, CDTI, Jaipur. 11. Ono3% January, 2023, SS(IS) held a meeting with the representatives of MHA Stakeholder, MoD, DRDO and senior officers of MHA to discuss the issue regarding continuation of project COSMOS. 12. The names of "Hoshangabad Railway Station" as "Narmadapuram Railway Station" in Madhya Pradesh and village "Nandihal P.H." as "Aaroodha Nandihal" in Karnataka were changed. 13. Following Bills have been assented to by the Hon'ble President of India : (i) The Code of Criminal Procedure (Telangana Amendment) Bill, 2020 on 06" January, 2023. i) The Punjab Bhondedar, Butemar, Dohlidar, Insar Miadi, Mukarraridar, Mundhimar, Panahi Qadeem, Saunjidar or Taraddadkar (Vesting of Proprietary Rights) Bill, 2020 on 13™ January, 2023. 14. | The National Survey of Enemy properties, spread across 20 States and 03 Union Territories, was started by Directorate General of Defence Estates. This will involve more than 12,000 properties already identified by O/o Custodian of Enemy Property for India. The survey started with properties in the State of Uttar Pradesh, wherein a majority of such properties are situated. 15. | Government has approved signing of MoU between Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), India and the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), Nigeria on Prevention of Illicit Trafficking in Narcotic Drugs, Psychotropic Substances and Precursor Chemicals and related matters. 16. On 12" January, 2023 & 18" January, 2023, Secretary (Border Management) held meetings regarding preparation of action plan for the Pilot Project on Vibrant Villages Programme. Further, on 23 January, 2023, he reviewed the telecom connectivity to Border Habitations and Border Out Posts (BOPs) of Border Guarding Forces (BGFs). 17. On10" January, 2023, Additional Secretary (NE), MHA has taken a meeting with Chief Secretary of Assam, CEM of Bodo Territorial Council (BTC) and representatives of Bodo groups of Assam to review the status of implementation of Bodo Accord (2020). 18. During the month of January, 2023 sanctions accorded to CAPFs are to the tune of Rs.190,62,89,386 for various equipments. 19. During the month of January, 2023, an amount of Rs.3555.60 crore has been released as Central share of SDRF to 07 States (viz; Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand and West Bengal). 20. Meetings of the Project Clearance Committee (PCC), MHA were held under the chairmanship of AS(LWE) with States of Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha and Telangana regarding progress of works under Special Infrastructure Scheme (SIS) and Work Plan for extended SIS scheme. 21. A Central Level Committee (CLC) meeting was held on 04" January, 2023 under the chairmanship of AS(LWE) with the Nodal Officers/DCs/DMs/SPs/ DFOs of Jharkhand, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha to review the progress of Special Central Assistance (SCA) Scheme in LWE affected districts and districts of concern. 22. One Advisory was issued to State Governments/CAPFs to sensitize them to counter the LWE activities in the LWE affected areas. 23. In the month of January, 2023, the Government has declared two organizations namely The Resistance Front (TRF) and People’s Anti-Fascist-Front (PAFF) as Terrorist Organizations. 24. In the month of January, 2023, the Government has declared 05 terrorists under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (as amended in 2019) and their names were added to the Fourth schedule of the said Act. 25. During the month under report, NCB seized 605.80 kg, 6854 Bottles and 24946 Tablets of Narcotics & Psychotropic substances and arrested 45 persons for involvement in drug trafficking. 26. Onos" January, 2023 administrative approval and Expenditure amounting to Rs.15,75,029/ - has been issued for acquisition of 390 sq. metres additional private land for construction of an approach road to ITBP’s SHQ at Likabalihas. 27. Final result of 400 native tribal youths as Constables (GD) in CRPF through recruitment rally from interior areas of Bijapur, Dantewada and Sukma district of Chhattisgarh has been declared on 29" November, 2022. Offer of appointment to all the candidates have been issued during the month of January, 2023. 28. MHA vide letter dated 31° January, 2023 has conveyed expenditure sanction for conducting recruitment related activities for CT (Technical & Tradesmen) through EdCIL (India) Limited against the total vacancies of 8686 involving estimated financial implication of Rs.23,83,60,000. 29. Delegation of financial powers of DsG/Directors of CAPFs, & some CPOs under the head ’Major Work’ from Rs.15.00 Crore to Rs.20.00 Crore, under ‘Minor Works’ from Rs.1.00 crore to Rs.2.00 crore and under ‘Land acquisition’ from Rs.5.00 crore to Rs.10.00 crore have been enhanced vide Ministry's OM No.|I-27012/54/2017-PF.1| dated 19" January, 2023. 30. Total 37,15,341 Ayushman CAPF cards have been issued to the beneficiaries. Total 1622 CGHS empanelled hospitals and 13,095 private AB-PMJAY empanelled hospitals are providing cashless health care services to CAPF beneficiaries under this scheme. 31. 1477 nos. of posts have been sanctioned for creation on augmentation of CISF Unit IGI Delhi, Mangalore Airport, SAC-PRL Ahmedabad, GAIL Pata and KAPS Kakrapar, 48 No. of posts have been sanctioned for reduction from CISF Unit, NTPC Kayamkulam and Infosys Mysore in the month of January, 2023. docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, December 2022
pages:
Ministry of Home _ Affairs-Major Achievements, _ significant
Development and important events for the month of December, 2022.

Union Home and Cooperation Minister presided over the 25" meeting of the
Eastern Zonal Council held in Kolkata on 07.12.2022.

2. On 09.12.2022, Union Home Secretary reviewed the implementation of
various guidelines/ SoPs/National Disaster Management Plan-2019 issued by NDMA
and other related issues on various disasters so as to minimize human losses in the
country, with all States/ UTs.

3. The 12" meeting of the Governing Body (GB) of the National Institute of Disaster
Management (NIDM) was held on 02.12.2022.

4. On 16.12.2022, Union Home Secretary held the meeting of the Sub-Committee of
National Executive Committee (SC-NEC), to consider the report of the Inter Ministerial
Central Teams on damage caused by Flood/landslides of 2022 in the States of Himachal
Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh.

5, A meeting regarding optimal use of PM-GATI Shakti portal by NE States (through
VC/Physical) was held by Home Secretary on 01.12.2022. DPIIT and BISAG(N) have
given detailed presentation on use of said portal in the meeting. The Senior Officers of
all NE States as well as MHA, MoDoNER, DPIIT, NEC, NESAC and Survey of India from
North East Region participated in the meeting.

6. Union Home Secretary reviewed the status of settlement of inter-state border
issues on 02.12.2022 and 26.12.2022 with the Chief Secretaries of Assam and
Arunachal Pradesh.

7. On 05.12.2022, Union Home Secretary wrote to the Secretaries, Power, I|&B
and Telecommunication regarding sharing of tower infrastructure for services such
as FM Radio, Mobile etc. in LWE affected and other difficult areas.

8. Ambassador of Germany met Home Secretary on 01.12.2022 and issues of
mutual concern were discussed.

9. Union Home Secretary held a meeting on 02.12.2022 with High Commissioner of
India to Bangladesh. Thereafter, the 18" Meeting of the Joint Working Group (JWG) on
Security and Border Management between India and Bangladesh was held on 5" -
6'" December, 2022 at New Delhi. The Indian delegation was led by Additional
Secretary (North East), MHA and the Bangladesh delegation was led by Additional
Secretary, Public Security Division, MHA, and Govt. of Bangladesh.

10. A Meeting was held on 16.12.2022 by the AS(LWE) with DGP Chhattisgarh and
Officers from Chhattisgarh State,& other Officers from D/o Telecom, M/o Rural
Development and M/o Railways regarding pending issues pertaining to the State of
Chhattisgarh.
11. A Central Level Committee (CLC) meeting was held on 30.12.2022 under the
Chairmanship of AS(LWE) with Senior Officers from Home/Police Department & Nodal
Officers of concerned of all LWE States to review the physical and Financial progress
under the Special Central Assistance (SCA) to most LWE affected districts & District of
Concern (DoC).

12. One Advisory was issued to State Governments/ CAPFs to sensitize them to
counter the LWE activities in the LWE affected areas.

13. | During the month of December, 2022, following bills have been assented to by
the Hon’ble President of India.

(i) The Tamil Nadu Apartment Ownership Bill, 2022
(ii) The Cade of Criminal Procedure (Manipur 3rd Amendment) Bill, 2022.
(iii) | The Factories (Assam Amendment) Bill, 2020

14. Final Negotiation Meeting on Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty in Criminal Matters
with Saudi Arabia was held on 06.12.2022 through VC. The Government of Kingdom of
the Saudi Arabia Delegation was led by Dr. Omar Saleh Al-Zahrani from Ministry of.
Justice and the Indian Delegation was led by Joint Secretary (CIC), MHA.

15. Presidential order has been issued for extending the time limit upto 01.06.2024
for conferring local status to candidates who migrate from any part of Telangana to
Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation for purpose of education and employment.

16. NOCs issued against proposals received from State Government for changing
the name of villages, towns, Railway Stations viz. ‘Nasrullaganj Nagar’ as 'Bhairunda’ in
Sehore District, Madhya Pradesh; Baudpur’ Railway Station under Khurda Division to
‘Randia Baudpur’ Railway Station; village ‘Kundam’ as ‘Kundeshwar Dham’ in District
Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh; revenue village ‘Bhaidgaon’ as ‘Devnagar’ in Janpad-
Rudraprayag, Uttarakhand; village ‘Sangama’ as 'Kundala Sangama’ of Bagalakote
District, Karnataka State; Veerangana Laxmibai Railway Station’ as Veerangana
Laxmibai Jhansi Railway’ in District Jnansi, Uttar Pradesh.

17. Total Value of all Sanction accorded to CAPFs during the month of December,
2022 is Rs. 1,15,26,38,779/- for procurement of equipments etc.

18. | During the month of December,2022, an amount of Rs.28.40 Crore was released,
as Central share of SDRF to the State Government of Tripura on 20.12.2022.

19. Three days training on Stata software imparted to about 70 Deputy Director and
below level technical grade officers of the ORGI in two batches from 19" to 21°
December, 2022 and 22" to 24"" December, 2022.
20. A total of 1,179 Cadres of United Democratic Liberation Front of Barak Valley
(UDLF/BV-545) and Bru Revolutionary Army of Union (BRA/U-634) surrendered along
with 335 arms on 12.12.2022 in Hailakandi district of Assam.

21. The Government of India and the Government of Manipur entered into a
Cessation of Operation (CoO) Agreement with Zeliangrong United Front (ZUF) group of
Manipur on 27.12.2022. ZUF agreed to abjure violence and join the peaceful democratic
process as established by iaw of the land.

22. National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) organized a two-day Conference on
‘Good Practices on CCTNS/ICJS’ on 15" & 16" December, 2022, in order to recognize
the persistent and path breaking efforts made by States/UTs in implementation of
CCTNS and ICJS projects as well as to disseminate the good practices adopted by
them. The event was inaugurated by Shri Ajay Kumar Mishra, Hon'ble MoS (Home).

23. During the month, more than 1800 kg of narcotic substance, 45,936 Proxyvon
tablets, 3293 bottles of Codeine based cough syrup etc. were seized and 31 persons
were arrested for their involvement in drug trafficking.

24. Audited Accounts of NHRC for the year 2020-21 were laid or the table of Lok
Sabha and Rajya Sabha on 13.12.2022 and 14.12.2022 respectively

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, November 2022
pages:
Ministry      of     Home       Affairs-Major           Achievements,         significant
 Development        and   important      events    for    the   month    of    November,
 2022.


        The Ministry of Home Affairs hosted the 3™ Ministerial Level Conference on
 Counter-Terrorism Financing ‘No Money For Terror' (NMFT) during 18-19" November,
 2022 to collaborate with countries across the world for suppressing the funding sources
 that allow terrorists and extremists to carry out their violent acts. Delegations from 77
 countries and 16 multilateral organizations participated in the Conference.

 2,     Union Home Secretary held a meeting with Civil Defence                Committee      on
 04.11.2022   in North Block, New       Delhi to review policies and           measures      for
 implementation of Civil Defence Set up in the country.

 3.      On 29.11.2022 Union Home Secretary held a meeting through Video Conference
 regarding finalization of details under the Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP).

4.     The Maharashtra Housing and Area Development (Amendment)               Bill, 2020    has
 been assented to by the Hon’ble President of India on 22.11.2022.

5       The first virtual Negotiation Meeting on Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty in
Criminal Matters with Saudi Arabia was held on 07.11.2022. The Indian side was led by
JS, Admin with representations from MEA,CBI, Law & Justice & IS.1l Division, MHA.

6.      Meeting between Government of India delegation led by Additional Secretary
 (WS), MHA and Belarus delegation led by Deputy Chairman of State Forensic
 Examination Committee was held on 09.11.2022.

7.     NOC issued for changing the name of “Ahroura Road Railway                 Station”    as
“Narayanpur Bazar Railway Station” in District Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh.

8.      A Meeting was held on 09.11.2022 under AS (LWE) with IG (Ops), ITBP, CRPF &
 CRPF-Odisha,     DIG (Ops)    ITBP-Chhattisgarh,    Director Intelligence-Bhubaneswar,
 Odisha, AD (IB) and Nodal officers from Chhattisgarh & Odisha State for considering the
 proposals of Odisha and ITBP Police under Assistance to Central Agencies for LWE
 Management (ACALWEM) Scheme.

9.     A Project Clearing Committee (PCC) review meeting was held on 11.11.2022
under AS(LWE) with Senior Officers from Home/ Police Department & Nodal Officers of
LWE States including Uttar Pradesh & West Bengal regarding progress of works under
Special Infrastructure Scheme (SIS) and Work Plan for extended SIS Scheme.

10.    A total of Rs. 6,07,13,250 released to Indian Air Force on account of Airlift
provided for Anti-LWE Operations and CAPFs under Assistance to Central Agencies
for LWE Management (ACALWEM) Scheme.
11.    A meeting was taken by Additional Secretary (NE), MHA with Chief Secretaries
and Senior Officers of Governments of Assam and Meghalaya on 28.11.2022 to discuss
the situation arising out of violent incident occurred on 22.11.2022 at Assam-Meghalaya
inter-state border.

12.     A meeting was held under the Chairmanship of Secretary (BM) on 23.11.2022,
regarding implementation of Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) in Border Villages.

13.     The first virtual meeting of Joint Working Group (JWG) between India and
Turkmenistan was held on 14.11.2022 for the cooperation in the field of Disaster
Management.      From    Indian side, the meeting was        chaired   by JS (DM),       MHA    with the
representatives from MEA, NDRF, NIDM & IMD. The meeting of JWG was held as per
Article ‘6" and MoU signed between India and                     Turkmenistan     on    14.11.2022      on
cooperation in the field of Disaster Management.

14.     During the month of November, 2022, an amount of Rs. 21.20 crore was
released in advance, as Central share of SDRF to the State Government of Sikkim on
17.11.2022,

15.        Total sanction accorded to CAPFs during the month of November 2022 is Rs.
8,14,54,478/ - for procurement of various equipments, vehicles etc.

16.    A meeting of High Powered Committee under the chairmanship of JS (PM) was
held on 24.11.2022 to consider annual Action Plans of 03 remaining States (Punjab,
West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh) and proposals of change of items. However, only the
Government of Punjab presented their Action Plan, which was approved by the
Committee.

17.      On 02.11.2022,     sanction for prosecution was          accorded    against 39 accused        in
accordance     with section       196 of CrPC    and   section    45(1) of the Unlawful        Activities
(Prevention) Act, 1967.

18.    Total 106 Coys of CAPFs (RAF-17, CRPF-21, BSF-19, SSB-16, ITBP-17, &
CISF-16) as direct induction have been ordered for deployment in various States/ UTs
(i.e   Chandigarh,   Jharkhand,       Madhya     Pradesh,   Arunachal        Pradesh,    Kerala,     Uttar
Pradesh,     Delhi and    Dadra    & Nagar     Haveli) for law and order duties for a specific
deployment period in the month of November-2022.

19.     The deployment period of 11 CAPFs Coys (CRPF-07, BSF-01, SSB-02 & CISF-
01) have been extended in the month of November,2022 in various states (i.e
Delhi, West Bengal & Ladakh) for law and order duties/ security arrangements.

20.    Total 126 Coys of CAPFs (CRPF-27, BSF-33, SSB-24, and ITBP-18 & CISF 24)
as direct induction have been ordered to deploy in various States (i.e Chhattisgarh,
Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan & Bihar) for Bye Election related duties in the month
of November, 2022.
21,    MHA has conveyed additional sanction of Rs. 3,25,104/- for acquisition of 2.876
acres land for Group Centre, CRPF, Bijnor, Lucknow-implementation of court order
dated 22.09.2021.

22.    23304 offer/Appointment letter issued to new appointees by CAPFs         & ARs
across the country during the month of November, 2022 as part of Rozgar Mela.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, October 2022
pages:
Ministry of Home _ Affairs-Major Achievements, — significant
Development and important events for the month of October, 2022.

A "Chintan Shivir" was organized by MHA from 27-28 October 2022 with the
Home Ministers of the States/UTs along with the Home Secretaries and DsG, Police of
the States/ UTs. The Chintan Shivir was presided over by the Union Home Minister.
The Hon'ble Prime Minister also addressed the Chintan Shivir on 28" October, 2022.
The Chintan Shivir, deliberated on selected topics of mutual concern to both the Centre
and the States.

Z. On 21* October, 2022, the National Crisis Management Committee (NCMC) met
under the Chairmanship of Cabinet Secretary to review the preparedness of Central

Ministries/Agencies and State /UT Governments for the impending cyclonic storm
‘SITRANG’ over the Bay of Bengal.

3. Union Home Secretary held a virtual meeting on 25" October, 2022 with Chief
Secretaries and DsGP of all States / UTs pertaining to the conduct of G20 events to
be held in India.

4. A meeting under Additional Secretary (DM) was held on 7" October, 2022 to
review the progress of infrastructure development of NDRF Academy, Nagpur.

5; During the month, the following bills have been assented to by the Hon’ble
President of India:

(i) The Code of Criminal Procedure (Gujarat Amendment) Bill, 2021
(ii) The Indian Partnership (Gujarat Amendment) Bill, 2021
(iii) | The Factories (Odisha Amendment) Bill, 2020

6. A meeting was taken by Joint Secretary (CS) on 17" October, 2022 with the
representatives of Office of Accountant Generals and State Government Officers to
discuss the apportionment of pension liabilities between Bihar and Jharkhand.

f. NOCs were issued for change in the name of Nagar Panchayat "Mundera
Baazar" as "Chauri-Chaura’ in Gorakhpur District and village” Telia Afghan" as ‘Telia
Shukla” in Deoria District, Uttar Pradesh.

8. A review meeting was held on 07" October, 2022 under AS(LWE) with Senior
Officers from Home / Police Department & Nodal Officers of LWE State (Bihar, MP &
UP) regarding progress of works under Special Infrastructure Scheme (SIS) and for
consideration of modification proposals under SIS scheme of Bihar, Madhya
Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
9. A Review Meeting was held on 18" October, 2022 with Senior Officers & Nodal
officers from most LWE affected districts and District of Concern (DoC) regarding
updation of data on MIS portal under Special Central Assistance (SCA) Scheme for
most LWE affected districts and District of Concern (DoC).

10. A total of Rs. 26.84 crore was released to Jharkhand State under Security
Related Expenditure (SRE) Scheme. Further, a total of Rs. 3.28 crore was released to
CRPF under Assistance to Central Agencies for LWE Management (ACALWEM)
Scheme.

11. On 17" October, 2022, a Meeting under Additional Secretary (NE), MHA was
held at New Delhi with the Monitoring Committee to monitor and redress issues
relating to racial discrimination faced by NE people.

12. During the month, meetings of Joint Monitoring Committee were held under
Additional Secretary (NE), MHA at New Delhi to review the progress of implementation
of the Bodo Accord, Karbi Accord, NLFT (SD) Agreement and the Bru Agreement.

13. The Central Government vide Notification No. S.O 4670 (E) to 4679 (E) dated
04" October, 2022 has declared 10 terrorists under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention)
Act 1967 (as amended in 2019) and their names were added to the Fourth Schedule
of the said Act.

14. On 06" October,2022 sanction for prosecution was accorded against 22 accused
persons in accordance with section 196 of CrPC and section 45(1) of the Unlawful
Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.

15. Total 57 Coys of CAPFs (RAF-38, CRPF-03, BSF-03, SSB-07, ITBP-04, & CISF-
02) were deployed in Puducherry, Telangana, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Delhi,
Haryana & Tamil Nadu for law and order duties for a specific deployment period.

16. Total 303 Coys of CAPFs (CRPF-85, BSF-61, SSB-56, ITBP-43, CISF-38 & RPF-
20) were deployed in Telangana, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, Haryana,
Odisha, Uttar Pradesh & Gujarat) for Bye Election/Assembly Election-2022.

17. | Sanction of Rs. 10.84 crore was conveyed for acquisition of 140 Kanal 19 Marla
land (17.52 acres) at 02 locations of District Pulwama (J&K) for establishment of
Battalion camping Sites of CRPF. Further, sanction of Rs. 4.65 crore was conveyed for
acquisition of 2.876 acres land for Group Centre CRPF, Bijnor, Lucknow.

18. Revised Items & Norms of Assistance from the State Disaster Response Fund
(SDRF)/National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) for the period of 2022-26 were issued
by MHA on 10" October, 2022.
19. An amount of Rs.17.20 crore as Central Share of SDRF was released in advance
by Central Government to State Government of Nagaland on 20" October,2022. °
Further,an amount 487.40 Cr. (Rs. 2.40 Cr. to Goa, Rs. 99.00 Cr. to Punjab & Rs.
386 Cr. to UP) as Central share of State Disaster Mitigation Fund (SDMF) was released
by Central Government on 06" October, 2022.

20. During the month, the total value of all sanctions accorded to CAPFs for
procurement of equipments, vehicles etc is Rs.116.03 crore.

21. ‘112’ Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) have been integrated with
‘139’ Rail Madad in all States and UTs.
