docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, September 2022
pages:
Ministry of Home _ Affairs-Major Achievements, — significant
Development and important events for the month of September,
2022.

A Memorandum of Settlement (MoS) has been signed on 15.09.2022 between
Gol, Government of Assam and representatives of 8 Adivasi Groups (BCF, ACMA,
AANLA, APA, STF, AANLAJ FG, BCF/ BT and ACMA/ FG) to end the decade's old crisis
of Adivasis and tea garden workers in Assam. Hon'ble Home Minister presided over the
signing of this historic agreement.

2. Hon'ble Home Minister chaired a meeting with Chief Ministers of Arunachal
Pradesh and Assam on 15.09.2022 at New Delhi on Assam-Arunachal Pradesh inter-
state border issues. Both States have prepared a roadmap to resolve their inter-state
border issues.

31 Hon'ble Home Minister chaired a meeting with Chief Minister of Tripura on
20.09.2022 to review implementation of Bru Agreement (2020). Timeline of Bru
agreement has been extended upto 28.02.2023.

4. Hon'ble Home Minister held a meeting on 09.09.2022 to review the revision of
items and Norms of Assistance from State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and
National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) for the period of 2021-26.

5. Hon'ble Home Minister took a meeting on 30.09.2022 to discuss the proposed
Agenda items for 8" meeting of NDMA to be chaired by Hon'ble Prime Minister.

6. Union Home Secretary had taken a meeting on 27.09.2022 with the Chief
Secretaries of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana along with the Ministries/ Departments
concerned to discuss the issues arising out of implementation of provisions of Andhra
Pradesh Reorganization Act, 2014.

7. Union Home Secretary held a meeting on 08.09.2022 to discuss issues regarding
sharing of Towers Infrastructure installed in LWE affected areas for services such as
mobile, FM Radio etc., with Secretary (1&B), Administrator (USOF) and other senior
officers.

8. Union Home Secretary had written to Secretary (MoRD) regarding inclusion of 13
(5 Most affected and 8 Districts of Concern) districts under their Roshni Scheme.

9. Union Home Secretary held the 53 High Level Empowered Committee meeting
on 14.09.2022 at North Block, New Delhi on border infrastructure.

10. —_In principle approval on Amendment to Census Act has been given by Hon'ble
Home Minister.

11. A two days All India DCOs conference was held on 15-16 September, 2022 at
Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi.
12. The Uttarakhand Civil Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2021 has been assented to by the
Hon'b1e President of India on 07.09.2022.

13. The Popular Front of India (PFI) and its associates or affiliates or fronts including
Rehab India Foundation (RIF), Campus Front of India (CFI), All India Imams Council
(AlIC), National Confederation of Human Rights Organization (NCHRO), National
Women’s Front, Junior Front, Empower India Foundation and Rehab Foundation, Kerala
has been declared as ‘unlawful association’ vide Notification dated the 28th September,
2022, published in the Gazette of India.

14. During the month of September, sanction for prosecution for filing the charge
sheet against 33 accused was accorded in accordance with section 45 (1) of the
Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 and 196 of CrPC.

15. | A Ceasefire Agreement with National Socialist Council of Nagaland (K)Niki group
has been extended for a further period of one year w.e.f. 08.09.2022 to 07.09.2023.

16. A Meeting was held on 12.09.2022 by Additional Secretary (LWE), MHA with
senior officers of Central Para Military Forces, three States namely Chhattisgarh, Odisha
& Maharashtra and other agencies regarding filling up of Security vacuum in LWE
affected areas of these States including their inter-state borders.

17. A meeting of the Standing Committee of Assistance to Central Agencies for LWE
Management (ACALWEM) Scheme was held on 02.09.2022 by Addl. Secretary (LWE),
MHA with Nodal officers of LWE affected areas & concerned agencies of MHA. Plan for
opening new camps for security forces, strengthening their existing camps, physical &
financial progress of construction of Night Landing Facilities and Joint Task Force
Camps were reviewed and finalized.

18. The 10" ORGI Seminar lecture on the topic "Bridging the Last Mile in Pro Poor
Public Welfare" was delivered by Shri Amarjeet Sinha, Member, Public Enterprises
Selection Board in the mixed mode (online and physical) at the ORGI’s Conference
Room, NDCC-11 Building Jai Singh Road, New Delhi, on 29"" September, 2022. Around
250 officers of ORGI/ DCOs attended the same.

19. Meeting between Gol delegation led by Joint Secretary (IC), MHA and US
delegation led by Assistant Secretary, Department of Homeland Security was held on
28.09.2022 to discuss issues relating to Homeland Security Dialogue.

20. A total of Rs. 237.87 crore released to Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh,
Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana and West Bengal States under
Security Related Expenditure (SRE) Scheme and Rs.20.87 crore was released to
Jharkhand and Bihar States under Special Infrastructure Scheme (SIS) including
construction of 250 Fortified Police Stations. Further, Rs.18.63 crore has been approved
for CRPF, BSF, ITBP and SSB under Civic Acton Programme (CAP) in LWE affected
areas.
21. Total Value of all Sanction accorded to CAPFs during the month of September is
Rs. 83.44 crore for various equipments etc.

22. During the month of September, 2022, an amount of Rs.780.00 crore was
released, as Central share of SDRF to 3 States (viz. Mizoram, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka).
In addition, an amount of Rs. 450.00 crore was released in advance from NDRF to the 2
States (viz Himachal Pradesh, Assam).

23. High Powered Committee under Joint Secretary (PM), MHA considered and
approved annual Action Plans of all 8 UTs and 9 States by holding 5 meetings on
05.09. 2022, 13.09.2022, 16.09.2022, 19.09.2022 and 26.09.2022.

24. ‘Total 64 Coys of CAPFs (RAF 36, CRPF-11, BSF-03, SSB-08, ITBP-05, & CISF-
01) as direct induction have been ordered for deployment in various States/ UTs of
Puducherry, Chandigarh, Jharkhand, Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Delhi,
Gujarat, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh & Lakshadweep for law and order duties for a
specific deployment period.

25. Vide MHA’s Notifications dated 30.09.2022, 9 districts and area of 16 Police
Stations in 4 other districts of Nagaland and Tirap Changlang and Longding districts
of Arunachal Pradesh and area of 2 police stations in Namsai district of Arunachal
Pradesh, bordering Assam have been declared as ‘disturbed areas’ under Section
3 of the Armed Forces(Special Powers) Act, 1948 for period of six months w.e.f.
01.10.2022 upto 31.03.2023.

26. During this period, outlying units comprising of the CDTIs & CAPT conducted a
range of training sessions which included 51 offline and 3 online course s and trained
5130 Personnel. A wide spectrum of professional courses was conducted.

27. Following regulations have been notified in the Gazette of India (Extraordinary)
on 19/09/2022 under Article 240 of the Constitution.

(i) “The Lakshadweep Value Added Tax Regulation, 2022”.

(11) “The Lakshadweep (Right to Public Services) Regulation, 2022”.

(iii} | “The Lakshadweep Building Development Board (Repeal) Regulation, 2022”.
(iv) “The Lakshadweep Co-operative Societies Regulation, 2022”.

(v) “The Lakshadweep Panchayat Regulation, 2022”.

28. | NOC issued for change in the name of “Patalpani Railway Station” as “Jannayak
Tantya Bhill Railway Station” in Indore District and name of village “Islam Nagar” as
“Jagdishpur” in Madhya Pradesh.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, August 2022
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant
Development and important events for the month of August, 2022.


       On 22nd August, 2022, 23rd meeting of Central Zonal Council was held at Bhopal
under the chairmanship of Hon'ble Union Home Minister. Chief Ministers of States of
Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Chhattisgarh were also present in the
meeting.

2.     Hon’ble Union Home Minister inaugurated the Centre of Excellence (CoE) for
DNA Forensics, Centre of Excellence for Cyber Security and Centre of Excellence for
Investigative and Forensic Psychology in NFSU, Gandhinagar.

3.   Hon'ble Union Home Minister performed the ‘Bhoomi Pujan’ for setting up a new
Campus of the National Forensic Sciences University at Bhopal.

4.      Hon’ble Union Home Minister launched the National Automated Fingerprint
Identification System (NAFIS) of the NCRB at the inaugural session of 2-day
National Security Strategies Conference-2022 in New Delhi. NAFIS will help in
investigation of cases with the help of centralized finger print database.

5.     Meeting of SCO Ministers of Internal Affairs & Public Security was held in
Tashkent from 17-19 August, 2022. The Government of India Delegation was led by
Shri Nityanand Rai, Hon'ble Minister of State for Home.

6.      ‘10th National Conference of Women in Police (NCWP)” was organized by
BPR&D in collaboration with Himachal Pradesh Police on 21-22 August 2022 at
Shimla, Himachal Pradesh. The conference was inaugurated by Hon’ble MoS (Home
Affairs) Government of India, Shri Nityanand Rai while Hon'ble Governor of Himachal
Pradesh Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar graced the valediction function.

7.    Additional Secretary (LWE) attended the Unified Command meeting chaired by
the CM, Chhattisgarh in Raipur to assess the left wing extremism scenario and discuss
the way forward to address the problem in Chhattisgarh.

8.    A total of Rs. 14,95,65,000/- was released to Indian Air Force on account of Airlift
charges provided for Anti-LWE Operations under Assistance to Central Agencies for
LWE Management (ACALWEM) Scheme.

9.     Under the aegis of the commemoration of 75th anniversary of India's
Independence “Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav", it was proposed to give Special Remission
to certain categories of prisoners in three phases. During first phase, 37 prisoners,
where concurrence of the Central Government was required, were released.

10.   The Registration (Tamil Nadu Second Amendment) Bill, 2021 and the Himachal
Pradesh Lokayukta (Amendment) Bill, 2021 have been assented to by the Hon’ble
President of India on 06th August, 2022 and 31st August, 2022 respectively.
11.     A M oll was signed between the National Disaster Management Authority
(NDMA) of the Republic of India and the National Disaster Management Authority
(NDMA) of the Republic of Maldives on cooperation in the field of Disaster
Management on 02nd August, 2022, during the visit of the President of Maldives
to India.

12.     NOCs were issued for changing the name of village “ Pilkhichamar” as
“Pilkhi” in Uttrakhand and village “Kunchi” as “Chandangarh” in Madhya Pradesh.

13.    Sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet against 42 accused persons
was accorded in accordance with section 45(1) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention)
Act, 1967.

14.    During the month of August 2022, total value of sanction of Rs. 102,92, 24,725
was issued to CAPFs under various Modernization heads.

15.   On 08th August, 2022, Guidelines of the scheme of “Assistance to States &
UTs for Modernization of Police” have been circulated.

16.   A total of 101 awards to the Fire Service, Home Guard and Civil Defence
personnel were announced on the occasion of the Independence Day, 2022.

17.    347 Police Medals for Gallantry (PMG), 87 President’s Police Medal (PPM) for
Distinguished Service and 648 Police Medal (PM) for Meritorious Service were
announced on the occasion of the Independence Day, 2022 for Police Personnel.
Further, 151 Home Minister's Medal for Excellence in Investigation were also
announced or this occasion.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, July 2022
pages:
Ministry  of   Home _ Affairs-Major    Achievements,     significant
  Development and important events for the month of July, 2022.


         On 19.07.2022, Hon'ble Home Minister chaired a review meeting with the heads of
 Central Police Trainings Institutes in which DGs of CAPFs also participated.

2.       On 30.07.2022, Hon’ble Union Home Minister also chaired a National Conference on
 “Drug Trafficking and National Security” at Raj Bhawan, Chandigarh with stakeholders from
 Central / State Government and Chief Ministers /Administrators / Lieutenant Governors of
 Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, UTs of Chandigarh and J&K. In continuation of this, a
 Conference on “Thematic cum Technical Session” for discussion on drug related issues was
 also held on 31.07.2022 with Chief Secretaries of concerned States and representatives from
 Central/ State Governments.

 S.      On 01.07.2022, Union Home Secretary held a meeting with the High Commissioner,
 Sri Lanka.

 4,      Union   Home      Secretary also chaired a meeting   on 14.07.2022 to discuss the
 feedback report on MMPDS        (Multi Mode Passive Detection System).

 5.     A Meeting was held on 05.07.2022 under the Chairmanship of AS(LWE) with the
 representatives of CAPFs and NYKS to review the implementation of MHA schemes i.e.
 ACALWEMS, Media Plan and CAP.

6.      Three Central Level Committee (CLC) meetings were held on 06.07.2022,
 07.07.2022 & 11.07.2022 under the Chairmanship of AS (LWE) with the Nodal Officers
/DCs/DMs/SPs/DFOs of Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Kerala,
Maharashtra and Odisha to review the progress of Special Central Assistance (SCA)
Scheme in LWE affected districts and districts of concern.

7       A Meeting       (through VC) was   held on 08.07.2022   under the Chairmanship    of
AS(LWE) with the Nodal Officers of 09 LWE affected States to review the progress of
works    under   Special    Infrastructure Scheme (SIS) in LWE affected areas.

8.      On 22.07.2022, sanction for prosecution was accorded against 07 accused
 persons in accordance with section 188 of CrPC in respect of NIA Case relating to
seizure of Counterfeit/ Fake Indian Currency Notes (FICN) worth Rupees 72.50 Lakh of
1000 and 500 rupee denomination.

9.        On 28.07.2022, sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet against 5
 accused persons was accorded in accordance with section 45(1) of the Unlawful
 Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.

10.    On 29.06.2022, approval has been granted for Categorization of the Coalition
for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) as an “International Organization” and
signing of Headquarters Agreement with CDRI for granting exemptions, immunities and
privileges as contemplated under the United Nations (Privileges and Immunities) Act,
1947 to CDRI.
11.    BPR&D organized a national symposium on "Trends in Dark net Crimes and
Monitoring Techniques (Special focus on Crypto currency driven crimes)" on 30.
06.2022, in which 512 personnel participated.

12.    On       15.07.2022,      a   meeting          of      the   members        of   "Micro      Mission:03
(Communication        &     Technology)"        was   held      under     the   Chairmanship      of the    DG,
BPR&D.

13.    An      advisory   was    issued    to     all Registrar         of High   Courts   to    hold   Judicial
Colloquium on Human Trafficking to sensitize the Judicial officers of all State /UTs.

14. | During the month of July 2022, following Bills have been assented to by the Hon
‘ble President of India:

      (i)        The Industrial Disputes (Uttarakhand Amendment) Bill, 2020 - On 30.05.
                 2022.

      (ii)       The Societies Registration (Uttar Pradesh Amendment) Bill, 2021: On 07.
                 07.2022.

       (iii)   © The    Haryana    Dholidar   Bhutimar, Bhondedar    and  Muqgararidar
                 (Vesting of Proprietary’ Rights) Amendment Bill, 2018 on 20.07.2022

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, June 2022
pages:
Ministry  of   Home _ Affairs-Major    Achievements, _ significant
 Development and important events for the month of June, 2022.


          Two meetings of the Parliamentary Consultative Committee for the Ministry of
 Home Affairs on the subject of "Disaster Management" and "Forensic Science
 Capacities: Strengthening for Timely and Scientific Investigation" were held under the
 chairmanship of Hon’ble Union Home Minister on 25.06.2022 & 26.06.2022 in Kevadia,
 Gujarat.

 Z      On 20.06.2022, a National Conference on "Cyber Apradh Se Azadi" was
 organized at Vigyan Bhawan.        Hon'ble Union Home      Minister inaugurated the
 Conference. It was attended by 1400 (approx.) persons from States/UTs Police, CAPFs,
 CPOs, judicial and students.

 3:     A meeting under the Chairmanship of Hon'ble Union Home Minister was held on
 02.06.2022 to review the overall preparedness to deal with floods in the coming
 monsoon season.

 4,        High    Level   Committee           (HLC)      meeting    was     held   under   the    Chairmanship      of

 Institutions"     was     organized      by     BPR&D        at    CDTI,    Ghaziabad      from     02.06.2022      to

 Rai, Hon’ble MoS Home, inaugurated the training symposium and Shri Ajay Kumar

 discussed issues pertaining to mutual interest.

 under BADP.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, May 2022
pages:
Ministry of Home  Affairs-Major Achievements, _ significant
Development and important events for the month of May, 2022.

The National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting was held under the
chairmanship of union Home Secretary on 10.05.2022, to review preparedness for
Severe Cyclonic Storm "ASANI" over west central Bay of Bengal.

2: Annual Conference of Relief Commissioners/Secretaries, Department of
Disaster Management of States/UTs to review the status of preparedness for South-
West Monsoon, 2022 was held on 18" & 19" at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The
conference was inaugurated by Union Home Secretary.

3, On 05.05.2022, Union Home Secretary chaired a meeting with the Secretary,
MoRD to review the progress of construction of Roads/Bridges under Road

Construction Project for LWE affected areas.

4. On 11.05.2022, Union Home Secretary reviewed the availability of latest
technology i.e Multi Mode Passive Detection System (MMPDS) in the field of Truck
Scanner with Department of Atomic Energy, Central Board of Indirect Taxes &
Customs, Land Ports Authority of India and Central Reserve Police Force.

5, On 23.05.2022, a meeting was held under the Chairmanship of Home
Secretary to discuss the apportionment of pension liabilities between Bihar and
Jharkhand, with the Chief Secretaries and Principal Accountant Generals of both the

states.

6. Further, on 31.05.2022, Union Home Secretary hold a meeting to discuss the
issue of allocation of adequate funds to NE States under Compensatory Afforestation
Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA)/ other schemes of MoEF & CC to

improve forest cover in North Eastern Region (NER).

Ps Further, on. 12.05.2022, Secretary (Coord), MHA hold a_ meeting
with Ministry of Road. Transport & Highways to review the progress in issues related
to Central Motor Vehicles Registration (CMVR) being faced by CAPFs during

registration/procurement of vehicles.

8. A meeting was held on 24.05.2022 under the chairmanship of DG (Awards)
with the representatives of State of Gujarat and UT Administration of Dadra & Nagar
Haveli and Daman & Diu (DNH & DD) to discuss the issues of Transfer of land to DNH
& DD in lieu of land given to Gujarat at Simbor in 1989 & Transfer of 4 villages
(Meghval, Nagar, Raymal & Madhuban) from the State of Gujarat to Dadra & Nagar

Haveli and Daman & Diu.

9. On 26.05.2022, a meeting of Monitoring Committee was held under Additional
Secretary (North East), MHA to monitor and redress issues relating to racial

discrimination faced by the people of North East,
10. A four-member Indian Delegation, led by Mr. Kamal Kishore, Member and
Secretary (1/C), NDMA attended the 7th session of the Global Platform on Disaster
Risk Reduction, in Bali, Indonesia from 23-28 May 2022. Dr.P.K.Mishra, Principal
Secretary to Hon'ble Prime Minister delivered a key note address, through VC, during
the inaugural, plenary session of the World Reconstruction Forum.

11. A meeting under Additional Secretary (DM) was held on 17.05.22 to review the
preparedness measures to deal effectively with the crisis situation in Ropeway

projects.

12. On 13.05.2022, Additional Secretary (LWE) held a meeting with the Nodal
Officers from Bihar, Chhattisgarh and CRPF regarding review of FOBs/Camps under
Assistance to Central Agencies for LWE Management (ACALWEM) Scheme.

13. On 18.05.2022, AS(LWE) held a meeting with the officers of
MoRD regarding implementation of Roshni/Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen.
Kasuhalya Yojana. (DDUGKY) in LWE Affected areas.

14. One Advisory was issued to State Govemments/CAPFs to sensitize them to
counter the LWE activities in the LWE affected areas.

15. EFC meeting to appraise MHA's proposal regarding the Vibrant Village
Programme was held on 20.05.2022.

16. 2nd Negotiation Meeting was held on 9-10 May, 2022 in New Delhi with Italy to
finalize the MLAT in Criminal Matters. JS(CIC) led the Indian delegation, while the
Italian delegation was led by Mr. Stefano Opilio, Director General for International
Affairs and International Judiciary Cooperation, Italian Ministry of Justice. Agreed
Minutes have been signed between the Heads of Delegation on 10.05.2022.

17. An exercise was undertaken in CAPFs to rationalize the Forms/Registers used
in CAPFs. 1178 Forms/Registers have been reduced to 451 i.e. 118 common and 333
Force specific. Some of these forms have also been digitized and efforts are in hand
to digitize more number of forms/registers.

18. 212 posts were sanctioned for augmentation of CISF personnel at Numaligarh
(NRL) Assam.

19. Total 47 Goys of CAPFs (BSF-07, CRPF-07, RAF-22, ITBP-07 & SSB-04) as
direct induction have been ordered for deployment in various States of Punjab,
Chandigarh, Telangana & Uttar Pradesh for law and order duties for a specific
deployment period. Further, total 09 Coys of CAPFs (BSF-02, CRPF-03, SSB-02 &
CISF-02) as direct induction have been ordered to deploy in Kerala, Odisha
Uttaralchand for Bye-Election related duties.

20. Deployment period of 14 Coys of CAPFs (BSF-03, CRPF-06, SSB-02 & CISF-
03) have been extended during May, 2022 in various States of Delhi, Haryana &
Ladakh) for law and order duties.
21. The Registration (Tamil Nadu Amendment) Bill, 2021 and the Prohibition of
Child Marriage (Haryana Amendment) Bill, 2020 have been assented to by the
Hon'ble President of India on 07.05.2022 and 13.05.2022 respectively.

22. The Code of Criminal Procedure (Jharkhand Amendment) Bill, 2020 and The
Code of Criminal Procedure (Karnataka Amendment) Bill, 2021 have been assented
to by the Hon'ble President of India on 24.05.2022.

23. Instructions for promulgation of "The Right to Fair Compensation and
Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Tripura
Amendment) Ordinance, 2020” have been conveyed to the State Government on
18.05.2022.

24. During the month, more than 3725 kg of narcotic substance, 2710 of Tramadol
tablets and 39479 bottles of Codeine based cough syrup were seized and 44 persons
were arrested for their involvement in drug trafficking.

25. On 10.05.2022, sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet against 14
accused persons was accorded in accordance with section 45(1) of the Unlawful
Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.

26. Kannur (Kerala) Airport has been included in the list of authorized ICPs for
entry of persons holding e-Visa.

27. Provisioning sanction of Rs. 204.19 crore and Expenditure sanction of Rs.28.84
lakh have been accorded to CAPFs for procurement of vehicles, other equipments etc.

28. Guidelines of the scheme of Modernization Plan IV of CAPFs to be
implemented till 31.03.2026 with the total outlay of Rs. 1523 Crore has been issued on
25.05.2022,

29. Sanction for foreign visit has been accorded on 12.05.2022 for a delegation of
CRPF to witness onsite demonstration/trial of Multi Mode Passive Detection System
(MMPDS) at the premises of M/s Decision Sciences in California, USA from
17.05.2022 to 20.05.2022.

30. Following change of names were effected: (i) the name of Shri "Flargobincipur
City" as "Shri Hargobindpur Sahib" in Punjab; (ii) name of the village "Kachrewadi"
Tal-Tasgaon, District - Sangli as "Limbgaon" in Maharasthra; (iii) name of the village
"Melmuri" in Tirur Taluk in Malappuram District as "Kclampuzha" village; (iv) name of
"Nsunyu" village to "Kithagha" village in Tseminyu Sub-Division under Kohima District
Nagaland; and (v) name of village "Acharra" as "Acharya Dham" in Tikamgarh District,
Madhya Pradesh.

31. 12th Meeting of Standing Committee of the Southern Zonal Council held on
28.05.2022 in Thiruananthapuram, Kerala.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, April 2022
pages:
Ministry of Home _ Affairs-Major Achievements, — significant
Development and important events for the month of April, 2022.

Hon'ble Home Minister inaugurated the "48th All India Police Science
Congress (AIPSC)" at CAPT, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh on 22.04.2022. Chief Minister
of MP, MoS (AM), Mos(NP) and the Home Minister of MP participated. The following
publications viz. Police Vigyan and Data on Police Organization (DOPO) was released
during this occasion.

2: A delegation led by H.E. Mr. Eammon Gilmore, Special Representative for
Human Rights, European Union met with Union Home Secretary on 28.04.2022. The EU
delegation raised some concerns on human rights. India's commitment to Human Rights
and the extant mechanisms in our democratic set up to address the challenges related to
HRs were reiterated.

a. On 20.04.2022, Union Home Secretary held a meeting with the Chief Secretaries of
NE States to discuss various issues of Helicopter Services in NER.

4. MLAT in Criminal Matters has been signed with Poland on 25.04.2022 in New
Delhi. SS(IS), MHA was the signatory from the Indian side.

5: A meeting between Additional Secretary (CIC), MHA and Mr Andrew Kefford,
Australian Deputy Secretary, Department of Home Affairs was held on 05.04.2022. The
meeting provided an opportunity to explore areas of potential bilateral security cooperation.

6; Ceasefire agreements with NSCN (NK) and NSCN (R) of Nagaland have been
extended for a further period of one year till 27.04.2023. Ceasefire agreement with NSCN (K-
Khango) of Nagaland has also been extended for one year upto 17.04.2023.

ie Meetings of the Joint Monitoring Committee (JMC) were held on 06.04.2022 under
Additional Secretary (NE) with the Chief Secretaries of Tripura and Assam to review
implementation of Bru Rehabilitation Scheme and Bodo & Karbi Agreement and with
the Principal Secretary, Tripura to review implementation of Memorandum of
Settlement(MoS) signed with NLFT(SD).

8. A review meeting was held on 19.04.2022 under Additional Secretary (LWE) for
expediting installation of Mobile Towers under Phase II of the Mobile Connectivity
Project in LWE affected areas.

9, Two Advisories were issued to State Governments/CAPFs to sensitize them to counter
the LWE activities in the LWE affected areas.

10. The Indian Stamp (Telangana Amendment) Bill, 2020 has been assented to by the
Hon'ble President of India on 31.03.2022.

11. During the month sanction for prosecution for filing charge sheets against 54
accused persons was accorded in accordance with section 45(1) of the Unlawful Activities
(Prevention) Act, 1967 in respect of cases relating to hatching of conspiracy &
planning to undertake violent terrorist acts in Jammu & Kashmir and other anti-national
activities.

12. Sanction was issued vide order dated 07.4.2022 for the visit of Director General
Assam Rifles with delegation (03 staff officers) to Nepal, for Assam Rifles Ex-serviceman
Rally during the year 2022.
13. During the month, a total 65 Coys of CAPFs (RAF-40, CRPF-08, BSF-02, SSB-
06, ITBP-07 & CISF-02) as direct induction have been ordered for deployment in various
States of Bihar, Jharkhand, Ladakh, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Telangana, Delhi
and Uttar Pradesh for law and order duties for a specific deployment period. Further a
total 02 Coys of BSF as direct induction have been ordered to deploy in West Bengal for
Bye-Election related duties.

14. — During the month of April, 2022, 15,031 kg of Narcotics substance, 53,675 tablets and
19,075 ampoules have been seized and total 54 persons were arrested for their
involvement in drug trafficking.

15. All States/ UTs have launched their State Citizen Centric Portals for
providing Citizen Centric Police Services connected to CCTNS. More than 9 crore citizen
service requests have been handled.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, February 2022
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, — significant
Development and important events for the month of February, 2022.

4th India-UK Home Affairs Dialogue was held on 10th February, 2022 in
virtual mode. The Government of India delegation was led by Union Home Secretary and UK
delegation was led by Mr. Matthew Rycroft, Permanent Secretary, Home Office. The Dialogue
covered a wide range of issues including cyber security, extradition cases, migration,
etc. UK authorities were impressed upon for the need to expedite the process of extradition.

A Union Home Secretary held a meeting with the Ambassador of France on
18.02.2022. Issues of mutual concern were discussed.

3 A total of 708 Underground Cadres of United Gorkha People Organisation
(UGPO-169), Tiwa Liberation Army (TLA-77), Rabha National Liberation Front (RNLF-28),
Adivasi Dragon Fighter (ADF-61), United People's Revolutionary Front (UPRF-29), National
Liberation Front of Bengali (NLFB-303) and National Santhal Liberation Army (NSLA-41)
surrendered at Guwahati (Assam) along with huge quantity of arms and ammunition.

4. A PCC meeting was held on 22.02.2022 through VC under the Chairmanship
of Additional Secretary (LWE) to review the progress of implementation and
submission of claims under Special Infrastructure Scheme .(SIS) including construction
of 250 Fortified Police Stations (FPS) with CCA(Home) and Nodal Officers of LWE

affected States.

5, A VC meeting was held on 10.02.2022 under AS (LWE) regarding Joint Task
Force Camp at Pusuguppa under Assistance to Central Agencies for LWE
Management (ACALWEM) Scheme with CRPF & Telangana Police.

6. A meeting of the Empowered Committee was held on 23.02.2022 under
AS(LWE) to review the progress of Important schemes in LWE affected areas with
DG(Media)-MHA, AD(IB)-MHA, DDG(Sales)-Prasar Bharati, DDG(Ops)-Prasar Bharati,
DDG(Planning)-AIR and AD(Policy)-AlR.

7. Rs.2,00,00,000/- was released to Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) under
Assistance to Central Agencies for LWE Management (ACALWEM) Scheme.
Rs.12,34,78,241/- released to Government of Bihar as reimbursement of claims under
Special Infrastructure Scheme (SIS) including construction of 250 Fortified Police Station

(FPS).

8. During the month of February, 2022 sanction for prosecution for filing the
charge sheet against 03 accused persons was accorded in accordance with section 45(1)
of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.

9. On 17.02.2022, a meeting of Dispute Resolution Sub-Committee was held
under Joint Secretarys (CS) with the representatives of Andhra Pradesh and
Telangana to carry out the preparatory work and recommend practical ways to
resolve the bilateral issues arising out of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganization Act,

2014.
10. Rs.26.56 crore has been sanctioned for acquisition of land measuring 70
acres for establishment of Bn HQrs at Barma under Frontier HQ SSB, Guwahati.

11. 21 Coys of CAPFs as direct induction have been ordered for deployment in
various States viz. Bihar, Karnataka, Chandigarh, Telangana and Gujarat for law and
order duties for a specific deployment period. Further a total 470 Coys of CAPFs
(CRPF-78, BSF-84, SSB-73, ITBP-64, SAPs-137 & CISF-34) as direct induction
have been ordered to deploy in various States for election related duties during
Assembly Election 2022 in 3 States of Manipur, Punjab & Uttar Pradesh.

12. During the month, various provisioning/authorization sanctions have been
accorded to CAPFs for procurement of equipment/BR Jackets etc. which inter-alia
includes the following:

(i) Procurement of 878 Nos. Hand Held Thermal Images (HHTIs) to
various border guarding battalions of BSF & Kartarpur Corridor Project
for an estimated financial implication of Rs.73,28,92,846/-;

(ii) | Procurement of 250 KVA diesel Generator set for 100 bedded Covid Care
Center at Group Center, CRPF for total cost of Rs. 18,12,999/-;

(iii) Procurement of 3180 Nos. BR Jackets and BR Helmets on augmentation
of CISF strength at Delhi Metro, GBS and SSG Bn. for an estimated
financial implication of Rs. 16,51,81,920/;

13. The meeting of Standing Committee on GeM (SCoGeM) of MHA was held
under AS&FA with all CAPFs, CPOs and other organizations of MHA on 16.02.2022 to
review the status of procurement of stores/services through GeM.

14. During the month, total 33959 Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) cards were
issued. 1207 OCI cards were issued in lieu of PIO cards and 381 OCI cards issued in
spouse based cases.

15. During the month, 212 Long Term Visa (LTV) applications from Pak nationals
have been granted by this Ministry.

16. 6 Pakistani fishermen have been repatriated to Pakistan from India in the
month of February, 2022.

17. During the month, FCRA registrations of 3 associations were suspended.

18. The Registration (Assam Amendment) Bill, 2021 and The Odisha Maritime Board
Bill, 2020 have been assented to by the Hon'ble President of India on 15.02.2022
and 18.02.2022 respectively.

pages:
Ministry of   Home     Affairs-Major    Achievements,   significant
Development and important events for the month of January, 2022.

      President of India has approved conferment of Padma Awards on the occasion of
Republic Day, 2022. The list comprises 4 Padma Vibhushan, 17 Padma Bhushan and 107
Padma Shri Awards
2.      Gallantry Medals and Service Medals were awarded to the State/Union
Territories/CAPF Officers/Personnel on the occasion of Republic Day, 2022.
3.     The President of India has also approved the conferment of Jeevan Raksha Padak
Series of Awards, 2021. The list includes 6 Sarvottam Jeevan Raksha Padak, 16 Uttam
Jeevan Raksha Padak and 29 Jeevan Raksha Padak.
 4.    One advisory has been issued to all the States/UTs to ensure strict compliance of
the provisions of Flag Code of India, 2002 and the Prevention of Insults to the National
Honour Act, 1971. Further, advisory was issued to all States and UTs for observance of
Martyrs Day in memory of those who sacrificed their lives during the struggle for India's
Freedom.

 5.     A Senior Officers Meeting (SoM) under Homeland Security Dialogue
between India and USA was held on 12th January, 2022 in virtual mode. USA delegation was
led by Mr. Robert Silvers, Under Secretary, Department of Homeland Security, USA, while
the Indian delegation was led by Union Home Secretary. Both sides reviewed the ongoing
cooperation and identified further steps that can be taken to explore opportunities and
synergies in advancing cooperation in counter-terrorism, cyber security, securing critical
infrastructure and global supply chains, maritime security, aviation security, customs
enforcement and trade security, among other issues.

6.   Union Home Secretary also had a Meeting with the Australian High
Commissioner on 28th January, 2022 to discuss the ongoing security cooperation.
 7.    14th meeting of the Standing Committee of the Central Zonal Council was held on
17.01.2022 in Bhopal and 12 th meeting of the Standing Committee of the Western
Zone Council was held on 28.01.2022 in Goa.
8.     On 06.01.2022, Union Home Secretary reviewed the implementation of Bru
Agreement, 2020 and NLFT(SD) Agreement, 2019 with Chief Secretary of Tripura. Union
Home Secretary also held a VC meeting on 12.01.2022 with the Chief Secretaries of Andhra
Pradesh and Telangana to discuss the pending bilateral issues.

9.    A total of Rs.13,41,000/- released to Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) for
organizing Special Project in interior areas under Civic Action Programme (CAP) in LWE
Affected areas 2021-22. Rs.140 crore released to Chhattisgarh and Rs. 20 crore to
Telangana State under Special Central Assistance (SCA) Scheme.
10.      On 10.01.2022, sanctioned an amount of Rs. 0.94 crore for allotment of land 2.97
acres belonging to Jaipur Development Authority (JDA) for construction of Separated
Family Accommodation (SFA) of SSB at Jaipur (Rajasthan).

11.     Total 17 Coys of CAPFs (RAF-04, CRPF-10 86 ITBP-03) have been
ordered for deployment in various States (i.e. Arunachal Pradesh, Gujarat, Telangana &
Delhi) for law and order duties.
12.   Further, 1555 Coys of CAPFs (CRPF-284, BSF-312, SSB-177, ITBP-141,
CISF-172, RPF-70 & SAPs-399) have been ordered for deployment in various
States for election related duties during Assembly Election-2022 in 5 States of Goa,
Manipur, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh & Uttarakhand.

13.   Deployment period of 61 Coys of CAPFs (RAF-05, CRPF-13, BSF-11,
SSB-11, ITBP-06 & CISF-15) have been extended during January 2022 for Delhi,
Haryana 85 CBI-West Bengal for law and order duties in the State/agency.
14.     One advisory has been issued to all State Governments/UTs
on Treatment and Care of Transgender Persons in Prisons to sensitize all prison officials
and take appropriate action for protection of rights of transgender prisoners and their
welfare.
15.    During the month of January 2022, sanction for prosecution for filing
charge sheets against 24 accused persons was accorded in accordance with section 45(1)
of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.
16.    During the month of January, 2022 total 30,607 Overseas Citizens of
India (OCI) cards were issued. 1,307 OCI cards were issued in lieu of PIO Cards.
17.     117 LTV (Long Term Visa) applications from Pak nationals have been
granted by this Ministry in the month of January, 2022. Further, 13 Citizenship
Certificates (CC) have been granted to eligible applicants.
18.   20 Indian fishermen have been repatriated to India from Pakistan in
the month of January, 2022.
19.    On 27.01.2022, orders under section 10(2) (1) of the Disaster
Management Act, 2005, were issued conveying that the MHA order dated 27.12
2021 to ensure compliance to the Normative Framework for taking evidence based
Covid-19 containment measures at district/local level as conveyed vide MoHFW
advisory dated 21st December 2021, will remain in force until 28.02.2022. Thereafter,
Home Secretary had written letter to all Chief Secretaries and Administrators of
States/UTs to ensure prompt and effective management of Covid-19, strict compliance with
the various advisories issued by the MoHFW on the new VOC and strict enforcement
of the COVID Appropriate Behaviour.

           केंद्रीय गृह सचिव ने तटीय सुरक्षा की समीक्ष करने के चिए तटीय राजययों/सोंघ राजय
क्षेत्यों सचहत सभी सोंबोंचित चहतिारकयों के साथ चिनाों क 20.12.2021 कय वीचियय

के माध्यम से बै ठ क आययचित की गई।

अोंतगात झारखोंि, चबहार एवों ओचिशा राजययों कय 220 करयड़ रु. की राचश िारी की गई।

10. कािना (नयगिी), रामपु र (एिपी) मे आईटीबीपी की 43वीों बटाचियन के चिए क्वाटा र
मास्टर भोंिार, क्वाटा र गािा , प्रशासचनक खोंि, रािपचत्त अचिकारी मेस आचि सचहत गैर
आवासीय भवनयों के चनमाा र् और स्थि चवकास तथा ब्क सेवाओों से सोंबोंचित काया के चिए
56,75,47,999/- रु. के चिए प्रशासचनक अनु मयिन और व्यय स्वीकृ चत चिनाों क
15.12.2021 कय प्रिान की गई है ।

11. गृह मोंत्ािय ने चिनाों क 27.12.2021 के आिे श के तहत नियिी, चििा- फरीिाबाि
में एसएसबी के ररिवा बटाचियन मुख्यािय की स्थापना के चिए 66.50 करयड़ रु. की िागत
से 70 एकड़ ग्राम पोंिायत भूचम के अोंतरर्/आवोंटन कय मोंिूरी प्रिान की है ।

12. चनिाा ररत तै नाती अवचि के चिए कानून एवों व्यवस्था ड्यूचटययों हे तु चवचभन्‍फन राजययों
(अथाा त िोंिीगढ़, उत्तर प्रिे श, तेिोंगाना और झारखोंि) में तै नाती के चिए सीिी भती
(इों िक्शन) के रूप में सीएपीएफ की कुि 47 कोंपचनययों (आरएएफ-23, सीआरपीएफ-07,
बीएसएफ-03, एसएसबी-07 एवों आईटीबीपी-07) कय आिे श चिए गए हैं ।

समीक्षा करने के चिए सोंयुक्त सचिव (पीएम) की अध्यक्षता में चिनाों क 07.12.2021 कय
आईिी (आरएएफ), सीआरपीएफ और चनिे शक, सीएसआईआर-सीएमईआरआई) के साथ
वीचियय कॉन्‍फरेंचसोंग के माध्यम से बैठक आययचित की गई।

14. बीपीआर एों ि िी और अक्तखि भारतीय तकनीकी चशक्षा सचमचत (एआईसीटीई) ने
साइबर सुरक्षा से सोंबोंचित मुद्यों के बारे में चिनाों क 08.12.2021कय है काथन मों थन-2021
का फाइनि सों युक्त रूप से आययचित चकया। है काथन के िौरान कुि 2203 सु झाव
प्राप्त हुए और 115 टीमयों ने फाइनि प्रचतययचगता में भाग चिया।

15. इस माह के िौरान, पाों ि सीिीटीआई और सीएपीटी भयपाि ने कुि 43 ऑनिाइन
पाठ्यक्रम सोंिाचित चकए चिनमें 1309 काचमाकयों कय प्रचशचक्षत चकया गया।

16. वामपोंथी उग्रवाि से प्रभाचवत क्षेत्यों में वामपोंथी उग्रवाि की गचतचवचिययों का मुकाबिा

17. चवचिचवरुद्ध चक्रयाकिाप (चनवारर्) अचिचनयम, 1967 की िारा 45(1) के अनुसार,
54 अचभयुक्तयों के चवरुद्ध आरयप पत् िाक्तखि करने के चिए अचभययिन की स्वीकृचत प्रिान
की गई।

18. चिनाों क 27.12.2021 कय, आपिा प्रबों िन अचिचनयम, 2005 की िारा 10(2) के
अों तगा त आिे श िारी करके राजय/सों घ राजय क्षे त् सरकारयों और राजय/सों घ राजय क्षे त्
प्राचिकरर्यों कय चनिे श चिया गया चक वे िे श के चवचभन्‍फन भागयों में वै ररएों ट ऑफ कन्‍फसना
(वीओसी) का बड़ी सों ख्या में पता िगने कय ध्यान में रखते हुए, चिनाों क 21 चिसों बर, 2021
कय स्वास््य एवों पररवार क्यार् मों त्ािय द्वारा यथा सों सूचित, चििा/स्थानीय स्तर पर
साक्ष्य आिाररत रयकथाम उपाय करने के चिए नॉमे चटव रेमवका के कायाा न्‍फवयन पर चविार
करें । यह आिे श चिनाों क 31.01.2022 तक िागू रहे गा। उसके बाि, राजययों/सोंघ राजय क्षे त्यों
के मुख्य सचिवयों और प्रशासकयों कय कयचवि-19 के त्वररत और प्रभावकारी प्रबोंिन के चिए
आवश्यक उपाय करने हे तु अिाशासकीय पत् िारी चकया गया चिसमें उनसे कहा गया चक
नए वीओसी के बारे में स्वास््य एवों पररवार क्यार् मोंत्ािय द्वारा िारी चवचभन्‍फन एिवाइिरी
और कयचवि अनुकूि व्यवहार का सख्ती से अनुपािन सु चनक्तश्ित चकया िाए।

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, April and May 2021
pages:
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

MONTHLY SUMMARY FOR THE CABINET FOR THE MONTH OF APRIL
AND MAY, 2021.

PART-I                                                       UNCLASSIFIED

     Hon‘ble Home Minister chaired a meeting with Chief Ministers of
Gujarat, Maharashtra and Administrator of Daman & Diu and Dadra Nagar
Haveli on 16th May, 2021 and reviewed the preparedness of States/ UT
and Central Ministries/Departments regarding Cyclonic           Storm
"TAUKTAE".
2.    Subsequent to the announcement made by Hon‘ble PM after his aerial
survey and visit to Gujarat on 19.5.2021, Central Government released an
amount of Rs. 1000 crores to the State Government of Gujarat on
20.5.2021.

3.     On 20.5.2021, Union Home Secretary wrote to four States and two UTs
on the eastern coast, which were likely to be affected by the cyclone "Yaas"
for taking additional precautionary measures in coastal districts with regard
to adequate power backup for hospitals, labs, vaccine cold chain and
other medical facilities.
4.     After visiting Cyclone affected areas of West Bengal and Odisha on
28.5.2021, Hon'ble Prime Minister announced a financial assistance of Rs.
1000 crore to Odisha, West Bengal and Jharkhand for immediate relief
activities. Accordingly, financial assistance from NDRF of Rs.500 crore to
Odisha, Rs. 300 crore to West Bengal and Rs.200 crore to Jharkhand
was released on 29.5.2021.

5.    Situation arising due to Cyclone Storms "Tauktae" & "YAAS" was
monitored 24x7 by the Central Government at the highest level and MHA
mobilized resources like NDRF, Indian Army, Indian Air Force, Indian
Navy and Indian Coast Guard to assist States/UTs in rescue and relief
operations.
6.    On 21st May, 2021, Annual Conference of Relief Commissioner/
Secretaries, Department of Disaster Management of States/ UTs to
review the status of preparedness for South- West Monsoon, 2021 was
held through video conference.
7.   Hon’ble Home Minister chaired a review meeting on 24.05.2021 with
the Chief Ministers of Odisha, West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh and Lt.
Governor of the A&N Islands, to assess the preparedness of States/ UT
and Central Ministries/Departments for dealing with the cyclone as well for
ensuring uninterrupted supply of Medical Oxygen.

8.    To deal with the resurgence of Covid-19 across the country, MHA
took various measures/actions to review/mitigate the situation:
     (i)   On 6th April, 2021, Union Home Secretary reviewed the
     management of COVID-19 situation in NCT of Delhi and UT of
     Chandigarh. Thereafter, on 9th April, 2021, I further reviewed the
     requirement of DRDO Hospital in NCT of Delhi in view of the surge
     in COVID-19 cases.
     (ii)  On 7th and 25th April and again on 21 st May, 2021, Union
     Home Secretary held meetings with the Empowered Group- 6 to
     review the Strategic issues related to management of Covid-19 and
     issues relating to management of supply chain and price rise.
     (iii)32 Composite Hospitals including Referral Hospital s of
     CAPFs, NSG & ARs comprising of 1890 beds have been geared
     up again to combat and address the issue of resurgence of
     Covid-19 cases of CAPFs.

     (iv)   On 15.04.2021, letter issued to States/UTs regarding
     utilizing upto 50% of actual allocation of SDRF for the current year,
     for containment measures of COVID-19 in conformity to approved
     items 86 norms.
     (v)  On 16.04.2021, letter issued to States/UTs regarding
     ensuring no restriction is imposed on movement of Medical
     oxygen.
     (vi) On 18.04.2021, DO letter was issued to States/UTs
     regarding taking necessary measures to prohibit supply of
     oxygen for industrial purposes.
     (vii)A meeting under Additional Secretary (UT), was held on
     19th April, 2021 to coordinate functioning of SVBP Covid
     Hospital (DRDO), Delhi Cantt.
     (viii) On 22.04.2021, order issued regarding taking measures for
     ensuring uninterrupted supply of oxygen. Further on the same day,
     DO letter issued to States/UTs regarding seamless supply and
     transport of Remdesivir.
     (ix) On 23.04.2021, DO letters issued to States/ UTs advising that
     Oxygen allocation to various districts/cities needs to be rationalized
     and also to provide security to oxygen transporting vehicles and to
     make provisions for exclusive corridors for transpiration and
     treating these vehicles like ambulances.

     (x)   On 25.04.2021, order was issued regarding stopping the
     supplies of oxygen for non-medical purpose.
     (xi) A meeting on 28th April, 2021 to review the augmentation of
     beds in DRDO Hospital and Setting up of two hospitals, one each in
     Jammu and Srinagar was held.
     (xii) On 29th April, 2021 Central Government released an
     assistance of Rs. 8873.60 crore, in advance from State Disaster
     Response Fund (SDRF) to all the 28 States Governments.
    (xiii). The meeting of the National Executive Committee (NEC) was
    held on 3 rd May, 2021 to review the current COVID-19 situation in
    the country and for ratification of Orders issued by MHA, since last
    meeting, for containment of Covid situation in the country.

    (xiv)  An order was issued on 29th May, 2021 to re-constitute 6
    Empowered Groups, into 10 Empowered Groups for decisively and
    effectively addressing evolving challenges from COVID-19.
    (xv)    MHA issued order on 27.05.2021 regarding extension of
    containment measures upto 30.06.2021. Thereafter, DO was issued
    to all Administrators and Chief Secretaries to ensure its compliance.
9.    On 9th April, 2021, Union Home Secretary presided over a Seminar
on preparing a Roadmap for next decade for Central and State Police
forces.

10. On 07/04/2021 authorization of 10 HHTIs with DVRs for security
of Kartarpur Sahib Corridor Project has been accorded at the estimated
cost of Rs. 1,37,43,504/-.
11.      On 15/04/2021 sanction for establishing a COVID -19
investigation laboratory in 200 bedded Referral Hospital ITBP Greater
Noida has been accorded at the total cost of Rs. 34,56,000/-.
12. On 19th April 2021, approval accorded to establish an electronic
'National Register for Working Dogs' (NRWD) under the aegis of Police K9
Cell of this Ministry to exclusively maintain records of working dogs

दलए दिनां क 11.05.2021 को अनुमोिन प्रिान दकया गया।

16. केंद्रीय गृह सदचव ने दिनां क 19.05.2021 को, िू रसं चार दवभाग, नई दिल्ली के
प्रदतदनदध के साथ वीदियो कॉन्‍फरें स के माध्यम से वामपं थी उग्रवाि से प्रभादवत राज्यों में
मोबाइल कनेस्िदवटी पररयोजना की प्रगदत की समीक्षा की।
17. अपर सदचव, एलिब्‍ल्यू ई ने वामपं थी उग्रवाि प्रबंधन योजना के दलए केंद्रीय
एजेंदसयों हे तु सहायता के अं तगा त दवदभन्‍फन पररयोजनाओं की प्रगदत की समीक्षा करने के
दलए तथा दसदवक कारा वाई काया क्रम के अं तगा त वषा 2020-21 में जारी की गई दनदध के
दलए उपयोग प्रमाण पत्रों की स्थथदत की समीक्षा करने के दलए दिनां क 12.4.2021 और
27.05.2021 को वीदियो कॉन्‍फरें स के माध्यम से बै ठ क की अध्यक्षता की।

18. वामपं थी उग्रवाि प्रबंधन योजना के दलए केंद्रीय एजेंदसयों हे तु सहायता के अं तगा त
सीआरपीएफ को कुल 13,76,30,102/- रुपए की रादश जारी की गई।

19 वामपं थी उग्रवाि प्रबं ध न योजना के दलए कें द्रीय एजें दसयों हे तु सहायता के
अं तगा त वामपं थी उग्रवाि-रोधी ऑपरे शनों के दलए उपलब्‍ध कराई गई एयर दलफ्ट की
सु दवधा की मि के दलए भारतीय वायु से ना को 9,04,10,417/- रुपए की रादश जारी की
गई।

20. वामपं थी उग्रवाि से प्रभादवत क्षे त्रों में वामपं थी उग्रवाि गदतदवदधयों का सामना करने
के दलए राज्य सरकारों/केंद्रीय सशथत्र पु दलस बलों को इस बारे में जानकारी प्रिान करने
के दलए उन्‍फहें एिवाइजरी जारी की गई है ।

21. अप्रै ल, 2021 में दवदधदवरुि दक्रयाकलाप (दनवारण) अदधदनयम, 1967 की धारा 45(1)
के अनुसार, 67 अदभयु क्तों के दवरुि आरोप-पत्र िास्खल करने हे तु अदभयोजन की थवीकृदत
प्रिान की गई।
22. मई, 2021 में दवदधदवरुि दक्रयाकलाप (दनवारण) अदधदनयम, 1967 की धारा 45(1) के
अनुसार, 10 अदभयु क्तों के दवरुि आरोप-पत्र िास्खल करने हे तु अदभयोजन की थवीकृदत
प्रिान की गई।
23. नागालैंि के एनएससीएन (एनके) और एनएससीएन (आर) के साथ सं घषा दवराम
सं बंधी करारों को दिनां क 28.04.2021 से एक और वषा की अवदध के दलए अथाा त् दिनां क
27.04.2022 तक के दलए बढ़ा दिया गया है । नागालैं ि के एएससीएन (के -खां गो) के साथ
सं घषा दवराम सं बंधी करार को दिनां क 18.04.2021 से एक वषा की अवदध के दलए अथाा त
दिनां क 17.04.2022 तक के दलए बढ़ाया गया है ।

24. अरुणाचल प्रिे श में दतरप, चां गलां ग और लोंगदिं ग दजलों तथा असम राज्य की
सीमा से लगे अरुणाचल प्रिे श के अन्‍फय दजलों में चार पु दलस थानों के अदधकार क्षे त्र में आने
वाले क्षे त्रों को दिनां क 01.04.2021 की अदधसू चना सं ख्या SO. 1440(E) के तहत दिनां क
01.04.2021 से 30.09.2021 तक छह माह की अवदध के दलए सशथत्र बल दवशे ष
शस्क्तयां अदधदनयम, 1958 के अं तगा त 'अशां त क्षे त्र' घोदषत दकया गया।
25. अप्रै ल, 2021 के िौरान, 2095 दकलोग्राम से अदधक थवापक पिाथों को जब्‍त दकया
गया है और िर ग टर ै दफदकंग में सं दलप्त रहने के कारण कुल 49 व्यस्क्तयों को दगरफ्तार दकया
गया।

26. मई, 2021 के िौरान, 44,060 दकलोग्राम से अदधक थवापक पिाथा और
1350 कोिीन आधाररत कफ दसरप जब्‍त दकए गए हैं और 23 व्यस्क्तयों को िर ग
टर ै दफदकं ग में उनकी सं दलप्तता के दलए दगरफ्तार दकया गया है ।

27. इन महीनों के िौरान, केंद्रीय सशथत्र पु दलस बलों की कुल 127 कंपदनयों
(सीआरपीएफ-46, बीएसएफ-26, एसएसबी-20, आईटीबीपी-16, सीआईएसएफ-15
और आरएएफ-4) को दवदशष्‍ट तै नाती अवदध के दलए, कानू न एवं व्यवथथा सं बंधी
ड्यू दटयों हे तु दवदभन्‍फन राज्यों (दिल्ली, ते लंगाना, उत्तर प्रिे श और जम्मू एवं कश्मीर) में
तै नाती हे तु आिे श दिया गया है ।

28. गृ ह मं त्रालय ने दिनां क 13.04.2021 से 11.06.2021 तक दनधाा ररत भारतीय
केंद्रीय सशथत्र पु दलस बल माउं ट एवरे थट एवं माउं ट होत्से एक्सदपिीशन 2021 में भाग
ले ने के दलए 38 एक्सदपिीशन टीम सिथयों के सं बंध में ने पाल के िे प्यू टेशन िौरे के दलए
दिनां क 10 मई, 2021 के पत्र के तहत थवीकृदत प्रिान कर िी है ।

29. असम राइफल्स की दकफायर बटादलयन हे तु फेलुंगरे में महत्वपू णा लोकेशन प्लान्‍फस
(केएलपी) की थथापना हे तु दिनां क 25.05.2021 को थवीकृदत आिे श जारी दकया गया ।

30. सभी राज्यों/सं घ राज्य क्षे त्रों ने दवदभन्‍फन पु दलस से वाओं के दलए अपने -अपने राज्य
नागररक से वा पोटा ल आरं भ दकए हैं तथा 6.30 क्रेट से वा सं बंधी अनुरोधों को पू रा दकया
गया है । पररयोजना के कुल 2000 करोड़ रु. के पररव्यय में से अभी तक राज्यों/सं घ
राज्य क्षे त्रों और केंद्रीय एजेंदसयों को 1877.42 करोड़ रु. की रादश जारी की गई है ।

31. पू रे िे श के 16191 पु दलस थानों में से 16189 पु दलस थानों अथाा त 99.97% पु दलस
थानों में सीसीटीएनएस सॉफ्टवे य र लगा दिया गया है । लगभग 16050 पु दलस थानों में
शत प्रदतशत प्राथदमदकयां सीसीटीएनएस के माध्यम से िजा की जा रही हैं अथाा त
सीसीटीएनएस पररयोजना के अं त गा त कवर दकए गए 15697 पु दलस थानों अथाा त्
96.94% पु दलस थानों में 99.12% कने स्िदवटी उपलब्‍ध है ।


                                            ****

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, March 2021
pages:
Ministry of   Home     Affairs-Major    Achievements,    significant
Development and important events for the month of March,2021.

        A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), was signed on 27 th March,
2021 between the Government of India and the Government of Bangladesh on
cooperation in the field of Disaster Management, Resilience and Mitigation during the
visit of the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India to Bangladesh.
2.    High-Level Committee (HLC), under the Chairmanship of Hon'ble
Home Minister, on 30.03.2021 approved the proposal to establish an Integrated
Control Room of Emergency Response (ICR-ER) in MHA, and Extension of
Emergency Response Support System (ERSS), for funding from the Preparedness
and Capacity Building Window of National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF).
3.     On 31.03.2021, Hon'ble Home Minister approved the Central
Assistance of Rs. 1021.22 crore to the States of Andhra Pradesh, Himachal
Pradesh,Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu for flood/landslides/cloudburst and
cyclonic storm Nivar during 2020-21.
4.    Meeting of the Consultative Committee for the M/o Home Affairs on
Peace efforts in North Eastern region was held on 12.03.2021 under the Chairmanship
of Hon'ble HM at Parliament House Annexe, New Delhi.

5.      A meeting between delegation from United Kingdom led by Lord Tariq
A h m a d o f W i m b le d o n , M i n is t e r o f S t a t e f o r S o u t h A s ia a n d t h e
Commonwealth and Government of India delegation led by Shri G.K. Reddy, Minister of
State for Home Affairs was held in New Delhi on 15.03.2021.

6.     On 19.03.2021, Union Home Secretary wrote to all Chief Secretaries and
Administrators of States/UTs for creating _awareness among the people to follow
COVID appropriate behavior and simultaneously take necessary action for its strict
enforcement. A meeting on 20.03.2021 was also held to review COVID-19
situation in NCT of Delhi and UT of Chandigarh.
7.    Meetings were held on 09.03.2021 under AS(LWE) to review the
progress of the implementation of Identified Individual Oriented Beneficiary Schemes in
Saturation Mode in LWE affected districts/blocks.

8.   A Letter of Authority was issued on 18.03.2021 for releasing an amount of
Rs.1,30,99,239 in favor of Prasar Bharti (Doordarshan) for telecasting of 3
Documentary films in Hindi with regional languages in the 7 LWE Affected States
under Media Plan Scheme in LWE affected areas 2020-21.

9.    Sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet against 55 accused persons
was accorded in accordance with section 45(1) of Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act,
1967.
10.    6 Coys of RAF were deployed in Telangana, Daman & Diu and Uttar Pradesh
for Law and Order duties. 1405 Coys of CAPFs have been provided for Law & Order
duties during Assembly Election-2021 in 5 States of Assam, Puducherry, Tamil Nadu,
West Bengal and Kerala.

11.   During the month, more than 4491 kg of narcotics substances have been
seized and total 83 persons were arrested for their involvement in drug trafficking.

12.   The name of Railway Station "Miyon Ka Bara" has been changed as "Mahesh
Nagar" on Barmer-Jodhpur Broad Gauge line in Jodhpur Division, Rajasthan.

13.   MHA vide order dated 23.03.2021, issued guidelines for effective control of
COVID-19, which will be valid from 01.04.2021 to 30.04.2021. Thereafter, Union
Home Secretary wrote to all Chief Secretaries and Administrators of States/ UTs to
ensure compliance of the guidelines for effective control of COVID-19.


                                        ****

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, January,2021
pages:
M inistry of   Home      A ffairs-M ajor   Achievem ents,    sign ifican t
Developm ent and im portant events fo r the m onth o f January,2021.

      Hon’ ble President of India has approved conferment of 119 Padma
Awards on the occasion of Republic Day -2021. The list comprises 7 Padma
Vibhushan, 10 Padma Bhushan and 102 Padma Shri Awards.

2.    Union Home Minister launched the Ayushman CAPF’ scheme on 23.01.2021
at Guwahati, Assam.

3.     The inaugural issue of "National Police K-9 Journal" has been released by
Hon'ble Union Home Minister on 02.01.2021. It is a biannual journal which will be
released in April and October every year.

4.     Union Home Secretary had a meeting with Mr Matthew John Rycroft, Permanent
Secretary, Home Office of the UK on 15th January, 2021 through VC. Issues of mutual
interest including anti-India activities of UK based pro-Khalistani extremist organizations
and safety of the Indian High Commission in London were discussed.

5.      Union Home Secretary chaired the 49th meeting of High Level Empowered
Committee held on 18thJanuary,2021 at North Block, New Delhi for border
infrastructure projects.

6.     President's Police Medal for G allantry, Police Medal for Gallantry,
President's Police Medal for Distinguished Service, Police Medal for Meritorious Service,
Correctional Service Medals on prison personnel etc., were awarded to the State/Union
Territories/CAPF Officers/Personnei on the occasion of Republic Day - 2021.

7.       Union Home       M inister's Trophy    for   Best   Police   Training
Institutions in India were awarded for the years 2016-17, 2017-18, 2018-19 and
2019-20. Union Home Minister's Medal for Excellence in Police training for the
year 2020 has been awarded to 277 State Police/CAPE/CPO police personnel.

8.     During the       month,     sanctions for prosecution          for filing     the
charge sheet against 50 accused persons were accorded in accordance with
section 45(1) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 and section 188 of CrPC.

9.     Advisory dated 12.01.2021 was issued for strict compliance of the provisions of
Flag Code of India, 2002 and the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971
and for not using the National Flag made of plastic.

10.   Advisory on Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 and the
Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Rules, 2020 was issued on 21.01.2021 to all
States & UTs to initiate necessary measures in term s of the Act and undertake
sensitization programmes for the police and prison officials.

11.   One Advisory was issued to the State Government/CAPFs to sensitize them to
counter the LWE activities in the LWE affected areas.
12. A       m eeting     was       held     by     A d d itio n a l S ecretary (Police
Modernization) with the Controlling Authorities of States/UTs (under PSAR Act, 2005) on
4.1.2021 on enforcement of the Act.

13.     CCTNS software has been deployed at 15,773 out of 16,156 Police Stations
across the country, i.e. 98%. Around 15,568 Police Stations are entering 100%
FIRs through CCTNS, i.e. 96%. Connectivity is available at 15,645 Police Stations
i.e. 97%. CCTNS National Data Centre is getting data from 36 States/UTs. Data
digitization of 3.90 crore records have been completed, i.e. 91% of the total target.

14.    On behalf of all CAPFs, a MoU has been signed by ITBP with KVIC to procure
Cotton Durries (initial demand of 1,71,520 Nos. for all CAPFs worth Rs.8.7 Cr.) on
06.01.2021.

15. Target fixation meeting with OFB and all CAPFs, CPOs, SPOs and UTPs was
organized on 22.01.2021 to finalize targets for supply of arms & ammunitions and
explosives from OFB for next financial year i.e. 2021-22. This is a major step in the
direction of procuring arms & ammunitions etc. from an indigenous source.

16.   Standing Committee on GeM (SCoGeM) meeting under Chairmanship of
AS&FA(F1) was organized on 20/01/2021 with IsG level officers of all CAPFs/CPOs. All
organizations were advised to procure all items (except sensitive) on GeM Portal
through the new functionality "Custom Bid" enabled by GeM.

17.    Agreement between NCRB and PwC was signed on 12th January, 2021
for development of course content for NCTC (National Cybercrime Training Centre). The
kick-off meeting was held on 18th January, 2021.

18. An order extending the validity of guidelines fo r COVID-19 surveillance,
containment and caution up to 28.02.2021 was issued on 27.01.2021. Thereafter, on the
same day, I wrote to all Chief Secretaries and Administrators of States/UTs to ensure
strict compliance of the COVID-19 guidelines.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, December2020
pages:
1967204/2021/CIC-C(I)

        Ministry of   Home     Affairs-Major    Achievements,   significant
        Development and important events for the month of December, 2020.


              On 10.12.2020 Union Home Secretary chaired a meeting on the preparation
       of Database for COVID-19 Vaccination for the Front Line Workers (FLWs) of the
       States i.e, Police personnel, Home Guards, Civil Defence volunteers, Prison
       staff and Disaster Management personnel. Subsequently, on 21.12.2020,
       Additional Secretary (UT) held a similar meeting in respect of the UTs. Detailed
       strategy in this regard was finalized.

       2.     On 14.12.2020, Union Home Secretary chaired meeting to discuss the
       funding requirement of SVBP Covid Hospital, Delhi Cantt. Secretary, DRDO was
       present in the meeting and the funding strategy for the hospital was deliberated at
       length.

       3.      On 23.12.2020, CCS approved the proposal for "Development of critical
       infrastructure in State of Arunachal Pradesh" which includes construction of 18
       foot tracks measuring 598.27 Km at an estimated cost of Rs.1162.19 Cr.

       4.    An order extending the validity of guidelines for Covid-19 surveillance,
       containm ent and caution up to 31.12.2021 was issued on 28.12.2020.
       Thereafter, on the same day, I wrote to all the Chief Secretaries and
       Administrators of States/ UTs to ensure compliance of the Covid -19 guidelines.

       5.    A training session through Video Conference was organized on
       29.12.2020 for the Nodal Officers (L-2 & L-3) of States/UTs regarding
       preparation of database of FLWS and was uploaded on Co-Win Portal.

       6.    During the month of December, 2020, Central Government has
       released an assistance of Rs.204.50 crore, in advance, to State Disaster Risk
       Management Fund (SDRMF)/State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and
       Rs.2.90 crore from NDRF to the State Government of Himachal Pradesh.


       7.    On 29.12.2020, Union Home Secretary chaired a meeting on Sub­
       committee of National Executive Committee (SC-NEC) to consider the report of
       Inter Ministerial Central Team on damage caused by Flood/Land Slides of 2020
       in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh.

       8.    The whole state of Nagaland has been declared as 'disturbed area' under
       Section 3 of the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 for a further period of
       six months w.e.f. 30.12.2020 Vide MHA's Notification No. SO 4767(E) dated
       30.12.2020.
1967204/2021/CIC-C(I)


        9.    Sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheets against 43 accused
        persons was accorded in accordance with section 45(1) of Unlawful Activities
        (Prevention) Act, 1967 and section 196 of Cr PC.

        10. During the month, more than 5193 kg of narcotic substances have been seized
        and 48 persons were arrested for their involvement in drug trafficking.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, November 2020
pages:
1941108/2020/CIC-C(I)
       Ministry of   Home     Affairs-Major    Achievements,  significant
       Development and important events for the month of November, 2020.


             On 4.11.2020, Union Home Secretary wrote to the Chief Secretaries
       of Govt, of Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya
       Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh regarding
       progress of roads in LWE affected areas.

       2.    On 19th November, 2020 Union Home Secretary spoke to the
       Australian Home Secretary and had a satisfactory discussion on various
       issues of mutual concern.

       3.    On 25.11 2020, guidelines for Covid -19 surveillance, containment
       and caution were issued which would be in force till 31.12.2020. I also wrote
       to the Chief Secretaries/Administrators of all States/UTs sensitizing them
       regarding strict compliance of these guidelines.

       4.    On 11.11.2020, Joint Secretary (LWE) held a meeting through Video
       Conference with BSF, CRPF & IB regarding heli-support for operations in
       Naxal affected areas. On 17.11.2020 he also held a meeting through Video
       Conference with IB and Nodal Officer of LWE affected States regarding
       review of districts under Security Related Expenditure (SRE) Scheme.

       5.     Sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet against 7 accused
       persons was accorded in accordance with section 45(1) of the Unlawful
       Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.

       6.    During the month 84 Nos. of Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various
       States for maintaining law and order duties for a specific period/time frame.
       7.    Massive plantation drive has been undertaken by CAPFs during the
       year 2020. Upto 30.11.2020, 1,46,92,297 saplings have been planted by
       the CAPFs.
       8.     An amount of Rs.4,47,54,600/- (Rupees Four crore forty seven lakh
       fifty four thousand six hundred only) has been sanctioned as Ex-gratia
       Compensation to the NOKs (Next of Kin) of CAPFs and ARs in 22 cases.


        9.    One Indian Civil prisoner was repatriated from Pakistan to India
        during the month. Twenty Pakistani fishermen and four Pakistani Civil
        prisoners were also repatriated.
1941108/2020/CIC-C(I)



       10. CCTNS software has been deployed at 15263 out of 16098 Police
       Stations across the country, and, around 15007 Police Stations out of 16098
       Police Stations are entering 100% FIRs through CCTNS.
       11. CCTNS National Data Centre is getting data from 36 States/UTs, Data
       digitization of 3.90 crore records has been completed which is 91.33% of the
       total target. All States/UTs have launched their State Citizen Centric
       Portals.
       12. During the month, Core Application Software [CAS(State)5.0} has
       been released to two States, Chhattisgarh (Java Stack) and Haryana
       (M icrosoft stack) on 19.11.2020 on pilot basis, after com pletion of
       Functional and Security Audit by Standardisation Testing and Quality
       Certification (STQC), Kolkata.
        13.  A booklet has been prepared on Mobile App for Crime Scene
       Photography/Videography, detailing scope and extent of the usage on
       Mobile App; Legal tenability of the evidence to be tendered in the form of
       video/data gathered using App; application of SoP vis-a-vis the role of
       Forensic / FSL teams; and variation between the time of videography and the
       time of uploading of the same on the web portal.

        14.  During the month, training on use of Mobile App for Crime Scene
       Photography/Videography was given to 67 Police Officers of South District
       Police of Delhi by NCRB officers. The App was duly integrated with Delhi
       CCTNS database using VPN.
        15.  Access of 1CJS/CCTNS search was provided to Enforcem ent
       Directorate (ED) on their request. Administrative user has been created for
       ED to create further users for their field officers to access ICJS/CCTNS
       Search.
        16.  National Automated Fingerprint Identification System (NAFIS) solution
       has been deployed in 29 SFPBx & 265 district sites. Total 425 workstations
       are completed till now.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, October 2020
pages:
1926504/2020/CIC-C(I)

        Ministry of   Home     Affairs-Major Achievements,      significant
        Development and important events for the month of October, 2020.


              The Rashtriya Ekta Diwas was celebrated on 31-10-2020. On this
        occasion, a special event was organized at statue of Unity at Kevadia,
        Gujarat, which was presided over by Hon'ble Prime Minister.

        2.    On 07.10.2020, MOS (G) took a meeting with the representatives of
        Gorkha Janmukti Morcha (GJM) on the issues related to Gorkhaland
        Territorial Administration (GTA).

       3     On 01.10.2020, Union Home Secretary chaired a meeting to review
       strategic issues relating to COVID-19 m anagem ent and facilitation of
       supply chain & logistics management in the country.

       4.    On 06.10.2020, Union Home Secretary chaired two meetings one with the
       DGs of Police & senior officers of Home and DM Departments of State/UT
       Governments and another meeting with the DsGP of CAPFs/CPOs regarding
       implementation of 'Jan Andolan’ for COVID appropriate behavior in the
       country.

       5.    An Order extending the validity of guidelines for re-opening dated
       30.09.2020, up to 30.11.2020 was issued.

       6.    On 08.10.2020, Union Home Secretary chaired a meeting of Sub­
       com m ittee of National Executive Committee (SC-NEC) to consider the
       report of Inter-Ministrial Central Team on damage caused by Cyclone Storm
       "Amphan" of 2020 in West Bengal.

       7.     On 22.10.2020, Union Home Secretary chaired a meeting of Sub­
       com m ittee of National Executive Committee (SC-NEC) to consider the
       report of Inter-Ministerial Central Team on damage caused by
       flood/landslides in 2020 in Karnataka and cyclone storm "Nisarga" of 2020 in
       Maharashtra.

       8.    On 01.10.2020, Union Home Secretary chaired a meeting of
       Delegated Investment Board (DIB) in connection with setting up of an
       Integrated Check Post (ICP) at Sabroom, South Tripura on Indo-
       Bangladesh Border, DIB proposal has been approved by the Hon'ble Home
       Minister and the same has been conveyed to LPAI.
1926504/2020/CIC-C(I)




        9.    During the month of October, 2020, assistance of Rs. 662 crore for
        Gujarat and Rs. 20.50 Crore for Nagaland has been released in advance
        from SDRF.

        10. An amount of Rs. 10,41,69,200/- (Rupees ten crore, forty one lakh,
        sixty nine thousand and two hundred) only has been sanctioned as Ex-
        gratia Compensation to the NOKs of CAPFs and ARs.

         11.    Union Home Secretary have Chaired a Video Conference with the
         representatives of Secretaries of MoRD, MoEFCC, MoRTH, DG:CRPF, Chief
         Secretaries,    Principal Secretaries   (Home),  Principal Secretaries
         (Implementing Department) of LWE affected States to review the
         progress of construction of roads under RRP-I and RCPLWEA in LWE
         affected States.

         12. A D.O letter issued to the Chief Secretary, Govt, of Jharkhand on
         13.10.2020 regarding pending ITIs and SDCs in LWE affected areas of
        jharkhand.

         13.  On 07.10.2020, JS (LWE) chaired a VC to review the progress of
        Aspirational District programme. He also took a meeting through VC to
        discuss upgradation of CAPF Hospitals in LWE theatre.

         14. Advisories were issued to the States Governments/ CAPFs to
        sensitize them to counter the LWE activities in the LW E affected areas.

         15.    Sanction for prosecution for filling the charge sheet against 24
        accused persons was accorded in accordance with section 45(1) of Unlawful
        Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 in respect of NIA Case.

        16.   Tirap, Changlang and Longding districts of Arunachal Pradesh and
        the areas falling with the jurisdiction of four police stations in other districts
        of Arunachal Pradesh, bordering the State of Assam have been notified
        on 01.10.2020 as 'disturbed area' under Section 3 of the Armed Forces
        (Special Powers) Act, 1958 for a further period of six months w.e.f.
        1.10.2020 to 31.03.2021.
                                                                                         311
1926504/2020/CIC-C(I)




        17.   Recruitment Rules for 2345 Technical posts, consisting of Group 'A', ’B'
        & 'C1of National Disaster Response Force were notified on 09-10-2020.

        18.     During the month, more than 4201 kg of Narcotics Substances have been
        seized and 40 persons were arrested for their involvement in drug
        trafficking

        19.  National Police University by the name of Rashtriya Raksha University
        (RRU) has been established through the Rashtriya Raksha University Act,
        2020 which came into effect from 01.10.2020. The draft RRU Rules have also
        been notified on 20.10.2020. Dr. Bimal Patel has been appointed as the
        Vice Chancellor of RRU.

        20. During the month, the Hon'ble President assented T h e Gujarat
        Prohibition of Transfer of Immovable Property and Provision for Protection of
        Tenants from Eviction from Premises in Disturbed Areas (Amendment) Bill,
        2019’ ; The Factories (Uttar Pradesh Amendment) Bill, 2020' and The Andhra
        Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Tribes Bill, 2019'.
