docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, September 2020
pages:
Ministry of   Home     Affairs-Major    Achievements,   significant
Development and important events for the month of September, 2020.


       Hon'ble Home Minister took a meeting with Chief Minister Tripura
on 21.09.2020 to review the pending issues of Tripura relating to Bru
Agreement signed on 16.01.2020 and MoS signed with NLFT/SD on
10.08.2019.

2.    On 20.09.2020 Union Home Minister took a meeting with Chief
Minister of Assam to discuss various issues of Assam including
implementation of Bodo Accord within timeline.
3.    Union Home Secretary have chaired a meeting on 08.09.2020 with the
representatives of cinemas/ multiplex Industry associations to hear their
view on the issue of re-opening of the industry and other ancillary matters.
4.   Union Home Secretary have also taken a meeting on 08.09.2020
regarding turnover of Medical and Para-Medical staff at Sardar Vallabh
Bhai Patel COVID-19 Hospital, New Delhi.

5.   Union Home Secretary have taken a meeting to review of
management of COVID-19 situation in National Capital Region (NCR) on
23.09.2020.
6.   For management of Covid-19 the Empowered Groups under
the Disaster Management Act, 2005 have been re-constituted on
11.09.2020.
7.   A D.O. letter was issued on 18-09-2020 to all Chief Secretaries and
Administrators of States/UTs regarding un-interrupted supply of Medical
Oxygen in the country.
8.     On 30.09.2020, MHA issued guidelines for phased re-opening and
extended the lockdown in Containment Zones upto 31.10.2020. D.O.
letter issued to all Chief Secretaries and Administrators of States/UTs to
ensure compliance of guidelines for phased re-opening.
9.     Ban on National Socialist Council of Nagaland (Khaplang) as
"Unlawful Associations" under Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967
has been extended for five more years upto 27.09.2025 vide MHA
Notification No. SO 3350 (E) dated 28.09.2020.
10. Suspension of Operation (So0) agreements with KNO (Kuki
National Organization) and UPF (United Progressive Front) of Manipur
have been extended for six more months till 28.02.2021.

11. Proposal for construction of 32 ICBR-II roads measuring 638.12 Km
amounting to Rs.12434.90 crore has been approved on 21.09.2020

13. The Advisory(SoP) on police service K9s(PSKs) has been issued
on16.09.2020 to ascertain the technical proficiency of PSKs in
detection of explosives and narcotics substances by conducting K9
Proficiency Evaluation Test (K9PET) among CAPFs and other Central or
State Police and Law Enforcement agencies. The advisory is aimed to
ensure technical proficiency detection of DoGs by each organization
internally every six months and annually by independent or third party
assessments for their certification in assigned task.
 14. AS (PM) review procurement plans of BSF and CRPF on 10.09.2020
respectively.
 15. On 28.09.2020, a meeting was conducted with all CAPFs to
review progress of creation of 100 new categories on GEM portal.

16. Sanctions for prosecution for filing the charge sheet against 35
accused persons were accorded in accorded in accordance with section
45(1) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 and section 196 of
CRPC.
17. The Rashtriya Raksha University Bill, 2020 was passed by both
houses of Parliament. The RRU Act,2020 has been notified on
28.09.2020. It became effective from 1st October, 2020.
18. The newly constituted Standing Committee for Police Research
(SCPR)n held its first meeting in September, 2020. The SCPR finalized
two projects for award of grant by BPR&D. These projects are : 'Functioning
and impact of open prisons on rehabilitation of prisoners of radicalization in
India' and 'An exploratory study on Prevention and Remedies'.

 19. During the month, the Hon'ble president assented 'The Contract
Labour (Regulation and Abolition) (Goa Amendment) Bill, 2020'; 'The
Industrial Disputes (Goa Amendment) Bill, 2020' ; and 'The Factories
Disputes (Goa Amendment) Bill, 2020'.

 20. Previous sanctions of the Hon'ble President have been conveyed
to State Govts. on 'Madhya Pradesh Sahukar (Sanshodhan) Vidheyak,
2020' and 'Madhya Pradesh Anusuchit Janjati Rin Vim ukti Vidheyak, 2020'.
21.    Instructions of the Hon'ble President for promulgation of 'The
Contract Labour Regulation and Abolition) (Odisha Amendment)
Ordinance' and 'The Factories (Odisha Amendment) Ordinance, 2020'
have been conveyed to the State Govt. on 17-09-2020.

                                     ****

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, August 2020
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant
  Development and important events for the month of August, 2020.


     Orders extending the lockdown in containment zones till
30.09.2020 and new guidelines for phased re-opening (Unlock-4) were
issued on 29.08.2020. A D.O. letter was also issued to all Chief
Secretaries and Administrators of States /UTs for strict compliance and
implementation of the guidelines.

2.    MHA has continued to rigorously monitor and take all necessary
actions for containment of Covid 19 pandemic. Revised SOP for
international travel on nonscheduled international flights under Vande
Bharat Scheme and Air Transport Bubble arrangement was issued on
22.08.2020.

3.    Further, on 22.08.2020 a D.O letter has been issued to all Chief
Secretaries and Administrators of States/UTs regarding non-imposing of
restriction on inter-State and intra-State movement of persons and goods
and services.

4.   On 07/08/2020, Union Home Secretary chaired the 48th High Level
Empowered Committee meeting on border infrastructure projects at North
Block, New Delhi.

5.   The Half Yearly Review of LWE scenario in the month of August, 2020
has been shared, through VC, with the State Governments' of Bihar,
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Odisha.

6.    Empowered Committee Meeting chaired by Special Secretary (Police)
was held on 07.08.2020 through VC to review the progress of
developmental works in respect of financial inclusion in LWE affected
districts.

7.   Special Secretary (Police) had also reviewed the implementation
mechanism for countering activities of CPI (Maoist) in Urban Areas on
07.08.2020 with the Nodal Officers from States, and also with agencies
though VC.
8.   Joint Secretary (LWE) held a review meeting on 10.08.2020 through
VC regarding upgradation of hospitals in LWE affected districts.

9.    An Advisory was issued to the State Governments /CAPFs to
sensitize them to counter the LWE activities in the LWE affected areas.

10. 215 Police Medals for Gallantry (PMG), 80 President's Police Medal
(PPM) for Distinguished Service and 631 Police Medal (PM) for
Meritorious Service were announced on the occasion of Independence
Day, 2020 for Police Personnel.
11. Total 113 awards to the Fire Service, Home Guards and Civil Defence
personnel were announced on the occasion of Independence Day, 2020.
12. Sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheets against 50
accused persons was accorded in accordance with section 45(1) of the
Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 and section 196 of CrPC.
13. Fake Indian Currency Notes (FICN) having face value of
Rs. 1,90,500/- in denomination of Rs.500/- and 4.949 Kg of narcotics
substance (heroin) worth approximately Rs.15 Cr. have been seized during
the month.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, July 2020
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant
    Development and important events for the month of July, 2020.

      Union Home Minister took a meeting on 02.07.2020 to review the
 Management of Covid-19 situation in National Capital Region and on
 03.07.2020 to review preparedness of measures to deal with monsoon and
 flood situation in major floor prone river basins in the country

2.    Union Home Secretary have written a D.O. dated 11.07.2020 to the
Chief Secretaries/ Administrator of all States/UTs on giving incentives to
NCC Certificate holders in recruitment to the State Police Forces.

3.    An advisory issued on 24.07.2020 to the Chief Secretaries/
Administrators of all States/ UTs on Welfare of families/ dependents of
Police/ CAPF personnel.

4.     09 (nine) nos. of ‘NOC’ have been issued for change of name of
villages.

5.     During the month more than 8041 kgs of Narcotics substance have
been seized. Total 47 persons were arrested for their involvement in drug
trafficking.

6.    Sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet against 55
accused person was accorded in accordance with section 45(1) of the
Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 and section 196 of CrPC. Fake
Indian Currency Notes (FICN) having face value of Rs.34,31,000/- in
domination of Rs.2000/- and Rs.500/- have been seized.

7.   The Ministry had declared (09) nine individuals as designated terrorists
under the provisions of the UA (P) A, 1967.

8.     During the month of July, 2020 The Contract Labour (Regulation &
Abolition) (Gujarat Amendment) Ordinance, 2020, The Factories Act
(Arunachal Pradesh Amendment) Ordinance, 2020, The Industrial Disputes
(Arunachal Pradesh Amendment) Ordinance, 2020, The Contract Labour
(Regulation & Abolition) (Arunachal Pradesh Amendment) Ordinance, 2020,
The Industrial Disputes and Certain other laws (Karnataka Amendment)
Ordinance, 2020, The Factories (Punjab Amendment) Ordinance, 2020,
Labour Laws (Gujarat Amendment) Ordinance, 2020, The Industrial
Disputes (The Tripura Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2020, The Industrial
Disputes (Assam Amendment) Ordinance, 2020, The Factories (Assam
Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2020 have been ftnalized and instruction of
the Hon' ble President for promulgation of the Ordinance have been
conveyed to State Governments. Hon' ble President has given his assent to
The Code of Criminal Procedure (Uttarakhand Amendment) Bill, 2019.

9. During the month of July 2020, 30,050 cybercrime incidents have been
reported on cybercrime portal and 273 FIRs have been registered.

10. 49 Chinese Mobile Apps were blocked for public access by Meity under
Section 69 A of IT Act, 2020.

गृह मंत्रालय की जुलाई, 2020 के ललए मुख्य उपलब्धियां, महत्वपूर्ण घटनाक्रम और

उल्लेखनीय कायणकलाप


         कें द्रीय गृ ह मं त्री महोदय ने , राष्‍्र ीय राजधानी क्षे त्र में कोविड-19 की स्थिवि के
प्रबं ध न की समीक्षा करने के विए वदनां क 02.07.2020 को ििा मानसू न और दे श में बाढ़
की अवधक सं भािना िािे प्रमु ख नदी बे वसन में बाढ़ की स्थिवि से वनप्ने के विए उपायों
की िै यारी की समीक्षा हे िु वदनां क 03.07.2020 को बै ठ क िी।

2.       केन्‍दद्रीय गृ ह सविि ने , राज्य पुविस बिों की भिी में एनसीसी प्रमाण-पत्र धारकों को
प्रोत्साहन दे ने के बारे में सभी राज्यों/संघ राज्य क्षेत्रों के मुख्य सवििों/प्रशासकों को वदनां क
11.07.2020 को अधध-शासकीय पत्र विखा है ।

3.     पुविस/केंद्रीय सशथत्र पुविस बि कावमधकों के पररिारों/आवििों के कल्याण के बारे में , सभी
राज्ों/संघ राज्य क्षेत्रों के मुख्य सवििों/प्रशासकों को वदनां क 24.07.2020 को परामशी पत्र जारी
वकया गया।

4.     09 गां िों के नाम बदिने के विए “अनापवि प्रमाण-पत्र” जारी वकया गया है ।

5.         इस माह के दौरान, 8041 वकिोग्राम से अवधक थिापक पदािध जब्ि वकए गए हैं ।
डर ग ्र ै विवकं ग में सं विप्ििा के विए कु ि 47 व्यस्ियों को वगरफ्तार वकया गया।

6.      विवधविरुद्ध वियाकिाप (वनिारण) अवधवनयम, 1967 की धारा 45(1) ििा दं ड प्रविया
सं वहिा की धारा 196 के अनु सार, 55 अवभयु िों के विरुद्ध आरोप-पत्र दास्खि करने के विए
अवभयोजन की थिीकृवि प्रदान की गई। दो हजार रु. (2000/-) ििा पां ि सौ रु. (500/-) के
नो्ों में कु ि 34,31,000 रु. अं वकि मू ल्य के जािी भारिीय करें सी नो् (एिआईसीएन)
जब्ि वकए गए हैं ।

7.      मं त्रािय ने विवधविरुद्ध वियाकिाप (वनिारण) अवधवनयम, 1967 के प्रािधानों के
अं िगध ि वदनां क 01 जु िाई, 2020 को 09 व्यस्ियों को नामोवदष्‍् आिं किादी घोविि वकया है I

8.      इस माह के दौरान, संविदा िवमक (विवनयमन और उन्‍दमू िन) (गुजराि सं शोधन) अध्यादे श,
2020, कारखाना अवधवनयम (अरुणािि प्रदे श संशोधन) अध्यादे श, 2020, औद्योवगक वििाद

(अरुणािि प्रदे श संशोधन) अध्यादे श, 2020, औद्योवगक वििाद ििा कविपय अन्‍दय विवधयां
(कनाध ्क सं शोधन) अध्यादे श, 2020, कारखाना (पंजाब सं शोधन) अध्यादे श, 2020, िम कानू न
(गुजराि संशोधन) अध्यादे श, 2020, औद्योवगक वििाद (वत्रपुरा वििीय सं शोधन) अध्यादे श, 2020,
औद्योवगक वििाद (असम संशोधन) अध्यादे श, 2020, करखाना (असम वििीय संशोधन)
अध्यादे श, 2020 को अंविम रूप वदया गया है ििा अध्यादे श को प्रख्यावपि वकए जाने के विए
माननीय राष्‍्र पवि का अनुदेश राज्य सरकारों को संसूविि वकया गया है । माननीय राष्‍्र पवि ने दं ड
प्रवकया संवहिा (उत्िराखं ड सं शोधन) विधे यक, 2019 को अपनी थिीकृवि प्रदान कर दी है ।

9.    इस माह के दौरान, साइबर अपराध पो्ध ि पर 30,050 साइबर अपराध संबंधी घ्नाएं सूविि
की गई हैं ििा 273 प्रािवमवकयां दजध की गई हैं ।

10.    आई्ी अवधवनयम, 2020 की धारा 69(क) के अं िगध ि, इिे क्‍्र ोवनक एिं सू िना प्रौद्योवगकी
मंत्रािय िारा 49 िीनी मोबाइि एप्प को जनिा की पहं ि के विए ब्िॉक कर वदया गया है ।

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, June 2020
pages:
Home Secretary
AJAY BHALLA, IAS                                                   'HNcI WcbK
                                                                Government of India
                                                                   North Block,
                                                                    New Delhi
   D.O. No. 1-25011/ 1/20Jp-Coord.I               16 th July,      2020




   Dear
              )


        I am writing this in respect of the significant developments
   pertaining to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) during the month
   June, 2020.

   2.   Honhle Home Minister held a high level review meeting, on
   01st June, 2020,with officials of NDMA, NDRF, IMD, and Indian
   Coast Guard on preparedness for dealing with Cyclone brewing in
   Arabian Sea. Honhle Home Minister also held a Video Conference
   meeting with Chief Ministers of Gujarat and Maharashtra.

   3.    Ministry of Home Affairs has deputed an Inter-Ministerial
   Central Team (IMCT) for an on-the-spot assessment of the damage
   and the admissibility of such supplemental central assistance in the
   wake of Cyclone ”Amphan” in West Bengal and Odisha and Cyclone
   “Nisarga” in Maharashtra. IMCT visited the Cyclone “Amphan”
   affected areas of West Bengal from 4-6 June, 2020 and Odisha from
   3-6 June, 2020.     Similarly, IMCT visited the Cyclone “Nisarga”
   affected areas of Maharashtra from 15-20 June, 2020.

   4.   Honhle Home Minister on 30.6.2020 held a meeting to review
   the activities of NDMA.

  5.   MHA has continued to rigorously monitor and take all
  necessary actions for containment of Covid 19 pandemic.
  Subsequent to issue of guidelines for Unlock-I, a modified SOP was
  issued on 01.06.2020, for movement of persons Stranded in India
  who desire to travel abroad.

  6.   Further, on 12.06.2020 I wrote to all Chief Secretaries and
  Administrators of States/UTs regarding clarification of movement
  during night curfew period.
                                                        ..contd.p/2..
                                  : : 2 ::

 7.    Hon'ble Home Minister reviewed management of Covid-19
 situation in Delhi on 14.06.2020 and thereafter several effective
 steps have been taken for management of Covid-19 situation in
 Delhi. These include four times increase in Covid-19 testing,
introduction of rapid antigen test, increasing Covid-19 beds to more
than 15,000, substantial increase in number of oxygenated
beds/ventilators, increase in number of ambulances to 609, conduct
of sero-survey, continuous review of containment zones, efficient
management of containment zones, setting up of District level and
UT level Covid Surveillance Centres etc. This has resulted in overall
improvement in Covid-19 situation in Delhi.

8.     HM again held a meeting on 18.06.2020, to review the
preparations of NCR for management of COVID-19 with the senior
officials of NCR.

9.   On 25.06.2020 & 26.06.2020, I held a meeting to discuss the
issues relating to operationalisation of makeshift 1000 bed hospital
through DRDO.

10. Orders extending the lockdown up to 31.07.2020 and new
guidelines for phased re-opening (Unlock-2) were issued on
29.06.2020. I also wrote to all Chief Secretaries and Administrators
of States/UTs impressing upon them the need for strict compliance
and implementation of the guidelines.

 11. I reviewed the progress of investigation in North East riot cases
and use of technology in Delhi Police in the meeting on 26.06.2020,
Directions for improvement in use of technology in Delhi Police were
issued during the meeting. Delhi Police has commenced use of
ICJS.

12. As on 30.6.2020, MHA has received more than 123 Supreme
Court and 260 High Court Cases relating to Covid-19 Pandemic out
of which more than 89 Supreme Court and 90 High Court cases
have been disposed in favour of Union of India.
                                                     ..contd.p/3..
                                :: 3 ::

13. During the month of June, 2020 sanction for prosecution for
filing the charge sheet against 31 accused persons was accorded in
accordance with section 45(1) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention)
Act, 1967 and Section 196 of CrPC.

       Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant
    Development and important events for the month of June, 2020.




      Hon'ble Home Minister held a high level review meeting, on 01st
June, 2020,with officials of NDMA, NDRF, IMD, and Indian Coast
Guard on preparedness for dealing with Cyclone brewing in Arabian
Sea. Hon'ble Home Minister also held a Video Conference meeting with
Chief Ministers of Gujarat and Maharashtra.

2.      M inistry of Home A ffairs has deputed an Inter-M inisterial
Central Team (IMCT) for an on-the-spot assessment of the damage and
the admissibility of such supplemental central assistance in the wake of
Cyclone "Amphan" in West Bengal and Odisha and Cyclone "N isarga" in
M aharashtra. IMCT visited the C yclone "Am phan" affected areas of
West Bengal from 4-6 June, 2020 and Odisha from 3-6 June, 2020.
S im ilarly, IMCT visited the C yclone "N isarga" affected areas of
Maharashtra from15-20 June, 2020.


3.     Hon' ble Home Minister on 30.6.2020 held a meeting to review the
activities of NDMA.

4.      M HA has co n tin u e d to rig o ro u s ly m o n ito r and take all
n e c e s s a ry a c tio n s fo r c o n ta in m e n t o f C ovid 19 p a n d e m ic.
Subsequent to issue of guidelines for Unlock-I, a modified SOP was
issued on 01.06.2020, for movement of persons Stranded in India who
desire to travel abroad.

5.   Further, on 12.06.2020 Union Home Secretary wrote to all Chief
Secretaries and Administrators of States/UTs regarding clarification of
movement during night curfew period.

6.      Hon’ble Home Minister reviewed management of Covid-19
situation in Delhi on 14.06.2020 and thereafter several effective steps
have been taken for management of Covid-19 situation in Delhi. These
include four tim es increase in Covid-19 testing, introduction of rapid
antigen test, increasing Covid-19 beds to more than 15,000, substantial
increase in num ber of oxygenated beds/ventilators, increase in number
of ambulances to 609, conduct of sero-survey, continuous review of
containment zones, efficient management of containment zones, setting
up of District level and UT level Covid Surveillance Centres etc. This has
resulted in overall improvement in Covid-19 situation in Delhi.
7.    HM again held a m eeting on 18.06.2020, to review the
preparations of NCR for management of COVID-19 with the senior officials
of NCR.

8.     On 25.06.2020 & 26.06.2020, Union Home Secretary held a meeting
to discuss the issues relating to operationalisation of makeshift 1000 bed
hospital through DRDO.

9.       Orders extending the lockdown up to 31.07.2020 and new
g u id e lin e s fo r phased re-opening (U n lo ck-2 ) w ere issued on
29.06.2020. Union Home Secretary also wrote to all Chief Secretaries and
Administrators of States/UTs impressing upon them the need for strict
compliance and implementation of the guidelines.

10.    Union Home Secretary reviewed the progress of investigation in North
East riot cases and use of technology in Delhi Police in the meeting held on
26.06.2020, Directions for improvement in use of technology in Delhi Police
were issued during the meeting. Delhi Police has commenced use of
ICJS.

11. As on 30.6.2020, MHA has received more than 123 Supreme Court
and 260 High Court Cases relating to Covid-19 Pandemic out of which
more than 89 Supreme Court and 90 High Court cases have been
disposed in favour of Union of India.


12. During the month of June, 2020 sanction for prosecution for filing the
charge sheet against 31 accused persons was accorded in accordance with
section 45 (1) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 and Section
196 of CrPC.

13. 28 Coys of CAPFs w ere deployed in various S tates i.e.
Telangana, Gujarat, Maharashtra, M.P, Goa and Daman 86 Diu frame

          Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant
        Development and important events for the month of May, 2020.

     To deal with the crisis/emergency situation arising out of Covid-19 in
the country, MHA has continued to take proactive measures to mitigate
the same. Some of these measures are delineated as under:

   I.     MHA vide orders dated 1.5.2020 and 17.5.2020, extended the
          lockdown period for four weeks in two phases with effect from
          4.5.2020 and again w.e.f 18.5.2020, along with fresh guidelines.

  II.     Empowered Groups were reconstituted vide this Ministry's order
          dated 1.5.2020 for planning and ensuring implementation of Covid-
          19 response activities.

 III.     Vide order dated 5.5,2020, SOPs for movement of Indian Nationals
          stranded outside the country and of specified persons to travel
          abroad have been issued keeping in view the emergent situation.
          This was further revised vide order dated 24.5.2020.

 IV.      Similarly SOPs for movement of persons by train were also issued
          vide order dated 11.5.2020. Revised SOPs on movement of stranded
          workers by trains were issued vide order dated 19.5.2020.

 V.       Amended guidelines regarding deletion of domestic air travel of
          passengers from the list of prohibited activities was issued vide
          order dated 20.5.2020.

VI.       Chief Secretaries of all States /UTs were informed about granting
          exemption for conduct of Board Examinations vide DO letter dated
          20.5.2020.

VII.      To ensure p ro p e r im p le m e n ta tio n o f the g u id e lin e s , C hief
          Secretaries of all States and administrators of UTs were informed
         about the violations and were directed to ensure strict compliance to
         the guidelines vide DO letter dated 21.5.2020.

viii.    MHA vide order dated 30.5.2020, issued guidelines on extension of
         Lock Down in Containment Zones and phased reopening. All Chief
         Secretaries and Administrators of UTs were informed regarding
         extension of lockdown in containment zones upto 30.6.2020 vide
         DO dated 30.5.2020.
 ix.   This Ministry continued to coordinate law and order situation in the
       country as well as strict observation of COV1D-19 lockdown
       guidelines in the country. Central Control Room (OCR) in the North
       Block was expanded to ensure uninterrupted supply and movement
       of essential goods and services, providing quick and adequate food
       and shelter to people, especially migrant workers, poor, homeless
       and destitute, by the States / Union Territories, facilitate movement of
       stranded migrant workers and prompt resolution of any request / other
       problem received from any aggrieved persons 24 X 7.

3.   The National Crisis Management Committee (NCMC), headed by
Cabinet Secretary, met regularly since 16.05.2020 onward till 21.05.2020 to
monitor the situation with the states and Central Ministries/Agencies
concerned regarding Amphan Cyclone. In order to help the Cyclone
Amphan effected states, Central Govt, has released an amount of Rs.
1000 crore to West Bengal and Rs. 500 Cr to Odisha on account basis
from National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF).

4.    On 15.05.2020, Hon'ble Home Minister held High Level Committee
meeting and approved additional Central Assistance of Rs. 122.33 crore to
the State of Meghalaya. (Rs. 18.871 crore), Manipur (Rs.34.81 crore) and
Rajasthan (Rs.68,65 crore) for flood/landslides/drought (Kharif)/
pest(locust) attack during 2019-20.

5.    On 20.5,2020 Union Home S e creta ry chaired the Annual
C onference of R e lie f Commissioners/ Secretaries, Department of
Disaster Management of the States/UTs, to review the status of
preparedness for south west monsoon, 2020. This was held through Video
conferencing.

6.    During the month, more than 3434 kgs of Narcotics substances
have been seized and 25 persons were arrested for their involvement in
drug trafficking.

7.    During the month sanction for prosecution for filing the charge
sheet against 17 accused persons was accorded in accordance with
section 45(1) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 and section
196 of CrPC. Fake Indian c u rre n c y notes of to ta l face value of
Rs.6,19,000/- have been seized.

8.    CCTNS software has been deployed at 15212 out of 16050 Police
Stations across the country. Around 14966 Police Stations out of 16050
Police Stations are entering 100% FIRs through CCTNS.
9.   CCTNS National Data Centre is getting data from 36 States/UTs.
Out of Total outlay of the Project of Rs 2000 crore. Rs. 1826,5 crore have
been released till date to States/UTs and Central Agencies.

10. During the month Adjudication report confirming the ban on
Hynniewtrep National Liberation Council (HNLC) of Meghalaya for a period
of five years w.e.f. 16.11.2019 by the Unlawful Activities (Prevention)
Tribunal has been published vide MHA's Notification No. S.O. 1684(E)
dated 29.5.2020.

11. Producing pups for training and preparation of police service K9s
(Police Dogs) is vital to meet huge requirement among Central Police and
Law Enforcement Agencies. To suitably address the issue, "Guidelines on
Breeding of Police Service K9s (PSKs) at CAPFs Dog Breeding &, training
Centre's" was issued to support scientific and professional breeding
norms, of principles of animal breeding and genetics. Further, breeding
mandate was accorded to BSF and ITBP also, apart from SSB, to scale up
the production of pups to make up the existing deficiency of Police
service K9s.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, March and April 2020
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
     and important events for the month of March and April, 2020.



       Various proactive measures have been taken by MHA and in my
capacity as Chairperson, National Executive Committee (NEC), to deal with
the situation arising out due to outbreak of COVID-19 in the country. Some of
these measures are delineated as under:

     i.    To enable Secretary. Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (MoHFW)
     for taking effective measures for containment of COV1D-19. on
     11.3.2020, Chairperson, National Executive C om m ittee (NFC),
     delegated pow er under D isaster Management (DM) Act, 2005 to
     Secretary. MoHFW to enhance the preparedness and containment of
     COVID-19 and other ancillary matters connected thereto.

     ii.  On 14.03.2020, with a view to augment the availability of funds with
     the State Governments. COVID- 19 was declared as notified disaster by
     Central Government for the purpose of providing assistance under
     State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) placed at the disposal of
     respective State Governments.

     iii.  National D isaster Management A uthority (NDMA) vide order
     dated 24.03.2020, after assessing the threatening situation of
     spreading of COVID-19 in the country and in exercise of its powers
     under section 6(2) (i) of the Disaster Management Act, 2005. directed
     the NEC to issue necessary guidelines to the Ministries/ Departments
     of Government of India, State Governments and State Authorities to
     take measures for ensuring social distancing.

      iv.   In compliance of NDMA’s aforesaid Order, Chairperson, NEC
      issued an Order dated 24th March, 2020 under DM Act, 2005 along
      with the guidelines on the measures to be taken by the Ministries/
      Departments of Government of India, States/ UTs Governments and
      State/ UTs Authorities for containment of COVID-19 Epidemic in the
      country. Vide this Order lockdown measures were implemented in the
      country for a period of 21 days with effect from 25th March, 2020.
v.    Further, for ensuring smooth supply of essential goods in all
parts of the country, a detailed Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
was issued by MHA on 26.03.2020 to all State,' UT Governments. In the
SOP, detailed procedure was laid down to ensure hassle free
movement of essential goods and all facilities in their supply chain
involved in manufacturing, wholesale or retail of such goods through
local stores, e-Commerce companies etc. after ensuring social
distancing.

vi.   On 28.03.2020. the Central Government allowed the State
Governments to use State Disaster Response Fund for providing food
and shelter to homeless people including migrant laborers, who were
stranded due to lockdown measures.

vii.   To deal with the situation and for effective implementation of the
lockdown measures, and to mitigate the economic hardship of the
migrant workers, an Order was issued on 29.03. 2020 with the
directions to the State/ UTs to take additional measures to ensure
adequate arrangements of temporary shelters, and provision of food
etc. for the poor and needy people, including migrant labourers,
stranded due to lockdown measures in their respective areas.

viii. Under the DM Act, 2005, vide order dated 29.3.2020, eleven
Empowered Groups of Officers were constituted keeping in view the
need for comprehensive action and integrated response to the COVID-
19 pandemic.

ix.   Addendums dated 25th March. 27th March. 2nd April. 3rd April and
10th April were also issued to allow additional exemptions during
lockdown.

x.    With a view to make adequate funds available to the State
Governments for effective response against COVID-19, as a special
dispensation, the 1st installment of Rs. 11,092 crore as Central Share
of State Disaster Risk Mitigation Fund (SDRMF) for financial year
2020-21 was released in advance to all States on 03 .04 .2020.

xi.    Considering the fact that the social distancing measures need to
be extended further to contain the spread of Covid-19, NDMA vide
Order dated 14th April, 2020 in exercise of its powers under section
6(2)(i) of the Disaster Management Act, 2005, directed the Ministries/
Departments of Government of India, State Governments and State
Authorities to continue the same measures for social distancing up to
03.05.2020.

xii.   In compliance of NDMA directions, Order dated 14th April, 2020
under DM Act, 2005 was issued giving directions to all
M inistries/D epartm ents of Government of India, States/ UTs
Governments and State/ Uts Authorities that lockdown measures
stipulated in consolidated guidelines of MHA for containment of
COVID-19 epidem ic in the country will continue to remain in force
up to 03.05.2020.

xiii. Vide Order dated 15th April, 2020 under DM Act, 2005 consolidated
revised guidelines was issued. With a view to mitigate the hardship of
public, additional activities were allowed w.e.f. 20th April, 2020 outside
containment zones. MHA also circulated National Directives for
COVID -19 management and a SOP for social distancing for offices,
workplaces. Factories and establishments.

xiv. In addition. Clarifications on queries received from various
Ministries/ Departments/ States/ Uts were also issued time to time
by this Ministry. To mitigate hardship to the public and also based on
the request received various Ministries/ Departments/ States/Uts,
selected additional activities were also allowed.

xv. Vide order dated 19.4.2020, 6 Inter-Ministerial Central Teams
(IMCTs) were constituted, two each for West Bengal and Maharashtra.
And one each for Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan to make on-spot
assessment of situation and issue necessary directions to State
Authorities for its redressal and submit their report to Central
Government in larger interest of general public.

xvi. MHA vide order dated 29.4.2020 allowed the inter-state movement
of migrant workers, pilgrims, tourists, students and other persons
stranded at different places as per Standard Operating Protocol laid
down in the aforesaid order.

xvii. MHA blacklisted 960 foreigners, presently in India on tourist visas,
for their involvement in Tablighi Jamaat activities. MHA has also
directed DGPs of all concerned States/UTs and CP, Delhi Police to
take necessary legal action against all such violators, on priority,
under relevant sections of the Foreigners Act, 1946 and Disaster
Management Act, 2005.
2.     Further, High Level Committee (HLC) meeting was held under Home
Minister on 27.3.2020 to consider the recommendations of SCNEC on
damage caused by flood/ landslides/ cyclone, storm and drought in Bihar,
Kerala. Karnataka, Maharashtra. Nagaland, Odisha, Rajasthan and West
Bengal. HLC approved additional Central assistance of Rs 5.751.27 crore
to eight States from National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) subject to the
adjustment of 50% of balances available in the SDRF account as on 1st April of
the financial year of 2018-19.

3.    Cabinet has approved the Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands Land
Revenue and Tenancy (Amendment) Regulation, 2020 on 26.02.2020. The
amendment regulation has been published in the gazette of India on
18.03.2020. The amendments will allow more economic activities in the
Lakshadweep group of islands by enabling transactions of land among
islanders in a transparent manner.

4.    On 12.03.2020, Hon’ble MoS Shri Nityanand Rai inaugurated online
portal of National Cyber Crime Training Centre (www.cytrain.ncrb.gov.in) at
NCRB New Delhi.

5.    On 02.03.2020, Union Home Secretary held a meeting with the
representatives of Government of Andhra Pradesh and Government of
Karnataka to resolve the Inter-State Boundary issue in Bellary Reserve Forest:
in meeting, both States were advised to cooperate in implementation of the
report of Surveyor General of India.

6.    An amount of Rs 378.23 crore (approx.) was released under the
relevant sub schemes of the umbrella scheme for Modernization of Police
Forces during the month of March 2020.

7.    ‘NOC has been issued for changing the name of 'Manduadih' Railway
Station as 'Banaras' in Varanasi District, Uttar Pradesh.

8.    CCTNS software has been deployed at 15,103 out of 16,023 Police
Stations across the country, i.e. 94.25%. Around 14,900 Police Stations are
entering 100% FIRs through CCTNS.

9.   A total of Rs 13.445 crore was released to 3 States /UTs viz., Goa,
Odisha and Puducherry for strengthening of DNA analysis. Cyber Forensics
and related facilities in their State Forensic Science laboratory under the
Nirbhaya Fund in the FY 1920-21.
10. The Government has approved the proposal for setting up of
National Forensic Sciences University. The National Forensic Sciences
University Bill, 2020 has been introduced in the Lok Sabha on 23.03.2020.

11. Ceasefire agreements signed with National Socialist Council of Nagaland
(NSCN)/ Neopao Konyak-Kitovi and NSCN/ Reformation have been extended
for a period of six months up to 27.10.2020. Ceasefire agreement with
NSCN/ K-Khango group has also been extended for a period of six months
up to 17.10.2020.

12. Tirap. Changlang and Longding districts of Arunachal Pradesh and the
areas falling within the jurisdiction of 4 Police Stations in other districts of
Arunachal Pradesh, bordering the State of Assam have been declared as •
Disturbed Area' under Section 3 of the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act,
1958 for a further period of six months w.e.f. 1.4.2020 to 30.09.2020.

13. A meeting of the Monitoring Committee to review the implementation
status of Memorandum of Settlement (MoS) dated 10.08.2019 signed with
NLFT (SD) of Tripura was held under Joint Secretary (NE), MHA on
20.03.2020.

14. First meeting of Joint Monitoring Committee was held on 20.03.2020 for
review of progress of implementation of agreement dated 16.01.2020 for
resettlement of Bru Migrants in Tripura.

15. During the month of March, more than 1.325 Kg of Narcotic
Substances have been seized. Illicit cultivation of Afeem spread over 99.75
acres of land has been destroyed. During the month of April 2020.
Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) seized 60 Kg of Opium, 61,368 tablets of
psychotropic drug and 840 bottles of codeine based cough syrup. Two
persons were arrested for their involvement in drug trafficking.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, January 2020
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
         and important events for the month of January, 2020.

      Padma Awards have been announced on the occasion of
Republic Day, 2020. This year the President has approved
conferment of 141 Padma Awards

2.    On 02.01.2020, Union Home Minister laid the foundation stone of
NDRF Academy and dedicated the new campus of National Fire Service
College (NFSC) at Nagpur to the nation.

3.    A historic agreement between Government of India,
Government of Assam and Bodo representatives was signed on
27.1.2020 in New Delhi, to end the over 50-year old Bodo crisis.

4.   On 6th January, 2020 High Level Committee meeting was held under
the Chairmanship of Union Home Minister. Central Assistance of
Rs. 5908.56 crore to the States of Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka,
Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tripura and Uttar Pradesh for
Fiood/Landslides/Cloudburst of 2019, was approved.

5.     Meeting of the Consultative Committee of Ministry of Home
Affairs on Disaster Management was held on 30.01.2020 under the
Chairmanship of Union Home Minister.

6.   In order to bring uniformity in the adoption of communication
equipment, the National Communication Standard 2020 has been released
by Union Minister of State for Home Affairs on 20.01.2020.

7.    On 20th January, 2020 , Union Home Secretary held the meeting of
the Sub-Committee of National Executive Committee (SC-NEC) to consider
the report of Inter-Ministerial Central Teams on floods/landslides of 2019
in Kerala and Rajasthan.

8.   On 16th January, 2020, a meeting between US Delegation led by Mr.
Mathew Pottinger, Deputy NSA, US National Security Council and
Government of India Delegation led by Union Home Secretary was held
in New Delhi.

9.      3rd meeting of the Joint Steering Committee and the Joint Working
Groups between India and Israel was held from 14-16 January, 2020 in
Israel.

10. Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty (MLAT) in Criminal Matters
between India and Brazil has been signed on 25.01.2020 in New Delhi
during the VVIP visit of President of Federative Republic of Brazil to
India.
11. The proposal for "Development of infrastructure for 47 Nos. New
Border Out Posts (BOPs) and 12 Nos. staging camps" for Indo -Tibetan
Border Police was approved on 08.01.2020.

12. 1042 Officers/Personnel from the State /UTs /CAPFs were given
Gallantry / Service Medals award on the occasion of Republic Day, 2020.

13.   Sanction has been issued for creation of 119 posts in CISF.

14. Total Number of 152 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States
Karnataka, Arunachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Meghalaya,
Telangana, Manipur, Assam, Tripura, Gujarat, Jharkhand and Bihar
for law & order duty.

15. 190 Coys of CAPFs/SAPs/IR Bns have been ordered for
deployment in NCT of Delhi for Assembly Election 2020.

16. An amount of Rs. 171.46 Crore has been sanctioned to CAPFs for
infrastructure development.

17. An amount of Rs. 2.1 crore has been sanctioned as Ex-gratia
Compensation to the NOKs of CAPFs, in 9 cases, during the month.

18. President's HG & CD Medal for Distinguished Service,
President's Fire Service Medal for Gallantry, President's Fire Service Medal
for Distinguished Service, Fire Service Medal for Meritorious Service award
were distributed to 153 Officers/personnel of Fire Service, Flome Guards
and Civil Defence.

19. In January, 2020 sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet
against 28 accused persons was accorded in accordance with section
45(1) of Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 and sections 188
and 196 of CrPc.

20. During the month, an amount of Rs.34.688 crore has been released
to the State Government of Uttar Pradesh under Border Area
Development Programme (BADP). The total fund released under
BADP, during the current financial year, as on 31.01.2020 is Rs.633.476
crore.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, December 2019
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
         and important events for the month of December, 2019.



      During the month I took a meeting to review the implementation
 status of decisions taken by the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS)
 regarding measures to be taken for Bodo Community in Assam.
 2.   Union Home Secretary chaired the 47th High •Level Empowered
 Committee meeting on 26.12.2019 to review various border projects.
 3.   The entire state of Nagaland has been declared as "disturbed
 area under Armed Forces Special Powers Act, 1958 for a period of six
 months from 30.12.2019 to 29.06.2020.

 4.   The Suspension of Operation (So0) agreements signed with
 National Democratic Front of Bodoland (NDFB)/ Ranjan Daimary and
 NDFP/ Progressive of Assam have been extended for a further period of
 six months upto 30.06.2020.

 5.   The Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (Merger of Union
Territories) Act, 2019 (Act No. 44 of 2019) has been notified on
09.12.2019. The provisions of the Act shall come into force on
26.01.2020.

6.    Gazette notification regarding extension of the Code of Criminal
Procedure (Haryana Amendment) Act, 2014 (Haryana Act No. 19 of
2015) to the UT of Chandigarh has been published in Gazette of India
(Extraordinary) on 16.12.2019.


7.    In compliance to the decisions of CoS, the Government Printing
Presses, at Daman & Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Chandigarh have
been closed. 02 nos. of Printing Press in Delhi Police and 05 nos. of
Printing Press in Lakshadweep have been also closed.

8.   NOC has been issued for changing the name of village "Amin" as
"Abhimanyupur" in District Kurukshetra, Haryana.
9.   CCTNS software has been deployed in 14973 Police Stations
across the country. 14695 Police Stations are entering 100% FIRs
through CCTNS. All States/ UTs have launched their State Citizen
Centric Portals. CCTNS National Data Centre is' getting data from 35
States/ UTs.

10. During the month, sanction for prosecution for‘filing the charge sheet
against 43 accused persons was accorded in accordance with section
45(1) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 and sections 188
86 196 of CrPC.

11. During the month of December, 2019 an amount of Rs 21.047 crore
has been released to the State Government of Sikkim under BADP.
The total fund released under BADP during the Current financial
year (2019-20) (as on 31.12.2019) is Rs 598.78 crore.

12. During the month Sub-Committee of National Executive
Committee (SC-NEC) meeting was held to consider the report of inter-
Ministerial Central Teams on Floods/Landslide/Cloudburst of 2019 in Assam,
Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh and on
unseasonal/heavy rains of October, 2019 in Maharashtra.

13. MHA has conducted an orientation workshop on 13th December, 2019
to sensitize States/ UTs officials for providing on line data through National
Disaster Management Information System (NDMIS). 52 officials from
17 States/ UTs have participated in the workshop.

14. 180 officials of various States Police/CAPFs/CPOs have been
awarded "ASADHARAN AASUCHANA KUSHALATA PADAK" for the year
2019, on 23rd December, 2019.

15. Sanction has been issued for creation of 899 posts in CISF.
16. Total Number of 250 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various
States Arunachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, Assam,
Manipur, Tripura, Meghalaya, Delhi, Puducherry, Karnataka, Gujarat for
maintaining law and order duties.

17. An amount of Rs 36.55 Crore was released for execution of
Swatchata Action Plan related works through CPWD during the years
2019-20 to 2020-21 at various locations of CRPF.

18. An amount of Rs 34.72 Crore has been sanctioned for
development of infrastructure to the CAPF. An amount of Rs. 4.54 Crore
has been sanctioned as Ex-gratia Compensation to the NOKs of CAPFs in
21 cases.

19, The Hon'ble President on 02.12.2019 has assented to the Tamil
Nadu Acquisition Law (Revival of Operation and Validation) Bill, 2019.

20. Instructions of the Hontle President for promulgation of the
Tamil Nadu Puratchi Thalaivi Dr. Jayalalithaa Memorial Foundation
Ordinance, 2019 have been conveyed to State Government on 20.12.2019.

21 The proposal for withdrawal of the Private Detective Agencies
(Regulation) Bill 2007 has been approved by the Cabinet in its meeting held
on 11-12-2019. Motion for withdrawal of the BilF, will be moved during the
coming session of Parliament.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, November 2019
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
        and important events for the month of November, 2019.


       The Hon tie Prime Minister on 09 November 2019 inaugurated the
Integrated Check Post (ICP) at Dera Baba Nanak, Kartarpur Sahib
Corridor to commemorate the 550th Birth Anniversary of Sri Guru Nanak
Dev ji. The ICP would facilitate Indian Pilgrims to visit the Gurudwara
Kartapur Sahib in Pakistan. The first official Jatha of pilgrims was also
flagged off by the Hon'ble Prime Minister. The state-of-the-art Passenger
Terminal Building was built by LPAI, MHA in a record time, is fully air
conditioned, akin to an airport and has over 50 immigration counters for
facilitating about 5000 pilgrims a day.

2.    Meeting between Gol Delegation led by Hon'ble Home Minister,
Shri Amit Shah and a delegation led by Hon'ble Internal Minister of
Uzbekistan, Mr. Pulat Bobojonov was held on 20th November, 2019.
During the meeting an Agreement was signed between the Ministry of
Home Affairs of the Republic of India and the Ministry of Internal
Affairs of the Republic of Uzbekistan on Cooperation in the field of
Combating Transnational Organized Crime and International
Terrorism.

3.   The Union Minister for Home Affairs, Shri Amit Shah inaugurated
the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Joint Exercise on Urban
Earthquake Search & Rescue-2019 in New Delhi on 04.11.2019. The
Exercise was organized by the National Disaster Response Force
(NDRF) from November 4-7, 2019.
4.    On 5th November, 2019, Union Home Secretary held a meeting to
consider the report of Inter-Ministerial Central Teams (IMCT) on
Floods/Landslides/Cyclone of 2019 in Karnataka, Maharashtra and
Tripura.

5.   During the month, three State bills were assented to by the
Hon'ble President of India. These are "The Indian Partnership (Gujarat
Amendment) Bill, 2019", "The Rajasthan Bovine Animal (Prohibition of
Slaughter and Regulation of Temporary Migration or Export)
(Amendment) Bill, 2018" and "The Civil Laws (Uttar Pradesh
Amendment) Bill 2019."

6.    During the month, sanction for prosecution for filing the charge
sheet against 30 accused persons was accorded in accordance with
section 45 (1) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 and
section 188 of CrPC in respect of NIA.
7.   The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Tribunal, by its order dated
06.11.2019, has confirmed the notification issued by the Central
Government on 14.05.2019 under which the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam
(LTTE) was declared an unlawful association.

8.    Under Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1976 ban on
Hynniewtrep National Liberation Council (HNLC) of Meghalaya,
National Democratic Front of Bodoland (NDFB) and United Liberation Front
of Assam (ULFA) as unlawful associations has been extended for five years
more upto 15.11.2024, 22.11.2024 and 26.11.2024 respectively.

9.    An amount of Rs. 1000 Cr. was released from National Disaster
Response Fund (NDRF) in advance, as an interim assistance for flood relief,
to the State Government of Madhya Pradesh.

10. During the month, an amount of Rs.36.90 crore was released to the
State Government of Punjab and Manipur under the Border Area
Development Programme (BADP).

11. 114 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States viz.
Arunachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Delhi, Telangana,
Karnataka, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Gujrat, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Kerala,
Manipur for maintaining law and order during various festivals etc.


12. On the recommendations of Election Commission of India, 343 Coys
of CAPFs were deployed in connection with Bye-
Election/Assembly Election duties in West Bengal, Uttarakhand,
Karnataka and Jharkhand.

13. An amount of Rs.16.03 Crore has been sanctioned for acquisition of
land and Rs.55.87 Crore has been sanctioned for development of
infrastructure to the CAPF. An amount of Rs.1.10 crore has been
sanctioned as Ex-gratia Compensation to the NOKs of CAPFs in 4
cases.

14. Sanction for creation of approx 2000 posts in CISF has been issued
during the month for the purpose of augmentation/induction.

15. During the month more than 5525 kgs of Narcotics substances, have
been seized. 38 persons including 02 foreign nationals were arrested for
their involvement in drug trafficking. In order to enhance the operational
effectiveness of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), MHA has approved
further enhancement/delegation of financial powers of Director General,
NCB.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, October 2019
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
         and important events for the month of October, 2019.


     An Agreement on Security Cooperation and a Memorandum of
Understanding in the field of combating illicit trafficking and smuggling of
narcotics drugs, psychotropic substances and chemical precursors
between the Republic of India and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia were
signed on 29.10.2019 during the visit of Hon' ble Prime Minister of India to
Saudi Arabia.

2.    The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the National Disaster
Management Authority (NDMA) organized a two-day workshop on
sensitization of Nodal Officers for Disaster Management in Central
Ministries/Departments, in New Delhi. Around 120 senior level
officers attended the workshop from Ministries / Department of the
Central Government, disaster management specialists, technical
institutions and premium training institutes including NDMA, National
Institute of Disaster Management and National Disaster Response
Force.

3.  During the month, advance release of Rs.1200 crore to the
State Government of Karnataka, Rs.600 crores to the State
Government of Maharashtra and Rs.400 crores to the State
Government of Bihar was made from SDRF/NDRF.

4.    On 14.10.2019, Union Home Secretary wrote letter to Chief
Secretary, Maharashtra for taking necessary measures for incident free
elections in the State.

5.   An amount of Rs.34.59 crore was released to LWE affected
States of Jharkhand and West Bengal as reimbursement under the
Security Related Expenditure scheme. An amount of Rs.17.16 crore was
released to CAPFs for carrying out various civic activities under the
scheme of Civic Action Programme in LWE affected areas.

6.    An advisory was issued to the State Government / CAPFs to
sensitize them on activities of Left Wing Extremists in the LWE
affected areas.

7.   72 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States viz.
Telangana, Bihar, Jharkhand, Arunanchal Pradesh, Manipur, Uttar
Pradesh, Delhi, and Punjab for maintaining law and order duty during
Friday Prayers, Dusshera/ Durga Puja Festival, Chehallum Festival,
Dipawali /Kalipuja, Chhath, Tawang Festival and Run for Unity etc .
8.   On the recommendations of Election Commission of India, 777
Coys of CAPFs were deployed in connection with Election duties in
Arunachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Tamilnadu, Odisha, Sikkim,
Puducherry, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya,
Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Bihar, Kerala, Assam, Gujarat, Telangana,
Haryana, Maharashtra and Jharkhand.

9. An amount of Rs.160.59 crore has been sanctioned for
development of infrastructure to the CAPF. An amount of Rs. 1.52 crore
has been sanctioned as Ex-gratia Compensation to the NOKs of CAPFs in
7 cases.

10. On 31st October, 2019, 160 officials of various States
Police/CAPFs/CPOs have been awarded "Union Home Minister's
Special Operation Medal" for the year 2019.

11. During October, 2019, sanction for prosecution for filing the charge
sheet against 38 accused persons was accorded under the Unlawful
Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 and CrPC.

12. 25 posts in the National Human Rights Commission has been
created during the month.

13. Rs. 155.37 crore has been released under the Umbrella Scheme for
Modernization of Police forces during the month.


14. During the month more than 1695 kgs of Narcotics substances and
Rs.28.32 lakhs have been seized. 47 persons including one foreign
national were arrested for their involvement in drug trafficking.

15. During the month, an amount of Rs.46 crore was released to the
State Government of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and
Uttarakhand under the Border Area Development Programme
(BADP). The Total fund released under BADP during the current financial
year (2019-20) as on 31.10.2019 is Rs.540.83 crore.

16. During the month, five State Bills were assented to by the Honble
President of India. These are "The Orissa Ground Water (Regulation,
Development & Management) Bill, 2011", "The Indian Stamp (Jharkhand
Amendment) Bill, 2018", "The Gujarat Control of Terrorism and organized
Crime Bill, 2015", "Industrial Dispute (Bihar Amendment) Bill, 2018" and
"The Maharashtra Media Persons and Media Institutions (Prevention of
Violence and Damage or Loss to Property Bill, 2017".
