docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, September 2019
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
        and important events for the month of September, 2019.

      On 24.09.2019, Hon'ble Home Minister launched the 'Private
Security Agency Licensing Portal' relating to issue of online license to private
security agencies. The Portal provides for common platform for making
online applications and issue of licenses/renewal of licenses for all
States/UTs. Antecedents check is done online through ICJS, and facility
of online payment of fees has been made available by integration of
payment gateway of all States/UTs. E-sign and geo-tagging features have
also been provided on the Portal.

2.    On 24.09.2019, Hon'ble Minister of State, Shri G. Kishan
Reddy launched the public awareness Media Campaign for hiring licensed
Private Security Agency only.

3.    On 17.09.2019, Union Home Secretary wrote a letter to the
Chief Secretary, Chhattisgarh for taking necessary measures for
incident free elections in Dantewada.

4.     On 04.09.2019, Maulana Masood Azhar, Hafiz Muhammad Saeed,
Zakir-ur-Rehman Lakhvi and Dawood Ibrahim Kaskar were declared as
individual terrorists and their names added to Schedule 4 of the Unlawful
Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.


5.    During September 2019, sanction for prosecution for filing the charge
sheet against 10 accused persons was accorded to NIA under section 45(1)
of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 and section 196 of CrPC.

6.    5th Meeting of the Monitoring Committee on the Bru
Repatriation was held on 06.09.2019 at New Delhi under the
Chairmanship of Special Secretary (IS), MHA to discuss issues relating
to repatriation of Brus from Tripura to Mizoram.

7.    In the 24th Sectoral Level Meeting between India and Myanmar,
held on 23 -24th September, 2019 at Myanmar, cooperation on internal
security, management of international borders, cooperation in prevention of
Drug Trafficking, Wildlife smuggling and issues of mutual concerns were
discussed.

8.    Cyber Crisis Management Plan (CCMP) of the Ministry of Home Affairs
released on 10.09.2019.
9.    On 20-09-2019, the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Tribunal
confirmed Government decision to declare the Jammu and Kashmir
Liberation Front (Mohd. Yasin Malik Faction) (JKLF-Y) an unlawful
association under the provisions of the Unlawful Activities
(Prevention) Act, 1967.

10. During September 2019, 51 persons including 17 foreign
nationals were arrested for their involvement in drug trafficking. More
than 4698 kg of Narcotic substance was seized.

11. A meeting of the Project Clearance Committee (PCC) was held under
the Chairmanship of Special Secretary (IS) on 16.09.2019 to approve the
Proposal/ Action Plan of Governments of Andhra Pradesh,
Chhattisgarh and Kerala under the Special Infrastructure Scheme, including
construction of 250 fortified police stations.

12. An amount of Rs. 66.17 crore was released to LWE affected States
as reimbursement under the Security Related Expenditure scheme. An
amount of Rs 580 crore was released to LWE affected States under the
Special Central Assistance (SCA) scheme for 30 most LWE affected
districts.
13. 56 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States viz
Telangana, Delhi, Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Madhya
Pradesh, Maharastra, Karnataka, Punjab, Chandigarh for maintaining law
and order duty during Friday Prayer, Ganesh Festival and Muharrum,
DUSU Election, visit of VVIPs, law and order duties at Saharanpur and
NTRO, Bhopal (MP).

14. On the recommendations of Election Commission of India, 144 Coys of
CAPFs were deployed in connection with election duties in Uttar
Pradesh, Kerala, Chhattisgarh, Tripura, Haryana and Maharashtra.


15. During the month, an amount of Rs.23.59 Crore for acquisition of land
and Rs. 160.59 Crore for development of infrastructure were sanctioned to
the CAPFs.

16. An amount of Rs.61.43 Crore was released under the Umbrella Scheme
for Modernization of Police Forces during the month.
17. During the month, an amount of Rs.267.36 Crore was released under
BADP to the State Governments of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam,
Gujarat, Jammu and Kashmir, Rajasthan and Tripura.
18. During the month, three State Bills were assented by the Honble
President of India. These are: 'The Bengaluru Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
School of Economics University Bill, 2018', The Jharkhand
University of Technology (Amendment) Bill, 2018' and The Tamil Nadu
Agricultural Produce and Livestock Contract Farming 85 Services
(Promotion &Facilitation) Bill, 2019'.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, August 2019
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
          and important events for the month of August, 2019.

     A declaration was issued under article 370(3) of the Indian
Constitution, thereby making all clauses of article 370 cease to be
operative and applying all provisions of the Indian Constitution to
Jammu and Kashmir without any modifications or exceptions
notwithstanding anything contained in the Constitution to Jammu and
Kashmir.

2. The Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order,
2019 was issued under article 370(1) which applied all provisions of the
Constitution of India without any exceptions and modifications, thereby
removing article 35A and other Constitutional ambiguities in relation to
Jammu and Kashmir.

3. During the month, the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization
Bill, 2019 was passed by the Parliament and assented by the
President of India, reorganising the existing State of Jammu and
Kashmir into successor Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir with
Legislature and successor Union Territory of Ladakh without
Legislature. The Central Government has notified the "appointed day"
as 31st October 2019 for purpose of the Reorganization Act. Before
the appointed day comes into force, certain actions are to be
taken by various Departments of Government of India and the State
Government of Jammu and Kashmir. For this purpose all
Ministries/Departments have been requested to designate Nodal
Officers to complete all the actions that are required to be taken by
them as per the provisions of the Act under intimation to MHA.

4.   7thMeeting of the India-Bangladesh Home Minister Level Talks (HMLT)
was held on 07.08.2019 at New Delhi. The HMLT was co-chaired by
Union Home Minister and Mr. Asaduzzaman Khan, Minister for Home
Affairs of Bangladesh. In the meeting, various security related issues
and mutual cooperation between the two countries including
confidence building measures etc. were discussed.

5.    A Delegation, led by Hon'ble Minister for Home Affairs &
Minister for Law of the Republic of Singapore, Mr. K Shanmugam, met Gol
Delegation, led by Hon'ble Home Minister on 31st August, 2019 in New
Delhi, to discuss the bilateral relations between the two nations.

6.   During the Financial Year 2019-20, the State Government of
J&K has been reimbursed Rs. 540.00 crore under SRE(Police) and Rs
159.76 crore under SRE(R&R). Under the ongoing scheme for giving
financial assistance to Displaced Persons from PoJK and Chhamb, Rs
133.10 crore has been disbursed, so far.
7.    The National Investigation Agency (Amendment) Act, 2019 and
the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Amendment Act, 2019 were passed
by the Parliament during Monsoon Session and provisions of these Acts
came into force w.e.f. 2" August, 2019 and 14th August, 2019 respectively.

 8. Sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet against 7
 accused persons was accorded under the Unlawful Activities
 (Prevention) Act, 1967 for terrorist and anti-national activities.

 9. A citizen centric Cyber Crime Reporting Portal www.cybercrime.gov.in
 was made operational on 30.08.2019 to enable citizens to report
 complaints pertaining to Cyber crime with special focus on Cyber-crime
 against Women and Children without visiting Police Station.

10. The Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) was declared an
 unlawful association under the provisions of the Unlawful Activities
(Prevention) Act, 1967 on 27th August, 2019.

11. The Jamaat-e-Islami (Jel), Jammu and Kashmir was declared an
unlawful association under the provisions of the Unlawful Activities
(Prevention) Act, 1967 on 30th August, 2019.

12. The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 was notified on
1st August, 2019, which came into force from 2nd August, 2019.

13. During the month, in 28 cases, 66 persons including 07 foreign nationals
(one Suriname & one Nigerian and five Afghani) have been arrested for
their involvement in drug trafficking. More than 3,649 Kg of narcotic
substances have been seized.

14. A tripartite Memorandum of Settlement (MoS) between the
Government of India, Government of Tripura and National Liberation Front of
Twipra led by Sh. Sabir Kumar Debbarma (NLFT/SD) was signed on
10.08.2019. As per MoS, NLFT(SD) has agreed to abjure the path of
violence, join mainstream and abide by the Constitution of India. As a
result, its 88 cadres surrendered with 44 arms in a surrender ceremony
held on 13.8.2019.

15. The 2nd meeting of Multi Disciplinary Committee constituted for
development of Eastern Nagaland was held on 16.08.2019 under the
Chairmanship of Special Secretary (Internal Security), MHA at New Delhi.

16. Suspension of Operation (SoO) agreements with KNO (Kuki National
Organization) and UPF (United Progressive Front) of Manipur have been
extended for six more months till 29.02.2020.
17. On 26.08.2019, a meeting was held under the Chairmanship of Hon'ble
Home Minister with the Chief Ministers of all the LWE affected States
and Union Ministers of concerned Union Ministries to review LWE situation
and the status of the issues related to Security and development in these
States.

18. In the month of August, Union Home Secretary shared the half-yearly
review of LWE scenario in their State with the Governments of Andhra
Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha and tri-junction of Maharashtra-
Madhya Pradesh-Chhattisgarh with the Government of Maharashtra.

19. During the month of August, 2019 an amount of Rs. 5109.00 Iakh has
been released to the State Government of Bihar under BADP. The total fund
released under BADP during the Current Financial Year (2019-20) (as on
31.08.2019) is Rs. 22747.81 lakh.

20. Establishment of an International Coalition for Disaster Resilient
Infrastructure (CDRI) approved and it will be launched by Hon'ble Prime
Minister on 23rd September, 2019 in the Climate Action Summit to be held in
New York.

21. The High Level Committee chaired by Union Home Minister met in New
Delhi on 19th August, 2019 and approved the additional Central Assistance
from National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) of Rs. 4432.10 crore to 3
States viz. Rs. 1029.39 crore to Karnataka (drought-rabi). Rs. 64.49 Crore to
Himachal Pradesh (avalanches hailstorms, landslides) and Rs. 3338.00 crore
to Odisha (cyclone-Fani).

22. Hon'ble President of India conferred Bharat Ratna on Shri Nanaji
Deshmukh (Posthumously), Dr. Bhupendra Kumar Hazarika (Posthumously)
and Shri Pranab Mukherjee in an Investiture Ceremony held at Rashtrapati
Bhawan, New Delhi on 8th August, 2019.

23. During the month, five State Bills were assented by the Hon'ble President
of India. These are: The Gujarat Agriculture Land Ceiling (Amendment) Bill,
2019', The Tamil Nadu Private Schools (Regulation) Bill, 2018', 'The Tripura
Industries (Facilitation) Bill, 2018', 'The Right to Fair Compensation and
Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Tamil
Nadu Second Amendment) Bill, 2014' and The Registration (Andhra Pradesh
Amendment) Bill, 2019'.

24. 03 President's Police Medal for Gallantry, 177 Police Medal for
Gallantry, 89 President's Police Medal for Distinguished Service & 680 Police
Medal for Meritorious Service were awarded to the State/UTs/CAPFs
Officers/Personnel on the occasion of Independence Day - 2019.
25. Prime Minister's Police Medal for Life Saving for the year -2018 were
awarded to 14 Police personnel of various States Police/ Organisations.


26. 96 Police Personnel of various States/UTs/CPOs were awarded "Union
Home Minister's Medal for Excellence in Investigation" for the year 2019.
"Union Home Minister's Medal for Excellence in Police Training" for the
year 2017-18 were awarded to 245 trainers of various Police Training
Institutions.

27. A sum of Rs.52.38 crore to Govt. of Chattisgarh and Rs. 3.3 crore to
Himachal Pradesh was reimbursed for raising IR Bns.

28. Total Number of 88 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in Telangana,
Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi, Chandigarh, Assam,
Dadra and Nagar Haveli, for maintaining law and order duty during Friday
Prayer, Bakrid festival. Independence Day Celebration, wake of
abrogation of Article 370, Shri Krishna Janmashtami Festival and
Muhrram Festival, security duty of Jails in Haryana, visit of VVIPs. 930
Commandos of CAPFs were provided to Delhi Police for security
arrangements during Independence Day Celebrations - 2019.

29. Amendment to the Para 8 of the Schedule appended to the
Citizenship (Regulation of Citizens and Issue of National Identity Cards)
Rules, 2003 was notified on 01.08.2019 for increasing time limit for filing
of appeal in Foreigners Tribunal to 120 days from 60 days.

30. As per the directions contained in Hon'ble Supreme Court Order
dated 13.08.2019 passed in WP(C) 274/2009, the NRC supplementary
list of inclusions has been published on 31.08.2019.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, July 2019
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
           and important events for the month of July, 2019.


       On 15.07.2019 the High Level Committee (HLC) has been reconstituted
 under the Chairmanship of Former Judge, Gauhati High Court for implementation
 of Clause 6 of the Assam Accord. The first meeting of the HLC was held on
 24.07.2019.

2.     The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Bill, 2019 to amend the
Protection of Human Right Act, 1993 was passed in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
on 19th July, 2019 and 22nd July, 2019 respectively. The Protection of Human Right
(Amendment) Act, 2019 was published in the Gazette of India on 27th July, 2019.

3.     Union Home Secretary held a meeting on 02.07.2019 to discuss the
issue of illegal immigrants in Nagaland. The meeting was attended by Dy. NSA,
Director (IB), Special Secretary (Internal Security), Chief Secretary of Nagaland, RGI
and other senior officers of MHA.

4.     A Delegation, led by Ms. P. Michou, Director General for the
Directorate General of Migrations, Home Affairs and Citizenship, European
Union, met the Gol Delegation, led by Secretary (BM), on 10th July, 2019 in New Delhi,
to discuss Strategic Cooperation on Cybercrime.

5.     A Parliamentary Delegation of Commission-I (Law, Politics and
Government) of the House of Representatives of Aceh, Indonesia, led by Mr. Azhari
Sip, met Gol Delegation led by Special Secretary (CS) on 15th July, 2019 in New
Delhi, to discuss issues concerning democratic system in India, Centre-State relations,
good governance, public service and administrative reforms.

6.    Civil List 2019 of the Indian Police Service was published during the
month.

7.     In the meeting of the Central Police Awards Committee (CPAC) on 26.07.2019, 188
recommendations for President's Police Medal (PPM) for Distinguished Service, 1141
recommendations for Police Medal (PM) for Meritorious Service, 77 Cases for President's
Police Medal for Gallantry (PPMG)/ Police Medal for Gallantry (PMG) were considered.

8.     Union Home Secretary chaired a meeting of the Sub-Committee of National
Executive Committee (SC-NEC) on 22nd July, 2019 to consider the report of the Inter-
Ministerial Central Team on damage caused by Cyclone "Fani" of 2019.
9.     The NDRF personnel carried out rescue and relief in the area of deployment in
co-ordination with State authority and rescued 33 personal and evacuated 16071 personnel
during the month.

10.    Sanction has been issued for creation of 106 posts in CISF for the purpose of
induction in the Fire Wing.

11.    181 Coys and 2 bomb disposal dog squad of CAPFs were deployed in the States
of Arunachal Pradesh, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana, Delhi, Uttarakhand,
Jammu and Kashmir for maintaining law and order duties, Car festival of Lord Shree
Jagannath at Puri, visit of VVIP at Varanasi district, Shrawan Mas Shivratri festival,
Friday prayer at Hyderabad, Ghatam Procession, Sri Ujjaini Mahakali Jathara, Bonalu
festival, Kanwaria Pilgrimage, Independence Day Celebration, Kanwar Mela at
Haridwar. 47 additional Covs of CAPFs has also been deployed in the States of Tamil
Nadu, Odisha and Tripura for election related duties.

12.     During the month an amount of Rs. 131.71 crore has been sanctioned for
acquisition of land and Rs 95.33 crore has been sanctioned for development of
infrastructure to the CAPFs.

13.    An amount of Rs. 12.40 crore has been sanctioned as Ex-gratia Compensation
to the NOKs of CAPFs in 41 cases.

14.    Sanction for prosecution for filling the charge sheet against 38 accused persons
was accorded under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 for terrorist and anti-
national activities.

15    On 02.07.19, Union Home Secretary held a meeting with the Chief
Secretaries and Director Generals of Police of LIVE affected States, Director Generals
of CAPFs and IB to review the LWE scenario.

16.    A meeting was held under the Chairmanship of Secretary (BM) on 18.07.19 with the
Department of Telecommunications, and the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting to
review the implementation of the various developmental schemes in the LWE affected
areas.

17.    A meeting of the Project Clearance Committee (PCC) was held under the
Chairmanship of Special Secretary (IS) on 10.07.19 to discuss the Proposal/ Action Plan
of the Government of Uttar Pradesh and Kerala under the 'Special Infrastructure Scheme,
including construction of 250 Fortified Police Stations' in the LWE affected States.

18.    An advisory was issued to the State Government / CAPFs to sensitize them
on activities of Left Wing Extremists in the LWE affected areas.
19. During the month, an amount of Rs 14668.33 lakh has been released to the
State Governments of Assam, Mizoram, Nagaland, Meghalaya and West Bengal
under Border Area Development Programme (BADP). The total fund released under BADP
during the Current financial year (2019-20) as on 31.07.2019 is Rs 17638.81 lakh.

20.    During the month, an amount of Rs 32.48 crore in total has been released to the
States of Mizoram, Kerala, Tripura, Nagaland, Chhattisgarh and Bihar under the
relevant sub-schemes of the umbrella scheme of Modernization of Police Forces.

21.   e-Visa facility has been extended to Benin and Belarus Nationals.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, June 2019
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
           and important events for the month of June, 2019.


        Hon'ble Home Minister, Shri Amit Shah chaired a high level
meeting on 11.06.2019 of State and Central Ministries/Agencies
concerned to review the preparedness to deal with the situation arising
out of Cyclone VAYU'.

2    A Memorandum of Understanding between National Security
Guards (NSG) and National Guards of the Armed Forces of the Kyrgyz
Republic was signed on 14.06.2019 during Hon'ble Prime Minister's visit to
Kyrgyz Republic.

 3.   Union Home Secretary wrote to the Chief Secretaries of
 Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh,
 Maharashtra, Odisha, Telangana, Kerala and West Bengal to have a
 detailed review of LWE scenario with their Director Generals of Police
 and other Officers.

 4.  Secretary (BM) held a meeting on 17.06.19 with the Nehru Yuva
 Kendra Sangathan to discuss the revised proposal for 12th Tribal Youth
 Exchange Program under Media Plan for LWE affected areas.

 5.   A meeting was held under Special Secretary(IS) on 20.06.19 with
 CRPF, Department for Promotion of Industry & Internal Trade and the
 Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organization to discuss monitoring
 and control over explosives by using technology to prevent leakage and
 misuse.

6.   An amount of Rs. 93.66 crore was released to LWE affected States as
reimbursement under the Security Related Expenditure Scheme.

7.    03 advisories were issued to the State Government / CAPFs to
sensitize them on activities of Left Wing Extremists in the LWE affected
areas.

8.    The President of India gave assent to 3 State Bills namely, The Code
of Criminal Procedure (Uttar Pradesh Amendment) Bill, 2018, The Industrial
Disputes (The Tamil Nadu Amendment) Bill, 2018 and The PEPSU
Tenancy and Agriculture Lands (Haryana Amendment) Bill, 2017.

9.   Sanction for prosecution for filling the charge sheet against 44
accused persons was accorded under the Unlawful Activities
(Prevention) Act, 1967 for terrorist and anti-national activities.
10. Rs. 10.71 crore has been released towards Assistance to State for
Modernization of Police.

11. For disseminating the Information Security Best Practices, a
booklet has been released and made available on MHA website.

12. 106 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Punjab,
Telangana, Bihar, Jharkhand, Gujarat, Odisha, Jammu and Kashmir for
Al vida ki Namnz and Id-Ul-Fitra, law and order duties in Ayodhya,
security arrangements in the context of swearing-in ceremony of Hon' ble
Prime Minister of India, security of outer periphery of the Parliament.
During Parliament Session from 16.06.2019 till conclusion of the
Parliament Session, law and order duties in connection with the
International Day of Yoga, Ghallughara Week in Punjab, Friday Prayer
in Hyderabad City, Annual Jagannath Rathyatra (Car festival), and
Sindhu Darshan festival in Leh.

13. Rs. 315.21 Crore has been sanctioned for development of
infrastructure to the CAPF.

14. An amount of Rs. 2970.48 lakh has been released to the State
Governments of Mizoram and Nagaland under BADP.

15. On 24th June 2019, Cabinet approved the proposal to re-
introduce the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Bill, 2019 to
amend the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.


16. 4th Meeting of Monitoring Committee to coordinate for
implementation of the Agreement signed on 3.7.2019 for repatriation of
Bru families from Tripura to Mizoram was held under Special Secretary
(IS), on 28.06.2019 at New Delhi.

17. The whole State of Nagaland has been declared as 'disturbed area'
under the Armed Forces Special Power Act, 1958 vide Notification No. S.O.
2261(E) dated 30.6.2019 for a period of six months w.e.f. 30.06.2019.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, May 2019
pages:
¥

Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant
Development and important events for the month of May, 2019.

The President of India gave assent to 7 State Bills namely, The Tamil
Nadu Forest (Amendment) Bill, 2017; The Criminal Law (Tripura
Amendment) Bill, 2018; The Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board Bill,
2018; The Code of Criminal Procedure (Andhra Pradesh Amendment)
Bill, 2018; The Rajasthan Apartment Ownership Bill, 2015; The
Bengal, Agra and Assam Civil Courts (Jharkhand Amendment) Bill,
2018 and The Dowry Prohibition (Bihar Amendment) (Repeal) Bill,
2018.

2. Union Home Secretary held a meeting of the Development
Investment Board on 6.5.2019 for appraisal of the Project
regarding creation of IT Automation of Foreigner Tribunal (FTs) by
developing e-FT application for detection, detention and deportation of
illegal migrants.

3. Union Home Secretary wrote to the Chief Secretaries of Andhra
Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh,
Maharashtra, Odisha and Telangana to set up a formal arrangement to
enquire into the incidents resulting in security forces/political
casualties that occur due to avoidable oversight.

4. Approval for setting up 400 additional Foreigners Tribunals in
Assam was granted to Government of Assam on 13.5.2019.

5. The Consultant Group (CG) meeting of Global Facility for Disaster
Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR) of the 6th Session of the Global
Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction (GPDRR) 2019 was held in
Geneva on 14.05.2019. In the meeting, India has been unanimously
chosen to co-chair Consultative Group (CG) of Global Facility of
Disaster Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR) for fiscal year 2020.

6. Jamaat-ul-Mujhahideen Bangladesh or Jamaat-ul-Mujhahideen
India or Jamaat-ul-Mujhahideen Hindustan and all its manifestations’
have been listed as terrorist organization involved in terrorism, in the
First Schedule to the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967

7. Sanction for prosecution for filling the charge sheet against 12
accused persons was accorded under the Unlawful Activities
(Prevention) Act, 1967 for terrorist and anti-national activities.

8. The adjudication report of the UAPA Tribunal regarding
declaration of NLFT and ATTF and Metei Organizations of Manipur as
Unlawful Association has been published in the Gazette of India.

9, A meeting was held on 30.5.2019 with officers of Nehru Yuva
Kendra Sangathan and CAPFs to discuss the proposal for 12th Tribal
Youth Exchange Program (TYEP) under Media Plan scheme.

10. 04 Advisories were issued to the State Government/ CAPFs to
sensitize them on activities of Left Wing Extremists in the LWE affected

areas.

11. During the month, Narcotics Control Bureau seized large
quantities of heroin, ganja, opium, cocaine and other narcotics and
arrested 91 persons including 7 foreign nationals in connection with

drugs trafficking.

12. An amount of Rs 765.29 crore has been sanctioned for
development of infrastructure to the CAPFs.

13. Sanctions have been issued for creation of 5524 posts in CISF
during the month.

14. A total of 233.38 km of Indo Nepal Border Roads were completed till
the end of May, 2019.

15. Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar Airport, Indore has been notified as an
authorized Immigration Check Post.(ICP) on 27.5.2019.

16. In pursuance of Supreme Court's Order dated 14.03.2019, I held a
meeting on 16.05.2019 with the Chief Secretaries of Bihar and
Jharkhand to discuss the issues of apportionment of pension liabilities

between the two States.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, April 2019
pages:
*

Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
and important events for the month of April, 2019.

A meeting of the High Level Committee (HLC) was held under the Chairmanship
of Hon’ble Home Minister on 15.04.2019 for Central Assistance to the States of Assam
for flood/landslide of 2018.

2. On 28.02.2019, the union Cabinet approved the proposal for signing of a
Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the National Crime Records Bureau
(NCRB), India and the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC),
USA regarding receiving of Tipline report on online child pornography and child sexual
exploitation contents from NCMEC. The MoU was signed on 26.04.2019.

x On 03.04.2019, Union Home Secretary reviewed the LWE scenario of the
country with the Intelligence Bureau.

4. On 04.04.19, Union Home Secretary held a Video Conference with Additional
Chief Secretaries (Home) Principal Secretaries (Home) of LWE affected states along
with officers of implementing Ministry to review physical/ financial progress of ‘Road
Connectivity Project in LWE affected areas’.

5. In pursuance of Supreme Court’s Order dated 14.03.2019, Home Secretary held
a meeting on 26.04.2019 with the Chief Secretaries of Bihar and Jharkhand to discuss
the issues of apportionment of pension liabilities between the two States.

6. Secretary (BM), MHA held a meeting on 10.04.2019 to discuss the proposal of
Government of Assam for creation of e-Foreigners Tribunal and creation of 1000
additional Foreigners Tribunal.

t A meeting to review implementation of provisions of A.P. Reorganization Act,
2014 was held by Special Secretary (CS) on 12.04.2019, with the representatives of all
the concerned Ministries and both the State Governments.

8. Special Secretary (IS), MHA held a meeting with NSCN/K-Khango faction on
15.04.2019 at New Delhi. A new Ceasefire Agreement was signed for one year with
NSCN/K-Khango faction w.e.f. 15.04.2019 to 14.04.2020.
9. Tirap, Changlang and Longding districts of Arunachal Pradesh and the areas
falling within the jurisdiction of 4 Police Stations in the districts of Arunachal Pradesh,
bordering the State of Assam have been declared as ‘disturbed area’ under Section 3 of
the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 for a further period of six months w.e.f.
01.4.2019 to 30.9.2019 vide Notification No. S.O. 1494 (E) dated 01.04.2019.

10. Secretary (BM) held meetings of Security Related Expenditure (SRE) Standing
Committee to finalize Annual Work Plans 2019-20 with Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Madhya
Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Maharashtra and
Odisha, during the month.

11. An amount of Rs. 4.31 crore was sanctioned as ex-gratia compensation to the
NOKs of CAPFs in 16 cases.

12. An amount of Rs. 25.05 crore was sanctioned for acquisition of land and Rs
118.95 crore was sanctioned for development of infrastructure to the CAPFs.

13. A total Number of 58 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States for Chaitra
Navratra, Dr.BhimraoAmbedkarJayanti,for maintaining law and order duties during visit
of VVIP at Prayagraj, Amroha, Ayodhya and other cities, Friday Prayer, Shab-E-Miraj,
Shri Ramnavami, Shri Hanuman Jayanthi, Shab-E-Barat, Security of Parliament House.

14. On the recommendation of Election Commission of India a total of 24 coys of
CAPFs were ordered for deployment in the states of Tamil Nadu, Goa, Karnataka in
connection with Bye- Election related duties alongwith VII phase of General election to
Lok Sabha, 2019.

15. | Sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet against 19 accused persons
was accorded under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 for terrorist and anti-
national activities.

16. During the month, Narcotics Control Bureau seized large quantities of heroin,
ganja, opium, cocaine and other narcotics and arrested 28 persons including 05 foreign
nationals in connection with drugs trafficking.
17. The President of India gave assent to 2 State Bills namely the Gujarat
Ownership Flats (Amendment) Bill, 2018 and the Criminal Law (Gujarat Amendment)
Bill, 2018 during the month.

18. Advisories were issued to the State Government / CAPFs to sensitize them on

activities of Left Wing Extremists in the LWE affected areas.

19. CCTNS software has been deployed in 14841 Police Stations across the country
and 14788 Police Stations are entering 100% FIRs through CCTNS.

20. Two days Data Users Conference for Census 2021 was held on 9-10" April,
2019 to take views of all stakeholders on various aspects related to Census.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, March 2019
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
and important events for the month of March, 2019.

Union Home Secretary reviewed the LWE situation in Bihar, Andhra Pradesh,
Kerala-Karnataka-Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra-Madhya Pradesh Chhattisgarh tri-
junction and shared the reviews with the Chief Secretaries.

2. He also wrote letters to Director Generals of Police of the LWE affected states and
the Director Generals of CAPFs regarding the ongoing Tactical Counter Offensive of CPI
(Maoist) and the need to adhere to the laid down SOPs in view of the ongoing
Parliamentary Elections.

3. Secretary (BM) held a_ video-conference to review the progress of
developmental/flagship schemes in the LWE affected areas with the representatives of
the states and Ministry of Skill Development & the Ministry of Road Transport.

4. Special Secretary (IS) took a meeting with CRPF, Department for Promotion of
Industry and Internal Trade, Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organization and other
stakeholders regarding monitoring and control over explosives by using technology to
prevent leakage and misuse.

5, Advisories were issued to the State Governments / CAPFs to sensitize them to
counter the LWE activities in the affected areas.

6. Union Home Secretary held a meeting of the Sub-Committee of National Executive
Committee (SC-NEC) for Central Assistance to the State of Assam for Flood during 2018.

7. The 3rd Indo-Japan Workshop on Disaster Risk Reduction was organized on
18.03.2019. It was attended by about 140 delegates from Japan and India. The objective
of the workshop was enhancing collaboration between research institutes, cities and the
private sector in the field of Disaster Risk Reduction.

8. The 2nd International Workshop on Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (IVW/DRI) was
held on 19-20 March, 2019. This was inaugurated by Dr. Rajeev Kumar, Vice-Chairman,
Niti Aayog The event brought together more than 200 participants from 33 national
governments, multilateral Development Banks, United Nations agencies, the private
sector and academia.

9. The Tripartite Talk among Government of India, Government of Manipur and
United Naga Council (UNC) was held at Senapati District Headquarters, Manipur on
09.03.2019.

10. The Sixth Joint Task Force between India and Bangladesh on prevention of
Human Trafficking was held on 11 -12th March, 2019 in New Delhi.

11. A meeting was held under the Chairmanship of Special Secretary (Internal
Security) on 26.03.2019 to discuss the issues of repatriation of Bru families from Tripura
to Mizoram.

12. For the first time, incentive funds of Rs. 7.69 crore each for implementation of
Police reforms have been released to 10 States, who have been found eligible viz. Andhra
Pradesh, Gujarat, Punjab, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh,
Uttrakhand and Uttar Pradesh.

13. High Powered Committee considered State Action Plans (SAPs), under Police
Modernization schemes, for 2019-20 during the Month of February and March. Out of 29
States, SAPs of 22 States have been approved. This is an achievement due to which
MHA is in a position to release funds to States in April itself.

14. The budget allocation for the financial year 2018-19 was Rs. 769 crore for Sub-
scheme of “Assistance to States for Modernization of Police”; against which Rs. 768.83
(100%) crore has been released. Also, the entire allocation of Rs. 100 crore for
“Assistance to the State Government for Special Project/Programmes for updating Police
Infrastructure; has been released.

45. Anamount of Rs. 79.75 crore was sanctioned for acquisition of land and Rs 155.77
crore was sanctioned for development of infrastructure to the CAPFs.

16. MHA has approved creation of 1719 posts of various ranks in the Battalions of
CRPF, BSF, CISF and SSB deployed in J &K, Left Wing Extremism affected areas and
NE Region during the year 2018-19 as a Pilot Project for augmentation/standardization
of standing strength of 10 and 20 Bed Hospitals of Battalions of CAPFs.

17. Atotal Number of 198 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States for Maha
Shiv Ratri festival, maintaining law and order duties during visit of VVIP, Holi festival and

also Friday Prayer in Hyderabad City.

48. An amount of Rs.1.45 crore was sanctioned as Ex-gratia Compensation to the
NOKs of CAPFs.

19. On the recommendation of Election Commission of India a total of 1512 coys of
CAPFs/SAPs/BWHGs from direct induction and 1198 Coys of CAPFs from existing

deployment were ordered for deployment in various states in connection with General

Parliament Election (GPE) — 2019.

20. A total of 219.94 km. of Indo Nepal Border Roads were completed till the end of

this month.

21. Anamount of Rs. 40 crore was released to Maharashtra and Odisha under Special

Central Assistance scheme.

22. An Amount of Rs. 9.08 crore was released to Government of Andhra Pradesh for

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, February 2019
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant
Development and important events for the month of February, 2019.

A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Republic of India
and the Korean National Police Agency of the Republic of Korea on combating
transnational crime and developing police cooperation was signed during the State
visit of Hon’ble Prime Minister of India to Seoul, Korea from 21-22 February, 2019.

2. The Union Home Minister Shri Rajnath Singh and Minister for Women and Child
Development, Smt. Maneka Sanjay Gandhi jointly launched the Women Safety
initiative of Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) in 16 States/UTs and
Mumbai city, on 19.2.2019. People in these states and UTs can now call a single pan
India number 112 for any emergency. In addition, Investigation Tracking System for

Sexual Offences (ITSSO) and Safe City Implementation Monitoring Portal were also
launched.

3. The Government approved the proposal to sign MoU between National Crime
Records Bureau and National Centre for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC)

USA for accessing tipline reports pertaining to child pornography for investigation and
prosecution of offenders.

4. A Secretary level meeting on Border Management and Security between India
and Bhutan was held during 14 -16 February, 2019 in Thimpu (Bhutan).

5, On 27.02.2019, 101 medal for Union Home Minister's Medal for Excellence in

Investigation was announced for the year 2018. These include 12 women police
officers.

6. Central Government has listed ‘Tehreek-ul-Mujahideen (TuM) and all its
manifestations’ as terrorist organization involved in terrorism in the First Schedule of
the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (37 of 1967) on 05.02.2019.

7. A meeting of Central Level Committee (CLC) was held under the chairmanship
of Special Secretary (Border Management) on 18.02.19 to review financial and

physical progress of works undertaken by States under Special Central Assistance
scheme.

8. A total of 216.24 km. of Indo Nepal Border Roads have been completed till the
end of this month.

9. Enhancement of Risk & Hardship Allowance to CAPFs personnel deployed in
the State of J& K and LWE Districts for Anti-naxal operations has been approved.

10. MHA vide letter dated 21.02.2019 conveyed approval of the competent authority
to allow non-entitled personnel of CAPF’s , AR and NSG to travel by air from Jammu
to Srinagar and back on official duty/transfer/tour and leave and also from Delhi to
Srinagar and back on official duty/transfer/tour.

141. An amount of Rs. 17.37 Crore has been sanctioned for acquisition of land and
Rs 650.62 Crore has been sanctioned for development of infrastructure to the CAPFs.
Further this Ministry has approved Rs.27 crore approx. for construction and
procurement of the various items under Swachhta Action Plan.

12, An amount of Rs.17.73 crore has been sanctioned as Ex-gratia Compensation
to the NOKs of CAPFs.

13. A total Number of 251 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States for
security of Parliament during Budget Session, maintaining law and order duties for
Friday Prayer in Hyderabad City, security arrangements during the visit of VVIP and
maintaining law and order at Mathura, Gautam Budh Nagar, Jhansi, Varansi,
Gorakhpur, Kumbh Mela, 12 AERO India Show 2019, Jharkhand; Dharna/protest
against Hon'ble LG of Puducherry and “Masi Magam” festival; and for maintaining law
and order from 22.2.2019 till further orders in J &K.

14. — Sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet against 31 accused persons
was accorded under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 for terrorist and
anti-national activities.

15. Instructions of the President for promulgation of the Andhra Pradesh (Andhra
Area) Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2018
have been conveyed to the State Government on 19.02.2019.

16. NOC has been issued for change in the name of village ‘Durjanpur’ as
‘Shivdham’ in District, Katni, Madhya Pradesh.

17. 02 advisories were issued to the State Government / CAPFs to sensitize them
to counter the LWE activities in the LWE affected areas.

18. Authorisation for Rs.195,95,23,594 and provisioning and expenditure sanction
for Rs.418,01,20,885 has been issued to the CAPFs for purchase of mine protected
vehicles, bullet proof vehicles & jackets, ambulance etc. Further, expenditure sanction
for Rs.16,84,24,459/- has been issued to NSG for purchase of 7 remotely operated
vehicle.

19. The National Register of Citizens (NRC) 1951 in Assam is being updated under
the provisions of Citizenship Act, 1955. The process of receipt of claims and objections
on the draft NRC has been completed on 31.12.2018. The verification process has
started from February 15, 2019. The final NRC will be published by 31.07.2019 after
the disposal of claims and objections as per the directions of the Hon'ble Supreme
Court of India.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, December 2018
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
and important events for the month of December, 2018.

A meeting of the High level Committee (HLC) was held under the Chairmanship of
Hon'ble Home Minister on 06.12.2018 and 17.12.2018 for Central Assistance to the
States of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha for being affected by Cyclone “Titli” and to the

State of Kerala for being affected by Flood; and to the State of Nagaland for being
affected by landslides in 2018.

Zo On 26.12.2018, a meeting of the Sub-Committee of National Executive Committee
(SC-NEC) was held under the Chairmanship of Union Home Secretary for Central
Assistance to the State of Tamil Nadu for Cyclone “Gaja”’.

3. The Committee set up under the Chairpersonship of Special Secretary (IS), MHA

to consider grant of ST status to six communities in Assam submitted its report on
28.12.2018 at New Delhi.

4. Vide Notification No. 6389 (E) dated 30.12.2018, entire State of Nagaland has
been declared as ‘disturbed area’ for a period of six months w.e.f. 30.12.2018 under
Section 3 of the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958.

oy A total Number of 74 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States for
maintaining law and order during Friday Prayer, Observance of Black Day, Mandala
Makaravilakku Festival, Sabrimala Temple, visit of VVIP, Dharam Sabha organized by
Vishwa Hindu Parishad at Ram Lila Ground, Delhi, Christmas Festival etc.

6. On the request of Government of Uttar Pradesh 70 Coys of CAPs and 10 Advance
Security Check Teams were ordered to be deployed for security arrangements during
Kumbh Mela 2019. On the request of Delhi Police 48 coys of CAPFs have been ordered

to be deployed for security arrangements in connection with Republic Day Celebration
2019.

Fs On the recommendation of Election Commission of India, 21 Coys order for
Retention/De-Induction of CAPFs were issued for Bye-Election’s EVM
Guarding/Counting duties at Gujarat, Jnarkhand Bye-Election.

8. On 26.12.2018, Central Government designated ‘Khalistan Liberation Force (KLF)
and all its manifestations’ as terrorist organisation by adding to the First Schedule of the
Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (37 of 1967).

9: The Government has approved the Scheme “Revamping of BADP” and its
continuation upto March 2020 with financial allocation of Rs. 3640 crore.

10. A total of 194.99 km. of Indo Nepal Border Roads have been completed till the end
of this month.

11. | The Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) has been constituted for advice on all
census related issues related to Census 2021.

12. The National Register of Citizens (NRC) 1951 in Assam is being updated under
the provisions of Citizenship Act, 1955 and the Citizenship (Registration of Citizens and
Issue of National Identity Cards) Rules, 2003. The applications for preparation of NRC in
Assam were invited in May-August, 2015 and after necessary scrutiny and verification,
the complete draft NRC has been published on 30.07.2018. The process of receipt of
claims and objections on the draft NRC has been completed on 31.12.2018. After the
disposal of claims and objections, the NRC is to be finalized as per the time lines
approved by the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India.

13. Ameeting of the SRE Standing Committee was held by Special Secretary (IS) on
11.12.18 to consider reimbursement of claims under the Security Related Expenditure
scheme for the year 2017-18.

14. An amount of Rs.27.35 crore was released to the States of Gujarat and Punjab
under the relevant sub schemes of the umbrella scheme for Modernization of Police
Forces, during the month.

15. During the month an amount of Rs.24.48 crore was released to the State
Governments of Manipur, Meghalaya and Nagaland. The total funds released under
Border Area Development Programme (BADP) for the financial year 2018 -19 (as on
31.12.2018) works out to be Rs.662.47 crore.

16. During the month an amount of Rs.4.65 crore approximately has been sanctioned
as ex-gratia compensation to the NOKs of CAPFs.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, November 2018
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
and important events for the month of November, 2018.

On 19.11.2018, a meeting of the High level Committee (HCL) was held under the

Chairmanship of Hon’ble Home Minister for Central Assistance to States of Karnataka for
Flood/Landslide-2018.

2. On 12.11.2018, agreement between the Republic of India and the Kingdom of
Morocco on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters was signed.

3. On 08.11.18, Union Home Secretary wrote letters to the Chief Secretary and
Director General of Police, Chhattisgarh regarding call by the CPI (Maoist) for boycott of
State Assembly Elections in Chhattisgarh.

4. On 19.11.18, Union Home Secretary wrote letters to Chief Secretary and Director
General of Police, Chhattisgarh and Director Generals of (CRPF, SSB, ITBP, BSF &

CISF) complimenting them for conduct of the first phase of State Assembly Elections
successfully.

5. Meeting of Monitoring Committee to review the status of implementation of
decisions taken under Agreed Text for Settlement signed between the Govt. of India, the
State Govt. of Meghalaya and ANVC (Achik National Volunteer Council) & ANVC/B was

held on 30.11.2018 at Shillong, Meghalaya under the Chairmanship of Chief Minister,
Meghalaya.

6. On 19.11.2018, Union Home Secretary held a tripartite meeting at New Delhi with
a delegation of Government of Assam, ABSU (All Bodo Students’ Union) and PJUACBM

(People's Joint Action Committee for Boroland Movement). The delegation also met the
Union Home Minister.

7. A Meeting of the Sub-Committee of National Executive Committee (SC-NEC) was
held under the Chairmanship of Home Secretary on 19.11.2018 for Central Assistance to

the States of Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Nagaland for Flood/landslides and Cyclone
“Titli” of 2018.

8. Vide Notification No. 5686(E) dated 13.11.2018, Meitei Extremist Groups of
Manipur, namely, Peoples’ Liberation Army (PLA), Revolutionary Peoples’ Front (RPF),
United National Liberation Front (UNLF), Manipur Peoples’ Army (MPA), Peoples’
Revolutionary Party of Kangleipak (PREPAK), Kangleipak Communist Party (KCP),
Kanglei Yaol Kanba Lup (KYKL), Coordination Committee (CorCom) and Alliance for
Socialist Unity Kangleipak (ASUK) have been declared as ‘Unlawful Associations’ under

Section 3 (1) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 from the date of publication
of notification.

9. A meeting with delegation of Eastern Naga People’s Organization (ENPO) and
Government of Nagaland was held on 14.11.2018 at New Delhi under the

Chairpersonship of Special Secretary (Internal Security), MHA to discuss demand of
ENPO.
10. A total Number of 76 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States for
maintaining law and order during Chehallum Festival, Dipawali, Goverdhan Pooja, Bhaiya
Dooj, Kali Puja, Chhath Puja Kartik Purnima, Barawvfat, Manipur Sangal Festival,
Mandala Makaravilakku Festival, Milad-Un-Nabi, Friday Prayer, Visit of VVIP, Election
Duty, All India Kisan Sangharsh and Parliament Duty etc.

11. On the recommendations of Election Commission of India, 40 coys of CAPFs were
deployed for Bye-Election in Karnataka State. Also, 2,265 coys of CAPFs were deployed
for Assembly Election in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Mizoram and
Telangana State. 15 CISF personnel were deployed on IS duty pattern at HSCL Office,
Kolkata.

12. The total funds released under Border Area Development Programme (BADP) till
the end of November works out to be Rs.637.98 crore, for the financial year 2018-19.

13. | Ahandbook titled 'A Handbook for Adolescent/Students on Cyber Safety' has been
published. The Handbook is for Adolescents/Students above 13 years of age and has
been prepared to provide an overview of various cyber threats that can impact children
and safeguards that can help in preventing cybercrimes. This handbook is meant to target
young students and to enable them to understand the cyber world better and prepare
themselves to be responsible cyber citizens of the future.

14. The President of India gave assent to 2 State Bills namely the Himachal Pradesh
Early Childhood Care and Education Centers (Registration & Regulation) Bill, 2017 and
the Tamil Nadu Vanniyakula Kshatriya Public Charitable Trusts and Endowments
(Protection and Maintenance) Bill, 2018 during the month.

15. Sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet against 17 accused persons
was accorded under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 for terrorist and anti
national activities.

16. Preparations towards Census 2021 are in progress. All necessary arrangements
for conducting a pilot survey for testing Questionnaires for Census 2021 have been made.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, October 2018
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
and important events for the month of October, 2018.

Union Home Minister held a meeting on 10.10.2018 to discuss the proposals of
the State Governments relating to grant of ST/SC status to various communities of
Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Maharashtra, UP, Himachal Pradesh, MP, Goa and Kerala.

2. A Government of People’s Republic of China (PRC) Delegation led by Mr.Zhao
Kezhi, Hon'ble Minister of Public Security met the Gol delegation led by Hon’ble Union
Home Minister on 22.10.2018 for the 1% High Level Meeting on Bilateral Security
Cooperation between Republic of India and People’s Republic of China. An “Agreement
on Cooperation “ between the two countries was signed.

3. The Union Home Minister met the then Prime Minister of Sri Lanka, Mr. Ranil
Wickremesinghe, on 19.10.2018. Matters of mutual interest concerning the two countries
were discussed.

4. On 08.10.2018, Shri Kiren Rijiju, MoS (H) held a meeting to discuss the status of
various issues relating to North Eastern Region.

5. The 22"¢ National Level Meeting between India and Myanmar took place on 25 —
26" October, 2018 under the Chairmanship of Union Home Secretary. The Myanmar
delegation was led by Major General Aung Thu, Deputy Minister, Ministry of Home
Affairs, Government of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar. In the meeting,
cooperation on internal security, management of international borders, cooperation in

prevention of Drug Trafficking, Wildlife smuggling and issues of mutual concerns were
discussed.

6. On 29.10.2018, Union Home Secretary held the 45" meeting of the High Level
Empowered Committee (HLEC).

7. National Liberation Front of Tripura (NLFT) and All Tripura Tiger Force (ATTF) of
Tripura have been declared as ‘Unlawful Associations’ under Section 3 (1) of the Unlawful
Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 vide Notification No. 5078 (E) dated 3.10.2018.

8. A Meeting of the Sub-Committee of National Executive Committee (SC-NEC) was
held under the Chairmanship of Union Home Secretary on 11.10.2018 for Central
Assistance to the State of Tripura and on 18.10.2018 for the State of Karnataka for
flood/landslides -2018.

9. The President of India gave assent to 4 State Bills namely the Gujarat Scheduled
Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other Backward Classes (Regulation of Issuance and
verification of caste certificates) Bill, 2018, the Tamil Nadu Forest (Amendment) Bill, 2018,
Gujarat Prevention of Fragmentation and Consolidation of Holdings (Amendment) Bill,
2018, the Code of Civil Procedure (Maharashtra Amendment) Bill, 2018 during the month.

10. A total number of 54 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States for

maintaining law and order during Dussehra Festivals and Friday Prayer, Moharrum, visit
of VVIP, at Satlok Aashram, Barwala, Hisar.

11. On the recommendations of ECI, 40 Coys of CAPFs were deployed for the Bye-
Election in Karnataka State. On the recommendations of ECI, 785 Coys of CAPFs were

deployed for Assembly Election in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Mizoram
and Telangana State.

12. 100ITBP Commandos were provided to Delhi Police during 19 — 215t October 2018
for security arrangements during the visit of VVIP in Delhi.

13. 04 advisories were issued to the State Government / CAPFs to sensitize them to
counter the LWE activities in LWE affected areas.

14. CCTNS software has been deployed at 14710 out of 14761 Police Stations across
the country excluding the State of Bihar, ie. 99.65%. Around 14659 Police Stations out

of 14761 Police Stations are entering 100% FIRs through CCTNS excluding State of
Bihar, ie.99.3%.

15. Data digitization of 3.89 crore records has been completed, i.e. 99.32% of the
total target.

16. Out of total outlay of the project of Rs.2000 crore, Rs.1802.5 crore have been
released till date to States/UTs and Central Agencies.

17. Extension of the Societies Registration (Goa, Daman & Diu First Amendment)
Act, 1979 and the Societies Registration (Goa Second Amendment) Act, 1998 to UT of
Dadra & Nagar Haveli was issued vide Notification dated 18.10.2018.

18. The complete draft National Register of Citizens (NRC) in Assam was published
on 30.07.2018 and Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for the next stage of the
exercise i.e. claims and objections was prepared by the Central Government in
consultation with the State Government, RGI and the State Coordinator and the same
was filed in the Hon’ble Supreme Court. The SOP filed by Union of India has been
approved by the Supreme Court vide its order dated 01.11.2018.

19. The process of receipt of claims and objections on draft NRC began from
25.09.2018 and will remain open upto 15.12.2018 in accordance with the directions of
Supreme Court. After digitization and compilation of all formalities and requirements,

notices will be issued by 15.01.2019 and verification process will commence from
01.02.2019.

20. NRC will be finalized only after the disposal of claims and objections and
timelines are approved by the Supreme Court.

KKKKK

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, September 2018
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
and important events for the month of September, 2018.

Union Home Minister held a meeting with the Chief Ministers of Assam,
Meghalaya, Mizoram and Tripura on 20.9.2018 at New Delhi to discuss the issues relating
to amendment of the Sixth Schedule, declaration of National Liberation Front of Tripura

(NLFT) and All Tripura Tiger Force (ATTF) as Unlawful Associations and repatriation of
Brus from Tripura to Mizoram.

2. On 12.09.2018, High Level Committee (HLC) Meeting was held under the
Chairmanship of Union Home Minister for Central Assistance to the States of

Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh for drought (Rabi) of 2017, Pest attacks and cyclone of
2017.

3. On 27.09.2018, approval for creation of National Disaster Response Force

Academy (NDRF Academy) at Nagpur by merging with it National Civil Defence College
(NCDC) at Nagpur was conveyed.

4. The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and Indian Space Research Organization
(ISRO), Department of Space signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on

20.09.2018 for setting up of a state-of-the-art Integrated Control! Room for Emergency
Response (ICR-ER).

5. The 2" Meeting of Monitoring Committee on Bru repatriation was held on

10.9.2018 at Aizwal (Mizoram) to discuss the issues relating to implementation of Bru
Agreement.

6. Tripartite talk among Government of India, Government of Manipur and United
Naga Council (UNC) was held at Senapati district in Manipur on 1.9.2018.

7. Tirap, Changlang and Longding districts of Arunachal Pradesh and the areas
falling within the jurisdiction of 8 Police Stations in the district of Arunachal Pradesh,
bordering the State of Assam have been declared as ‘disturbed area’ under Section 3 of
the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 for a further period of six months beyond
30.9.2018 upto 31.3.2019.

8. Union Cabinet approved signing of Mutual Cooperation in Combating lllicit
Trafficking in Narcotic Drugs Psychotropic Substances between India and Uzbekistan on
26.09.2018.

9. The President of India gave assent to 4 State Bills namely the Cigarettes & Other
Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement & Regulation of Trade & Commerce,
Production, Supply Distribution) (Punjab Amendment) Bill, 2018, the Cigarettes & Other
Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement & Regulation of Trade & Commerce,
Production, Supply Distribution) (Maharashtra Amendment) Bill, 2018, the Inter State
Migrants Workman (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) (Uttar Pradesh

Amendment) Bill, 2018 and the Indian Forest (Manipur Amendment) Bill, 2018 during the
month.

10. A total number of 481 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States for urban
local bodies/Panchayat Election related duties (J&K), maintaining law and order duties
during Janmashtami, Muharram, Ganesh Utsav festival, Friday Prayer and security
arrangements for visit of VVIPs.

11. During the month, Narcotics Control Bureau seized large quantities of heroin,
ganja, opium, cocaine and other narcotics and arrested 53 persons including 03 foreign

nationals in connection with drugs trafficking. Indian currency worth Rs. 23,31,760/- was
also seized.

12. Jammu Zone seized 60 kg Heroin, arrested 4 persons, recovered cash worth Rs.
22,49,400/- and seized 02 vehicles. It is the biggest seizure of Heroine this year by any

agency in India and exposed the nexus of drugs traffickers and foiled their attempts of
drugs smuggling.

13. Sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet against 23 accused persons

was accorded under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 for terrorist and anti
national activities.

14. During the month, an amount of Rs. 113.36 crore was released to the State
Government of Assam, Nagaland, Sikkim, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Uttrakhand. The total
funds released under Border Area Development Programme (BADP) so far during the
financial year 2018-19 works out to Rs.637.98 crore.

15. |The complete draft National Register of Citizen (NRC) in Assam was published on
30.07.2018 and Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for the next stage of the exercise
i.e. claims and objections have been prepared by the Central Government in consultation
with the State Government, RGI and the State Coordinator and the same has been filed
in the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India for its approval. On the direction of the Court, the
process of receipt of claims and objections has started from 25'? September, 2018 and
will be open for a period of 60 days upto 23 November, 2018. Next date for hearing the
matter for approval of SOP is fixed on 23.10.2018.

KKKK

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, August 2018
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
          and important events for the month of August, 2018.

        The President made the following appointments/ changes:

(i)     Shri Lal Ji Tandon as the governor of Bihar.
(ii)    Shri Satyadev Narayan Arya as the Governor of Haryana.
(iii)   Smt. Baby Rani Maurya as the Governor of Uttarakhand.
(iv)    Shri Satya Pal Malik, Governor of Bihar is transferred and appointed as Governor
        of Jammu & Kashmir.
(v)     Shri Ganga Prasad, Governor of Meghalaya was transferred and appointed as
        Governor of Sikkim.
(vi)    Shri Tathagata Roy, Governor of Tripura is transferred and appointed as
        Governor of Meghalaya.
(vii)   Shri Kaptan Singh Solanki, Governor of Haryana was transferred and appointed
        as Governor of Tripura.

2. On 02.08.2018, Union Home Secretary wrote letters to Chief Secretaries of
Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh and Bihar sharing the half yearly LWE
scenario in the States.
3. On 08.08.2018, Home Secretary wrote letters to Chief Secretaries of Kerala,
Karnataka and Tamil Nadu sharing half yearly LWE scenario in Kerala-Karnataka-
Tamil Nadu (KKT) tri-junction.
4.      Suspension of Operation (SoO) Agreements with Kuki National Organization
(KNO) and United People’s Front (UPF) of Manipur was extended for another one year
till 31.8.2019.

5.     The 1st Meeting of Monitoring Committee on Bru repatriation was held under the
Chairpersonship of Special Secretary(IS), MHA on 10.8.2018 at Damcherra in Tripura
to discuss the issues relating to implementation of Bru Agreement.

6.     On 09.08.2018, the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Bill, 2018 was
introduced in Lok Sabha to amend the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

 7.    The Umbrella Scheme Border Infrastructure and Management :(BIM) containing
 60 projects and with an outlay of Rs.8606 crore has been approved.

 8.     Powers of High Level Empowered Committee (HLEC) enhanced from Rs.100
 crore to 500 crore and the mandate of Technical Committee expanded to appraise the
 Technical projects.
9.     02 President’s Police Medal, 177 Police Medal, 88 President’s Police Medal and
675 Police Medal were awarded to the State/UTs/CAPFs/CPOs for Gallantry,
Distinguished Service and Meritorious Service on the occasion of Independence Day,
2018.

10.   Various Gallantry, Distinguished Service and Meritorious Service awards were
announced to the Fire Service, Home Guards and Civil Defence Personnel on the
occasion of Independence Day, 2018.

11.    A total number of 91 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States for
maintaining law and order duties and security arrangements for visit of VVIPs, Kanwaria
Pilgrimage, Annual Bonalu Festival, Bakrid Festival and Independence Day
Celebrations. 822 Commandos (CRPF, BSF, ITBP, CISF, SSB and NSG) had been
provided for Independence Day Celebration 2018.

12.   On the recommendations of the Election Commission of India, 8 Coys of CAPFs
were deployed for Bye-Election in Meghalaya.

13.    A Government of People’s Republic of China (PRC) Delegation met the Indian
Delegation on 28.08.2018 to hold discussions on the forthcoming visit of Hon’ble
Minister of Public Security of PRC and the proposed agreement on security cooperation
between the two countries.

14.   The President of India gave assent to 6 State Bills namely the Chhattisgarh
Ayurvigyan Parishad (Amendment) Vidheyak, 2016, the Industrial Disputes (Assam
Amendment) Bill, 2017, the Chhattisgarh Shops and Establishments (Regulation of
Employment and Conditions of Service) Bill, 2017, the Karnataka Good Samaritan and
Medical Professional (Protection and Regulation during Emergency Situations) Bill,
2016, the Motor Vehicles (Haryana Amendment) Bill, 2018 and the Telangana
Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas,
Immoral Traffic Offenders and Land Grabbers (Amendment) Bill 2017 during the month.

15.   The Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill, 2018 was also assented to by the Hon’ble
President on 11.08.2018.
16.    e-Visa, LSI and Biometric Enrolment Software has been operationalised in the 08
Indian Missions i.e Canada (Ottawa), Russia (St. Petersburg), Russia (Vladivostok),
Germany (Munich), Belgium (Brussels), Norway (Oslo), Hungry (Budapest) and Croatia
(Zagreb), making it to a total of 152 Missions out of 178 Missions abroad.
17.    Notification dated 13.08.2018 was issued declaring Zokhawthar Land Check
Post of Mizoram State as an Authorised Immigration Check Post (ICP) and appointment
of Superintendent of Police, Champhai District, Mizoram as the “Civil Authority”.
18.   An Order dated 02.08.2018 was issued specifying that a person registered as an
Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder under section 7 A of the Citizenship Act,
1955 shall be eligible for appointment as teaching faculty in Indian Institute of Science,
Bangalore and the new AIIMS set up by the Central Government under the Pradhan
mantra Swasthya Suraksha Yojana.
19.   CCTNS software has been deployed at 14677 out of 14747 Police Stations
across the country excluding the State of Bihar, i.e. 99.52%.
20.     Data digitization of 3.89 crore records has been completed, i.e. 96.76% of the
total target. The States of Bihar and Rajasthan will be starting digitization after selection
of system integrator in state.
21.    All States/UTs have launched their State Citizen Centric Portals.
22.   Sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet against 16 accused persons
was accorded under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 relating to terrorist
and anti national activities.
23.     An amount of Rs.5.34 crore was released to CAPFs for carrying out various civic
activities under the scheme of Civic Action Programme in LWE affected areas.


                                            ****

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, July 2018
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant Development
           and important events for the month of July, 2018.

      On 12.07.2018 Hon’ble Home Minister launched Border Area Development
Programme Online Management System which will improve implementation and
monitoring of works/projects.

2.     On 21.07.2018 Hon’ble Home Minister launched the Student Police Cadet
Programme from Tau Devi Lal Stadium Gurugram (Haryana), initially to be implemented
in select Government Schools across the country. An amount of Rs. 68.13 crore has
been released to the States, earmarking Rs. 50000 for each School for implementation
of the Programme.

3.    On 4.7.2018, Home Minister met representatives of Bodo groups of Assam to
discuss their demands.

4.     Shri Kiren Rijiju, Minister of State (Home) held a meeting on 20.7.2018 to discuss
issues relating to grant of Scheduled Tribe status to six communities in Assam.

5.     Shri Ram Shakal, Shri Rakesh Sinha, Dr. Sonal Mansingh and Shri Raghunath
Mahapatra have been nominated to the Council of States under article 80 (1)(a) of the
Constitution of India.

6. A meeting was chaired by Cabinet Secretary on 23.07.18 to review security and
development issues in LWE affected areas.
7. On 02.07.18, Union Home Secretary held an Inter Ministerial Empowered
Committee (IMEC) meeting with the Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development to
consider the project proposals of Government of Andhra Pradesh under Road
Connectivity Project for Left Wing Extremism (RCPLWE) affected areas.
8. Union Home Secretary wrote letters to Chief Secretaries of Chhattisgarh and
Odisha sharing the half yearly LWE scenario in the States.
9.   On 3.7.2018, a tripartite agreement was signed between Government of India,
Governments of Mizoram and Tripura and Mizoram Bru Displaced People’s Forum
(MBDPF) for repatriation of 5,407 Bru families (32,876 persons) presently in temporary
camps in Tripura to Mizoram before 30.9.2018.


10.   During the month, an amount of Rs. 236.83 crore was released to the State
Government of Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh, J&K,
Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and West Bengal under Border Area
Development Programme (BADP). The total funds released under BADP so far during
the financial year 2018-19 works out to Rs.399.44 crore.
11.   A Cabinet Note on the Umbrella Scheme “Relief and Rehabilitation of Migrants
and Repatriates” was approved by the Cabinet on 04.07.2018.

12.     Senior Officers’ Meeting (SOM) between India and USA of the six Sub-Groups
constituted under the Homeland Security Dialogue mechanism between the two
countries was held on 18.07.2018. The SOM deliberated on a draft Work Plan relating
to the activities of the six Sub-Groups.

13.   The complete Draft National Register of Citizens (NRC) has been published on
30.07.2018. Now every applicant whose name does not appear in draft will be given an
opportunity to file his claim. Any person can object to inclusion of any name in draft
NRC too. After disposal of such claims and objections the final NRC will be published.

14.    A total number of 236 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States for
maintaining law and order duties and security arrangements for visit of VVIPs,
Parliament Complex during session, Independence Day 2018, Sharwani Mela, Shrawan
Shivaratri/Kanwar Mela, NRC process.
15.    The President of India gave assent to 2 State Bills namely the Gujarat
Agricultural Lands Ceiling (Amendment) Bill 2015, the Gujarat Agricultural Lands Ceiling
(Amendment) Bill, 2017 and the Maharashtra Apartment Ownership (Amendment) Bill,
2018 during the month.

16.   Sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet against 5 accused persons
was accorded under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 relating to attack on
the convoy of Indian Army and seizure of Fake Indian Currency Notes.
17.    During the month, the Narcotics Control Bureau seized large quantities of
heroin, ganja, opium, cocaine and other narcotics and arrested 61 persons including 05
African national in connection with drug trafficking.

                                        ******

Director Generals of Police of LWE affected States sharing best practices of C-60 of

29 inhabited islands in the Union Territory of Andaman & Nicobar Island from the

14. During the month, an amount of Rs. 63.47 crore was released to the State
Government of Nagaland, Sikkim, Meghalaya and Mizoram. The total funds released
under Border Area Development Programme (BADP) so far during the financial year
2018-19 works out to Rs.162.61 crore.

15. This Ministry contributed towards holding of Conference of Governors at
Rashtrapati Bhavan on 4 - 5 June, 2018.

reimbursement under the Security Related Expenditure scheme.

(AQIS) and Islamic State in Khorasan Province (ISKP)/ ISIS Wilayat Khorasan/

maintaining law and order duties and security arrangements for AmarnathYatra
2018, Eid-ul-Fitr, International Day of Yoga, area domination and road sanitization

Stations are entering 100% FIRs through CCTNS, i.e. 91.06%.

released till date to States/UTs and Central Agencies.

(Jharkhand Amendment) Bill, 2017, the indian Penal Code and Code of Criminal
Procedure (Maharashtra Amendment) Bill, 2017, the Chhattisgarh Nagar Tatha
Gram Nivesh (Amendment & Validation) Bill, 2017, the Right to Fair Compensation
and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation & Resettlement (Jharkhand
Amendment) Bill, 2017, the Assam Witch Hunting (Prohibition, Preservation &

Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant

on 2™ April, 2018 at Rashtrapati Bhavan where the President of India conferred
Padma Awards on 43 awardees.

April, 2018 under the chairmanship of Hon’ble Home Minister.

26.04.2018, under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Home Minister.

connectivity issues in LWE affected States.

5. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance, 2018 was promulgated on

21.04.2018 to provide effective deterrence and stringent penalties for offences of
rape.

Criminality and Tackling Serious Organized Crime was signed during tre visit of
Hon'ble Prime Minister to U.K.

Transformation of Aspirational Districts and to review the LWE situation in
Jharkhand.

Maharashtra, respectively, on the success achieved by CRPF in Jharkhand and for

to sensitize them to counter the LWE activities in the LWE affected areas.

Changlang and Longding districts of Arunachal Pradesh and the areas falling within
the jurisdiction of 8 Police Stations in the districts of Arunachal Pradesh, bordering
the State of Assam as ‘disturbed area’ under Section 3 of the Armed Forces (Special
Powers) Act, 1958 w.e.f. 1.4.2018 upto 30.9.2018. Further, AFSPA, 1958 has been
removed from the State of Meghalaya w.e.f. 1.4.2018.

(Reformation) [NSCN(R)] and National Socialist Council of Nagaland (Neopao
Konyank-Kitovi) [NSCN(NK)] were extended for one year i.e. upto 27.4.2019.

National Executive Committee (SC-NEC) for central assistance to the States of

Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim and UT of Lakshadweep for flood/landslides and
Cyclone Ockhi of 2017.

13. The 43 High Level Empowered Committee (HLEC) meeting on border
infrastructure projects was held by the Union Home Secretary on 18.04.2018.

14. An amount of Rs. 22.28 crore was released to the State Government of
Arunachal under Border Area Development Programme (BADP).

15. A total number of 148 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States for
security arrangements, law and order duties, Amarnath Yatra etc. A total of 570 Coys
of CAPFs/SAPs have been deployed for Assembly Elections, 2018 in Karnataka, on
the recommendations of Election Commission of India,.

Public Trust (Amendment) Bill, 2017, the Bihar Agriculture and Rural Area
Development Agency (Repeal) Bill, 2017, the Right to Fair Compensation and
Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation & Resettlement (Maarasntra
Amendment) Bill, 2018 and the Maharashtra Slum Areas (Improvement, Clearance
and Redevelopment) (Amendment) Bill, 2017 during the month. One mercy petition
of death row convict was decided by the Hon’ble President on 23.04.2018.

was accorded under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 for car°ying out
anti-national activities.

18. During the month, Narcotics Control Bureau seized large quantities of
heroin, ganja, opium, cocaine and other narcotics and arrested 65 persons including
08 foreign nationals in connection with drugs trafficking. Indian currency worth Rs.
18,46 ,600/- was also seized.

pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant

The First Investiture Ceremony for conferment of the Padma Awards was held
on 20.03.2018 at Rashtrapati Bhavan where the President of India conferred Padma
Awards on 43 awardees.

2018 wherein issues of mutual interest to both countries were discussed.

= Agreement between Government of Republic of India and Government of
French Republic on the Prevention of Illicit Consumption and Suppression of Illicit
Trafficking of Narcotic Drug, Psychotropic Substances and Chemical Precursors, as
well as related Offences was signed on 10.03.2018.

a subordinate legislation under the Enemy Property (Amendment & Validation) Act,
2017. The guidelines for disposal of Enemy Property Order, 2018 and Transfer of
Property (vested in the Custodian) order, 2018 were also notified on 21.03.2018.

5. The Disaster Management division, Ministry of Home Affairs and the
Government of Japan jointly organized a two day workshop on Disaster Risk
Reduction from 19-20 March, 2018 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The workshop
deliberated on various themes viz. disaster management, policy framework, risk
assessment, disaster resilient infrastructure, early warning system, preparedness by
sub national governments and approaches by private sector.

6. On 19.3.201807 Union Home Secretary held a meeting to review the
disturbed area status in Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya. The meeting was
attended by senior officers of Assam, Meghalaya & Arunachal Pradesh,
representatives of IB, MoD and Cabinet Secretariat.

he Special Secretary (IS) on 16.3.2018 held a meeting in Agartala (Tripura) to

United Naga Council was held on 23. 3. 2018 at Senapati (Manipur)

also held by Union Home Secretary to discuss the issues relating to Assam-
Mizoram border disputes.

districts advising them to visit the areas and send reports/views on the required
policy intervention in the thematic areas of health and nutrition, education,
agriculture and water resources, financial inclusion, skill development and basic
infrastructure provided.

States for expediting their projects in view of the relaxation given by M/o
Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

reimbursement under the Security Related Expenditure (SRE) scheme. Another Rs
50 crore was released to Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chattisgarh, Jharkahnd,
Maharashtra, Telengana and Odisha under the "Special Infrastructure Scheme".

to sensitize them to counter the LWE activities in the LWE affected areas.

Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Himachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim,
Jammu & Kashmir, Manipur, Punjab, and Uttrakhand. The total funds released under
Border Area Development Programme (BADP) so far during the current financial
year 2017-18 (up to Mar., 2018) works out to Rs.1100 crore.

15. 9" Meeting of the Steering Committee for review of Coastal Security under
the chairmanship of Special Secretary (BM) was held on 27" March, 2018

16. Passenger Terminal Building at Integrated Check Post at Moreh has been
operationalised w.e.f 15.03.2018.

1967 for carrying out anti-national activities.

Water and Sewage Board (Repeal) Bill, 2017 during the month of March, 2018.

Rs. 452.10 crore for Modernization of Police Forces (MPF) Scheme. Out of Rs.
452.10 crore total Rs. 451.75 + 62 crore for Spl Projects/programmes under new
scheme amounting to a total of Rs. 513.75 crore was released to the States up to
March, 2018.

across the country. Also, all States/UTs have launched their State Citizen Centric

Portals.
