pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant
Development and important events for the month of February, 2018.

On 26.2.2018, a meeting of High Level Committee (HLC) was held under
the Chairmanship of the Hon’ble Home Minister for central assistance to the States
of Bihar, Gujarat, Kerala, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal,
affected by CycloneOckhi/Flood.

2. 24" All India Forensic Science Conference was organised by Directorate
of Forensic Sciences (DFSS) in collaboration with Gujarat University and Raksha
Shakti University in Ahmadabad on “Harnessing new Vistas in Academics and
Forensic Science’ from 10-12" February, 2018. The conference was inaugurated by
Hon'ble Union Home Minister.

3. Union Home Secretary held meetings on 02.02.2018 and 15.2.2018 to
review repatriation of Bru migrants from Tripura to Mizoram. Special Secretary (IS)
also held a meeting on 16.2.2018 to discuss the issues relating to imparting skill
development training to youths of Bru community on their repatriation from Tripura to
Mizoram.

4. On 02.02.2018, Union Home Secretary held a meeting to review the re-
deployment of CAPFs in LWE areas and on 16.02.2018 to review the development
issues of the Department of Posts, Department of Telecommunication, Ministry of
Environment, Forests & Climate Change, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
and the Department of School Education and Literacy in LWE areas.

5. Union Home Secretary wrote letters to the Chief Secretaries of
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Bihar, Odisha,Telangana, Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil
Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and West Bengal sharing
with them the LWE scenario for 2017 and the way forward.

6. A total number of 268 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States
(Telengana, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Arunachal Pradesh, Haryana, Puducherry,
Gujarat, Meghalaya, Daman & Diu, Punjab and Tripura) for law and order duties,
VVIP Security and various festivals. On the recommendations of Election
Commission of India, a total of 29 Coys of CAPFs have been deployed in Madhya
Pradesh and Odisha for Bye-Elections and in Meghalaya for Assembly elections.

7. A Committee under the chairmanship of Special Secretary (IS) has
been constituted to review the security of CARGO Complex at Airports.

opium, cocaine and other narcotics. 52 persons including 4 foreign Nationals were
arrested in connection with drug trafficking.

Working Groups between India and Israel took place on 27 and 28 February, 2018.
Issues of mutual interest between the two countries, covering areas related to
Capacity Building, Border Management and Police Modernization, were discussed.

10. An amount of Rs. 147.58 crore was released to the State Governments
of Meghalaya, Gujarat, Manipur, Punjab, Arunachal Pradesh, West Bengal, Assam,
Rajasthan and Uttrakhand under the Border Areas Development Programme
(BADP). The total funds released under BADP so far during the current financial year
2017-18 works out to Rs. 1000.23 crore.

11. The President of India gave assent to 6 State Bills namely the
Apprentices (Maharashtra Amendment) Bill, 2017, the Commonwealth Trust,
Kozhikode (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertaking) Bill, 2012, the Sales Promotion
(Conditions of Service) (Uttar Pradesh Amendment) Bill, 2017, the Prevention of
Cruelty to Animals (Karnataka Second Amendment) Bill, 2017, the Maharashtra
Agricultural Lands (Ceiling and Holdings) (Amendment) Bill, 2017 and the
Maharashtra Essential Services Maintenance Bill, 2017 during the month.

12. An amount of Rs.175 crore was released to 35 worst LWE affected
districts of Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Maharashtra,
Telangana and Odisha (@ Rs.5 crore per district) under Special Central Assistance
scheme.

13. During the month, sanction for prosecution for filing the charge sheet
against 09 accused persons was accorded under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention)
Act, 1967 relating to seizure of Fake Indian Currency Notes and for carrying out anti-
national activities.

14. The Director Generals of CAPFs have been delegated financial power
for procurement of motor vehicles for their newly raised units/establishments up to
Rs. 20 Cr. In each case. CAPFs/NIA/IB has also been allowed to procure new
vehicles against condemnation on “Category to Category basis’.

15. An amount of Rs.385.27 crore was sanctioned for authorization
provisioning and expenditure for Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) etc.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, December 2017
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs-Major Achievements, significant
Development and important events for the month of December, 2017.



       A High Level Committee (HLC) Meeting was held under the Chairmanship of
the Hon’ble Home Minister on 13.12.2017 for central assistance to the States of
Mizoram , Manipur and Kerala affected by flood/landslides/ drought in 2017.

 2.     A meeting to review the Indo-Bangladesh Border (IBB) issues with Chief
Ministers of IBB states was held under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Home Minister
on 07.12.2017 at Kolkota.
 3.     On 29.12.2017, hon’ble Home Minister held a review meeting with various
Central Ministers to discuss development issues in the LWE States.
 4.    Union Home Secretary visited Arunachal Pradesh on 1-2 December, 2017and
held discussions with Senior Officers of Central Ministries, Army and CAPFs and
reviewed the security situation in the State. Union Home Secretary also visited the
border post of ITBP at Kibithu and interacted with ITBP and Army officials.

 5.     The Sub-Committee of National Executive Committee (SC-NEC) considered
central assistance to the State of Bihar in the wake of flood of 2017.
6.    During the month, advisories were issued to Chief Secretaries of Andhra
Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Odisha and Telangana for
speedy implementation of Skill Development Scheme and the Pradhan Mantri
Kaushal Vikas Yojna in LWE affected districts.
7.     During the month, sanction for prosecution for filing charge sheet against 02
accused persons was accorded under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967
relating to arrest and deportation of an ISIS operative.

8.    The whole State of Nagaland has been declared as “Disturbed Area” under
the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 for a period of six months w.e.f.
30.12.2017.

9.     An amount of Rs.38.7 crore was sanctioned for authorization provisioning
and expenditure for Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs).

10.    On 07.12.2017, notification was issued regarding declaration of Vijayawada
Airport of Andhra Pradesh as an authorized Immigration Check Post (ICP) and
appointment of Deputy Commissioner, Police, Vijayawada, District Krishna as the
“Civil Authority”. E-visa scheme has also been implemented at Vishakhapatnam
Airport w.e.f. 13.12.2017.
11.   Stay and travel regulations for Tibetan Refugees in India have been
streamlined and decisions conveyed to all concerned authorities for compliance.

12.    The Competent Authority has given approval to approval to Bureau of
Immigration for appointment of 1000 Immigration assistants on contractual basis,
conversion of 350 posts from higher to lower grade and giving more scope for
recruitment of Ex-Servicemen on contractual basis by including IB & CAPF
personnel.

13.   The Ministry has finlaised the stay Visa/Residential Permit/Long Term Visa
(LTV) Policy for Afghan nationals in India.

14.    During the month, the Narcotics Control Bureau seized large quantities of
heroin, ganja, opium, cocaine and other narcotics. 26 persons including 1
Venezuelan national in connection with drug trafficking.

15.    Notifications regarding delegation of powers and functions of State
Government to the Administrator/LG under the Aadhar (Target Delivery of Financial
and others Subsidies and Services) Act, 2016 and under the Rights of Persons with
Disabilities Act, 2016 have been issued to all UTs.

16.   An amount of Rs. 6.33 crore has been sanctioned as ex-gratia compensation
to the next of kin (NOKs) of CAPFs in 23 cases.

17.   Approval of 5 acres land to CISF for establishment of Kendriya Vidhyalaya at
CISF campus [Special Security Group (SSG)], Greater Noida was granted on
22.12.2017.

18.   Sanction for construction of infrastructure for an amount of Rs.369.84 crores
was granted to ITBP & BSF .

19.    116 coys of CAPFs were deployed in the States of Arunachal Pradesh,
Telangana, Delhi, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Meghalaya & Karnataka for law and
order duties as well as various festivals.

20.   113 coys of CAPFs were deployed on the recommendations of Election
Commission of India for preparation of National Register of Citizens in Assam,
Municipal and Assembly Election duties in Uttar Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Tamil
Nadu & West Bengal.

21.     An amount of Rs. 17.82 crores was released during the month to the State of
Jammu & Kashmir under Border Area Development Program (BADP), making a
total of Rs. 74.24 crores during the current financial year.

Developments and important events for the month of November, 2017

       A Government of India Delegation, led by Hon’ble Union Home Minister visited

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, August 2016
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs- Major Achievements, significant
Developments and important events for the month of August, 2016

7'n Meeting of SAARC Secretaries of Interior/Home and 7" Meeting of SAARC
Immigration Authorities was held in Islamabad, Pakistan from 2-4 August, 2016. The
Government of India delegation was led by Hon’ble Home Minister.

2s A meeting on counter terrorism and countering cross border movement of terrorism
was attended by MOS (R) on 10" August, 2016 at Bali, Indonesia.

3: On 27.08.2016 Union Home Secretary held a meeting on Perception Management
relating to left Wing Extremism. Meetings were also held during the month at the level of
Additional Secretary (LWE) on 12.08.2016 and 23.08.2016 through Video Conference to
review the schemes implemented in 35 LWE affected districts and distribution of title

deeds under Forest Rights Act in LWE affected States.

4. During the month of August, 06 advisories were issued to the State Governments/
CAPFs to sensitize them to counter the LWE activities in LWE affected areas.

5. A sum of Rs.1 crore was released as one time welfare grant to CRPF on
23.08.2016 for providing financial assistance to the injured CRPF personnel due to stone
pelting in J&K.

6. 213 Coys of CAPFs were deployed in various States (J&K, Karnataka, Arunachal
Pradesh, Bihar, Punjab, Tripura, Megahlaya) for law and order duties.

7. 24 Coys and 02 Platoon of CAPFs were deployed in various States (UP,
Telangana, Delhi, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh) for law and order duties as well as festivals.

8. 950 Medals under President’s Police Medal for Gallantry/ Police Medal for
Gallantry/ Distinguished Service / Meritorious Service were awarded to the police
personnel of States/UTs/CAPFs on the occasion of Independence Day — 2016.

9. The quarterly targets for border infrastructure works along Indo-Pak border (IPB)
were reviewed with the objective to complete all pending works by March, 2018, in the 5"
Steering committee meeting on Indo Pak Border held on 3.8.2016 under the
Chairmanship of Secretary (BM) . Another meeting was held on 12.8.2016 to review the
issues related to management of Indo Bangladesh Border.

10. The following Governors were appointed by the President under Article 155 of the
Constitution:

(i) Shri Banwarilal Purohit as the Governor of Assam,
(ii) Dr. Najma A. Heptulla as the Governor of Manipur and
(iii) | ShriV.P. Singh Badnore as the Governor of Punjab.
11. | The pension of freedom fighter pensioners has been enhanced by about 20%
w.e.f. 15.08.2016. It has also been decided that Dearness Allowance/Dearness Relief
system applicable to Central Government employees twice a year shall apply to freedom
fighter pensioners.

12. The Enemy Property (Amendment and Validation) Fourth Ordinance, 2016 dated
28.08.2016 as per the report of the Select Committee of Rajya Sabha has been
promulgated on 28.08.2016 to give continuous effect to the earlier ordinances on the
subject.

13. A total amount of Rs. 48.94 Crore was released to three states i.e. Rajasthan,
Tamil Nadu and Nagaland in respect of MPF scheme till August, 2016. The meetings of
High Powered Committee (HPC) to consider and approve the State Action Plan proposals
of States of Haryana, Meghalaya, Madhya Pradesh, Goa, Gujarat, Jammu & Kashmir,
Assam, Tripura and Arunachal Pradesh were held during the month.

14. Out of Budgetary provision, the budget estimate for the financial year 2016-17 for
CCTNS is Rs. 250 crore under the plan head an amount of Rs. 49.65 crore were released
to the States i.e. Punjab, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, NCRB, Mizoram.

15. Biometric Enrollment Software facility has been operationalized at 79 Indian
Missions abroad and in total C-Visa has been implemented in 163 Indian Missions.

16. During the month sanction for prosecution for filing charge sheets against 6
accused persons was accorded under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 in
cases relating to terrorist and anti-national activities, murder, seizure of Fake Indian
Currency Notes in various parts of the country.

17. National Institute of Disaster Management (Southern Campus) has started
functioning from a rented premises at Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh. The first activity
took place on 17.08.2016 with the holding of its one-day Orientation Programme on
“Capacity Building for Disaster Resilience at local level’.

18. | The Hon’ble President assented to three State Bills namely, the Payment of Wages
(Haryana Amendment) Bill, 2016, the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in
Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Settlement (Gujarat Amendment ) Bill, 2016 and the
Code of Criminal Procedure (Maharashtra Amendment) Bill, 2015 during the month.

19. Under ACC Vacancy Monitoring System (AVMS), Divisions are taking necessary
action for updating the status relating to ACC posts.

20. The capture of biometrics for creation of National Population Register, using UIDAI
(Unique Identification Authority of India) enrolment software, has been done for 20.49
crore persons (5 year +) out of total targeted population of 20.72 crore spread over ten
NPR States/UTs.

docs.title: Monthly Major Achievements of MHA, July 2016
pages:
Ministry of Home Affairs — Major Achievements, significant
developments and important events for the month of July, 2016

On 21% July,2016, Hon'ble Prime Minister inaugurated ICP Petrapole .

2. . The 4th Home Minister Level Talks between India and Bangladesh were
held on 28th July, 2016. In the meeting, issues related to security, border
management, bilateral cooperation in counter terrorism and checking insurgency
including intelligence exchange, operationalisation and implementation of various
Agreements/ MoUs viz. Agreement on Combating Terrorism and Organized Crime
and Illicit Drug Trafficking, Coordinated Border Management Plan (CBMP),
addendum to the Bilateral Extradition Treaty of 2013, MoU on Establishment of
Collaborative Relationship to Combat Transnational! legal Activities at Sea, MoU
to Prevent and Counter Smuggling and Circulation of Fake Currency Notes, MoU
on Bilateral Cooperation for Prevention of Human Trafficking especially Trafficking
of Women and Children, repatriation of released prisoners and victims of human
trafficking, maritime security cooperation, different bilateral mechanisms including
HS level talks, DG level meetings, meeting between DMs/DCs of border districts,
consular and fisherman issues etc. were discussed.

3. A Cabinet Note regarding enhancement of compensation from Rs. 3 to Rs.
5 lakhs under the Central Scheme has been approved by the Union Home Minister
and the same has been sent to Cabinet Sectt. for consideration.

4. The meeting of BRICS Heads of Anti Drug Working Group was organized
by Narcotic Control Bureau (NCB), Ministry of Home Affairs on 8th July, 2016.
Various issues relating to combating drug trafficking, drug-money laundering and
financial investigation related to drug proceeds were discussed.

5. A Government of India delegation led by Hon’ble Union Home Minister met
Government of Malaysia Delegation led by Dato Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Deputy
Prime Minister on 18.07.2016 in New Delhi. Discussions were held on bilateral
security relations between the two countries.

6. On 07.07.2016 Memorandum of Understanding between the Government
of India and the Government of Mozambique was signed on Drug Demand
Reduction and Prevention of Illicit Trafficking in Narcotic Drugs, Psychotropic
substances and Precursor Chemicals and Related matters.

7. On 26! - 27" July, 2016,Union Home Secretary led the 20!" National Level
Meeting between India and Myanmar on security related issues. In the meeting,
issues related to security and border management, activities of insurgent groups
along the international border, arms smuggling, exchange of intelligence
information, cooperation in prevention of drug trafficking, smuggling of wildlife
articles, constructions in boundary areas, joint inspection of boundary pillars and
construction of additional boundary pillars on the international border, consular
issues including prisoners in jails of the other country and capacity building
Programmes for Myanmar Police, narcotics, Wildlife crime Control and for disaster
mitigation etc. were discussed.
8. A Review Group meeting was held by Cabinet Secretary on 08.07.2016 on
Left Wing Extremism (LWE) issues.

9. During July, 2016, 05 advisories were issued to the State Governments/
CAPFs to sensitize them to counter the LWE activities in LWE affected areas,

10. A meeting of the National Executive Committee was chaired by Union Home
Secretary on 22.07.2016 to consider the deliberations made in the meeting of the
Sub-Committee of National Executive Committee (SE-NEC) held in compliance of
the direction of Hon'ble Supreme Court. A meeting of the High Level Committee
was held on 29.07.2016 to consider the report of the Subcommittee of National
Executive Committee (SC-NEC) on damage caused by
hailstorm/drought/earthquake during 2015-16 in Rajasthan, U.P. and Manipur.

11. A meeting of the Departmental Consultative Committee of MHA was held
on 04.07.2016 to discuss “Disaster Management Preparedness”.

12. 32°¢ High Level Empowered Committee (HLEC) meeting was held on
28.07.2016 by Union Home Secretary. During the meeting border infrastructure
estimates amounting to Rs. 1050.19 crore were considered.

13. An advisory to all the state Governments/UTs was. issued for Strengthening
the security of Airports on 27.07.2016

14. An Indian Delegation visited Singapore from 4th to 6th July 2016 and

reviewed the pending Letters Rogatory (LRs) and Extradition matters between
India and Singapore.

15. NDAL-ALIS (NDAL-Arms Licence Issuance System) for online data on
various aspects of licensing of arms was launched on 22.07.2016.

16. 20072 Police (Antrik Suraksha Seva) Padak, 61 Parakram Padak and 153

Home Minister's Medals were awarded to Police personnel of various
States/UTs/CAPFs/CPOs during the month.

17. Out of Budgetary provision, the Budget Estimates for the Financial Year
2016-17 is Rs.595.00 Crore under the ‘Non-Plan’ in respect of Modernization of
State Police Forces (MPF) Scheme. The meeting of High Powered Committee
(HPC) to consider and approve the State Action Plan proposals of States of Bihar,

Sikkim, Mizoram, West Bengal, Odisha, Himachal Pradesh, Tripura and Arunachal
Pradesh were held during the month.

18. Meeting of Committee of Non-Plan Expenditure (CNE) /Expenditure
Finance Committee (EFC) for consideration of Umbrella Scheme of
“Modernization of Police Forces” was held on 20.07.2016. This umbrella scheme
includes sub-schemes of Assistance to States for Modernization of Police (existing
MPF Scheme), Crime and Criminal Tracking Network Systems (CCTNS), Security
Related Expenditure (SRE) of NE States, J&K and LWE affected areas & Special
Infrastructure Scheme (SIS), Projects under Inter- State Police Wireless,
Assistance to States for Special Projects/ Programmes for upgrading Police
infrastructure and Modernization of Fire & Emergency Services.

19. All States/ UTs were advised to roll out sustained campaign “Operation
Muskan-ll" from 18" July to 31S July, 2016, throughout the country to rescue missing
children.

20. During the month sanction for prosecution for filing charge sheets against
38 accused persons was accorded under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act,
1967 in cases relating to promotion of the ideology of ISIS, inciting others to
become member of ISIS and indulging in terrorist and anti-national activities,
murder, seizure of Fake Indian Currency Notes in various parts of the country.

21. Notification regarding delegation of powers and functions of the Appropriate
Government to the Administrator of UTs of Daman & Diu, Dadra & Nagar Haveli,
Chandigarh, Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar Islands under the Street
Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 has
been issued on 06.07.2016.

22. — Instructions of the President for promulgation of the Court Fees (Jharkhand
Amendment) Ordinance, 2016 were conveyed to the State Government on
14.07.2016.

23. Nodal Officer for ACC Vacancy Monitoring System (AVMS) has been
notified and the details registered in AVMS. Concerned Divisions have been
instructed to register in the AVMS System and update the details of ACC posts.
Necessary action is being taken by them in this regard.

24. Thecapture of biometrics for creation of National Population Register, using
UIDAI (Unique Identification Authority of India) enrolment software, has been done
for 20.29 crore persons (5 year +) out of total targeted population of 20.72 crore
spread over ten NPR States/UTs.
